editor.addToDashboard.add.context: Blue button in the footer of the dialog that adds a device to a dashboard. It puts a tile for the device on the picked dashboard. A command.

editor.addToDashboard.alreadyOn.context: Small grey note at the right of a dashboard in the list. The device already has a tile on that dashboard (it can still be added again).

editor.addToDashboard.dashboards.context: Name of the list of dashboards in the dialog that adds a device to a dashboard, read out by screen readers. One of the dashboards can be picked. Not visible as text.

editor.addToDashboard.description.en: Its tile goes at the bottom, in the look that suits it best; move or restyle it there.
editor.addToDashboard.description.context: Text under the title of the dialog that adds a device to a dashboard. It says where the new tile (a box on the dashboard that shows the device) lands and that it can be moved and restyled afterwards.

editor.addToDashboard.noDashboards.en: There are no dashboards yet; make one first, from the sidebar.
editor.addToDashboard.noDashboards.context: Shown in the dialog that adds a device to a dashboard when the person has no dashboards at all. The sidebar is the navigation column at the left of the app, where a new dashboard is made.

editor.addToDashboard.title.context: Title of the dialog that opens from a device on the Devices page. The person picks the dashboard the device gets a tile on.

params.device: The name of the device, as the person named it in Homey. Not translated.

editor.alignPicker.label.context: Screen reader label of the grid of nine places where the content of a tile can sit, used when the screen using the grid gives no label. Not shown.

editor.alignPicker.place.en: {y, select, start {Top} center {Middle} other {Bottom}} {x, select, start {left} center {centre} other {right}}
editor.alignPicker.place.context: Name of one place in the grid, as a tooltip and screen reader label: first the place up and down, then the place sideways, for example "Top left", "Middle right" or "Bottom centre". Order the two parts as the language says it.

params.x: The place sideways: "start" is the left, "center" the centre, "end" the right.
params.y: The place up and down: "start" is the top, "center" the middle, "end" the bottom.

editor.alignPicker.placeMiddle.context: Name of the place in the very middle of the grid of places, as a tooltip and screen reader label.

editor.alignPicker.placeSideways.context: Name of one place of a grid that has only one row, as a tooltip and screen reader label: the content sits at the left, in the centre or at the right of the tile.

params.x: The place sideways: "start" is the left, "center" the centre, "end" the right.

editor.alignPicker.placeUpright.context: Name of one place of a grid that has only one column, as a tooltip and screen reader label: the content sits at the top, in the middle or at the bottom of the tile.

params.y: The place up and down: "start" is the top, "center" the middle, "end" the bottom.

editor.alignPicker.shareWidth.context: Button next to the grid of places, on and off: the items of the tile split the whole width between them instead of sitting at one place.

editor.applianceExample.title.context: Title of the example Appliance tile in the add-widgets window preview: the name a person would give their washing machine in their Homey.

editor.applianceIcon.cards.context: Screen reader label of the group of cards in the Appliance widget settings, where one picture of an appliance is picked. Not visible as text.

editor.applianceIcon.dishwasher.context: Label under a small moving picture of a dishwasher, one of the choices for the icon of an Appliance widget.

editor.applianceIcon.dryer.context: Label under a small moving picture of a tumble dryer, one of the choices for the icon of an Appliance widget.

editor.applianceIcon.library.context: Small caption above the icon picker that shows after "Another icon" is chosen in the Appliance widget settings. The library is the Phosphor icon library plus Tiledash’s own icons.

editor.applianceIcon.moving.context: Small caption above the three cards of an appliance that is drawn as a moving picture (washing machine, dryer, dishwasher) in the settings of the Appliance widget. It says these pictures move while the appliance runs.

editor.applianceIcon.other.context: Label under the last card in the choices for the icon of an Appliance widget. It lets the person pick any icon from the library instead of a moving machine.

editor.applianceIcon.pickerName.context: Name of the icon picker shown under "From the library" in the Appliance widget settings. It is used in screen reader labels such as "Search icon" and is lowercased there. Not visible as text.

editor.applianceIcon.washer.context: Label under a small moving picture of a washing machine, one of the choices for the icon of an Appliance widget.

editor.applianceSource.kindPower.context: Second option of the two-way switch: the appliance runs while its electrical power use is above a limit.

editor.applianceSource.kindState.context: First option of the two-way switch: the appliance runs while a yes/no value (such as a device’s on/off) says yes. Also the screen reader label of the value field under it.

editor.applianceSource.nowHint.en: now {watts, number} W: {running, select, yes {running} other {not running}}
editor.applianceSource.nowHint.context: Help text under the limit slider: the power the appliance draws right now, and whether that counts as running. W is the unit watt.

params.running: Whether that is above the limit: yes (counts as running) or no. A select value, not shown.
params.watts: The power it draws now, in watts, rounded to a whole number.

editor.applianceSource.powerField.context: Label of the field under the option Power use, where the power reading is picked, and its screen reader label. The electrical power an appliance draws.

editor.applianceSource.powerPlaceholder.en: Pick a power reading or variable
editor.applianceSource.powerPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the Power field before anything is picked: it asks for a power reading of a device or a number variable.

editor.applianceSource.runningAbove.context: Label of the slider that sets the limit in Power use: the appliance counts as running above this power. W is the unit watt.

params.above: The limit in watts, a whole number from 1 to 200.

editor.applianceSource.runningWhen.context: Label of the first choice in the settings of an appliance: when does it count as running? The dots lead on to the two options below it (On or off, Power use).

editor.applianceSource.runningWhenLabel.context: Screen reader label of the two-way switch between On or off and Power use. Not visible as text.

editor.applianceSource.stateField.en: It runs while this is on
editor.applianceSource.stateField.context: Label of the field under the option On or off, where a yes/no value is picked. A sentence start: it continues with what is picked. "On" means the value says yes, or the appliance is switched on.

editor.applianceSource.stateHint.en: Yes, a number above 0, or words other than off count as running.
editor.applianceSource.stateHint.context: Help text under the On or off field: which values count as running. A text value such as "on" or "washing" counts; "off" does not.

editor.applianceSource.statePlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the On or off field before anything is picked: it asks for a value that is yes or no.

editor.applianceSource.threshold.context: Screen reader label of the slider that sets the power limit above which the appliance counts as running. Not visible as text.

editor.borderSides.allSides.context: Small text next to the width slider while the border is drawn on all four sides of the tile.

editor.borderSides.bottom.context: Name of the bottom side of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that side, and one of the words in the list of sides that have a border.

editor.borderSides.label.context: Screen reader label of the row of choice buttons for the style of the line around the tile. Not shown.

editor.borderSides.left.context: Name of the left side of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that side, and one of the words in the list of sides that have a border.

editor.borderSides.right.context: Name of the right side of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that side, and one of the words in the list of sides that have a border.

editor.borderSides.sidesLabel.context: Screen reader label of the little tile whose four sides are buttons that switch the border on or off for that side. Not shown.

editor.borderSides.styleDashed.context: Choice button for the style of the border: a line made of short dashes. Short.

editor.borderSides.styleNone.context: Choice button for the style of the border: no border line at all. Short.

editor.borderSides.styleSolid.context: Choice button for the style of the border: an unbroken line. Short.

editor.borderSides.styleTheme.context: Choice button for the style of the border: use the theme’s border, with no change of the tile’s own. Short.

editor.borderSides.top.context: Name of the top side of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that side, and one of the words in the list of sides that have a border.

editor.borderSides.widthLabel.context: Screen reader label of the slider for the thickness of the border line. Not shown.

editor.busyEditor.addDevice.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown that adds a device to the "Busy now" widget.

editor.busyEditor.addDevicePlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the dropdown that adds a device to the "Busy now" widget. The three dots mean it opens a list.

editor.busyEditor.afterFinish.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses how long a thing stays on the widget once it is no longer busy.

editor.busyEditor.automaticIcon.context: Small button in the Look tab, shown once the icon was changed: it goes back to the icon Tiledash picks by itself for the device.

editor.busyEditor.detailLeft.context: Choice in the dropdown "Under its name": the line under a busy thing shows how long it still has to go, such as the minutes left of a wash.

editor.busyEditor.detailNone.context: Choice in the dropdown "Under its name": no line under the name of a busy thing.

editor.busyEditor.detailPower.context: Choice in the dropdown "Under its name": the line under a busy thing shows the power it draws now, in watts.

editor.busyEditor.detailSince.context: Choice in the dropdown "Under its name": the line under a busy thing says since when it has been busy, such as "since 14:05".

editor.busyEditor.detailWords.context: Choice in the dropdown "Under its name": the line under a busy thing shows a text read from the device or a variable, such as the program a washer runs.

editor.busyEditor.empty.en: Nothing yet: add the things you want to see while they run.
editor.busyEditor.empty.context: Empty-state line under the list of the "Busy now" widget when it watches nothing yet: add devices or other things, such as washing machines.

editor.busyEditor.hintDevice.en: Its device is the one it follows; its history is the reading that says it runs.
editor.busyEditor.hintDevice.context: Help text in the Tap tab of a thing that follows a device: tapping can open that device or show its history, which is the history of the reading that says the thing runs.

editor.busyEditor.hintVariable.en: It follows a variable, so it can open a dashboard or start a flow.
editor.busyEditor.hintVariable.context: Help text in the Tap tab of a thing that follows a Logic variable instead of a device: it has no device to open, so a tap can open a dashboard or start a flow.

editor.busyEditor.icon.context: Small label above the icon picker in the Look tab of a busy thing.

editor.busyEditor.iconOnly.context: Small grey tag after the name of a row whose name is hidden on the tile: only its icon and the detail show.

editor.busyEditor.keep120.context: Choice in the dropdown "After it finishes": the thing stays on the widget for 2 hours with the status Done. Keep the quotes and the number.

editor.busyEditor.keep15.context: Choice in the dropdown "After it finishes": the thing stays on the widget for 15 minutes with the status Done. Keep the quotes and the number.

editor.busyEditor.keepNone.context: Choice in the dropdown "After it finishes": the thing disappears from the widget the moment it is no longer busy.

editor.busyEditor.keepShort0.context: Part of the one-line summary of a closed row, after the middle dots: when it finishes the thing is removed at once. Lower case, a few words.

editor.busyEditor.keepShort120.context: Part of the one-line summary of a closed row, after the middle dots: when it finishes it stays for 2 hours as Done. Lower case, a few words.

editor.busyEditor.keepShort15.context: Part of the one-line summary of a closed row, after the middle dots: when it finishes it stays for 15 minutes as Done. Lower case, a few words.

editor.busyEditor.keepWidget.en: Like the rest of the widget
editor.busyEditor.keepWidget.context: Choice in the dropdown "After it finishes": this thing stays on the widget for as long as the widget’s own setting says.

editor.busyEditor.name.context: Label of the text field where the name of a busy thing is typed.

editor.busyEditor.newName.context: The starting name of a new thing added with "Something else…". The person usually renames it. A plain name for a washing machine.

editor.busyEditor.pickMinutes.context: Placeholder of the field that picks the reading or variable holding the minutes left, shown while none is picked.

editor.busyEditor.pickText.context: Placeholder of the field that picks the reading or variable holding the text to show under the name, shown while none is picked.

editor.busyEditor.powerAbove.context: Part of the one-line summary of a row that is busy while a device draws power: the device name, then the power in watts above which it counts as busy. For example: Washing plug above 10 W.

params.above: The power threshold, a number in watts. Keep W.
params.name: The name of the device (or "Removed"). Not translated.

editor.busyEditor.readFrom.context: Label of the field that picks where the "Time left" or "In words" detail is read from: a reading of a device or a variable.

editor.busyEditor.remove.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button on a row: it removes that thing from the widget.

params.name: The name of the thing, such as "Washing machine". Not translated.

editor.busyEditor.removed.context: Name shown for a device or variable that a busy thing follows but that no longer exists in the Homey, in the one-line summary of a row.

editor.busyEditor.settingsOf.context: Screen reader label of the three tabs (Watch, Look, Tap) of an opened row. Not visible as text.

params.name: The name of the thing, such as "Washing machine". Not translated.

editor.busyEditor.showName.context: Label of a switch in the Look tab: whether the name of the thing shows on the tile. Also the screen reader label of the switch.

editor.busyEditor.showNameOff.en: Off: just its icon and the detail.
editor.busyEditor.showNameOff.context: Small explanation under the switch "Show its name": when it is off, the tile shows only the icon and the detail line.

editor.busyEditor.somethingElse.context: Button that adds a thing that is not a device to the "Busy now" widget, such as a washing machine known only from a variable or a smart plug. The three dots mean more is asked next.

editor.busyEditor.stateOf.context: Part of the one-line summary of a row that is busy while a device’s reading is on: the device, a colon, then which reading. For example: Washing machine: On/off.

params.device: The name of the device (or "Removed"). Not translated.
params.reading: The title of the device’s reading, such as "On/off". Not translated.

editor.busyEditor.tabLook.context: Second of three tabs of an opened row (the others are Watch and Tap): how the thing looks (its name and icon). A noun or verb for the appearance.

editor.busyEditor.tabTap.context: Third of three tabs of an opened row (the others are Watch and Look): what tapping, holding or double tapping the thing does.

editor.busyEditor.tabWatch.context: First of three tabs of an opened row (the others are Look and Tap): what makes the thing count as busy and what the detail shows. A verb: what the widget watches.

editor.busyEditor.tapChip.context: Last part of the one-line summary of a closed row, after the middle dots, when the thing has a tap, hold or double tap that does something. Lower case, two words at most.

editor.busyEditor.underName.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what the line under the name of a busy thing shows (since when, power, time left, text or nothing).

editor.busyExample.dishwasher.context: Made-up name of the example dishwasher in the preview of the "Busy now" tile. The English source is not an English word on purpose: write the usual plain name of a dishwasher in the language.

editor.busyExample.dryer.context: Made-up name of the example tumble dryer in the preview of the "Busy now" tile. The English source is not an English word on purpose: write the usual plain name of a tumble dryer in the language.

editor.busyExample.music.context: Made-up name of the example music player in the preview of the "Busy now" tile. The English source is not an English word on purpose: write the plain word for music in the language.

editor.busyExample.title.context: Title of the example "Busy now" tile in the add-widgets window preview: the widget lists devices that are running right now.

editor.busyExample.washer.context: Made-up name of the example washing machine in the preview of the "Busy now" tile. The English source is not an English word on purpose (a Dutch home’s name for it): write the usual plain name of a washing machine in the language, as a person would name it in their Homey.

editor.buttonsEditor.addButton.context: Button with a plus icon that opens the area for adding a button to the widget.

editor.buttonsEditor.atMost.context: Text of the disabled add button once the widget has as many buttons as it can take. For example: At most 12.

params.max: The most buttons the widget takes. A number.

editor.buttonsEditor.change.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small pencil button on a button in the list: it opens the settings of that button.

params.name: The name of the button’s device, flow, mood or dashboard. Not translated.

editor.buttonsEditor.colour.context: Label of the row of colour swatches that colours one button.

editor.buttonsEditor.doneAdding.context: Small button that closes the add-a-button area and goes back to the list of buttons.

editor.buttonsEditor.icon.context: Label of the icon picker that gives one button its own icon.

editor.buttonsEditor.kindDashboard.context: Second line of a button in the list that opens a dashboard, and the grey label of a dashboard candidate in the add list.

editor.buttonsEditor.kindDevice.context: Second line of a button in the list when it is a device whose action is unknown, and the grey kind label of a candidate: this button controls a device.

editor.buttonsEditor.kindFlow.context: Second line of a button in the list that starts a flow, and the grey kind label of a flow candidate when it has no folder. A flow is a Homey automation: keep the word Flow.

editor.buttonsEditor.kindMood.context: Second line of a button in the list that sets a mood, and the grey label of a mood candidate that has no room. A mood is a Homey scene.

editor.buttonsEditor.label.context: Label of the text field where a button gets its own name instead of the device’s, and the screen reader label of that field.

editor.buttonsEditor.moveDown.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a button one place down in the list.

editor.buttonsEditor.moveUp.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a button one place up in the list.

editor.buttonsEditor.noRoom.context: Heading above the devices in the add list that are not in any room.

editor.buttonsEditor.none.context: Empty-state line where the list of buttons would be, before one is added.

editor.buttonsEditor.nothingToAdd.context: Line in the add-a-button area when the open tab has nothing left to add, without a search. For example: Nothing to add in Moods.

params.tab: The label of the open tab, such as "Moods". Already translated.

editor.buttonsEditor.remove.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button that removes a button from the widget.

editor.buttonsEditor.removedFromHomey.context: Name shown for a button whose device, flow, mood or dashboard no longer exists in the Homey, in place of its name.

editor.buttonsEditor.search.en: Search devices, flows, moods and dashboards
editor.buttonsEditor.search.context: Placeholder of the search box in the add-a-button area. It searches every tab at once.

editor.buttonsEditor.sliderValue.context: Screen reader label of the slider that sets the level a device button goes to. Not visible as text.

editor.buttonsEditor.tabDashboards.context: Tab in the add-a-button area: the list of dashboards. The other tabs are Devices, Flows and Moods.

editor.buttonsEditor.tabDevices.context: Tab in the add-a-button area: the list of devices. The other tabs are Flows, Moods and Dashboards.

editor.buttonsEditor.tabFlows.context: Tab in the add-a-button area: the list of flows (Homey automations). The other tabs are Devices, Moods and Dashboards.

editor.buttonsEditor.tabMoods.context: Tab in the add-a-button area: the list of moods (Homey scenes). The other tabs are Devices, Flows and Dashboards.

editor.buttonsEditor.toValue.context: Label above a slider that sets the level a device button goes to. For example: To 30%.

params.value: The level the slider is at now, with its unit: "30%" or "21 °C".

editor.buttonsEditor.whatItDoes.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what a device button does when tapped: switch it on and off, dim it to a level, and so on.

editor.buttonsEditor.whatToAdd.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs (Devices, Flows, Moods, Dashboards) in the add-a-button area. Not visible as text.

editor.buttonsExample.title.context: Title of the example Buttons tile in the add-widgets window preview: the widget shows a row of buttons that switch devices, start flows and set moods.

editor.chartSettings.ariaDetail.context: Screen reader label of the switch "Detail". Not visible as text.

editor.chartSettings.ariaPlacement.context: Screen reader label of the switch "Placement". Not visible as text.

editor.chartSettings.ariaRange.context: Screen reader label of the switch "Range". Not visible as text.

editor.chartSettings.ariaType.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown "Type". Not visible as text.

editor.chartSettings.detail15m.context: Option in the "Detail" segmented control of a chart: one point for every 15 minutes.

editor.chartSettings.detailAuto.context: First option in the "Detail" segmented control of a chart: as fine as the data allows (the finest points), chosen automatically. The others are 15 min, Hourly and Daily.

editor.chartSettings.detailDaily.context: Option in the "Detail" segmented control of a chart: one point for every day.

editor.chartSettings.detailHourly.context: Option in the "Detail" segmented control of a chart: one point for every hour.

editor.chartSettings.fewer.context: Small button under the ticked readings that folds the rarely used readings away again.

editor.chartSettings.fieldDetail.context: Label of the switch that chooses how fine the chart is: how many points it has (fine, 15 min, hourly, daily).

editor.chartSettings.fieldPlacement.context: Label of the switch that chooses where the chart sits on the tile: behind the content or below it.

editor.chartSettings.fieldRange.context: Label of the switch that chooses the period the chart covers (6 h, 12 h, 24 h, 7 days, 30 days).

editor.chartSettings.fieldType.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses the type of the chart (area, line, columns…).

editor.chartSettings.limit.en: Below the content the chart draws {most, plural, one {# reading: the first one ticked} other {# readings: the first # ticked}}.
editor.chartSettings.limit.context: Note shown when more readings are ticked than a chart below the content can draw: only the first ones ticked are drawn.

params.most: How many readings a chart below the content draws. A number.

editor.chartSettings.more.context: Small button under the readings the tile shows: it unfolds the other readings of the device, many of which a meter has. The number says how many.

params.count: How many more readings there are. A number.

editor.chartSettings.placeBackground.context: First of two options (segmented control) for "Placement" of a chart: it is drawn behind the content of the tile. The other is "Below".

editor.chartSettings.placeInline.context: Second of two options (segmented control) for "Placement" of a chart: it is drawn below the content of the tile. The other is "Behind".

editor.chartSettings.range12h.context: Option in the "Range" segmented control of a chart: the last 12 hours. h is hours.

editor.chartSettings.range24h.context: Option in the "Range" segmented control of a chart: the last 24 hours. h is hours.

editor.chartSettings.range30d.context: Option in the "Range" segmented control of a chart: the last 30 days.

editor.chartSettings.range6h.context: Option in the "Range" segmented control of a chart: the last 6 hours. h is hours. The other options are 12 h, 24 h, 7 days and 30 days.

editor.chartSettings.range7d.context: Option in the "Range" segmented control of a chart: the last 7 days.

editor.chartSettings.smooth.context: Label of a switch: whether the lines of the chart are drawn smooth instead of with straight pieces between points. Also its screen reader label.

editor.chartSettings.tickOne.en: Tick a reading to draw its history on the tile. It shows what’s recorded, so start recording it in the device’s details if you haven’t.
editor.chartSettings.tickOne.context: Help text shown while no reading is ticked: ticking one makes the tile draw a chart. A reading only has a history when it is recorded, which is switched on in the details of the device.

editor.chartSettings.typeArea.context: Choice in the dropdown "Type" for a chart: a line with the space under it filled. The other types are Line, Columns, Stacked columns and Steps.

editor.chartSettings.typeBar.context: Choice in the dropdown "Type" for a chart: vertical bars, one per period.

editor.chartSettings.typeLine.context: Choice in the dropdown "Type" for a chart: a plain line.

editor.chartSettings.typeStacked.context: Choice in the dropdown "Type" for a chart: vertical bars with the readings stacked on top of each other.

editor.chartSettings.typeStep.context: Choice in the dropdown "Type" for a chart: a line that stays level until the value changes, like stairs.

editor.childPageTabs.add.context: Label and tooltip of the plus button after the page tabs of a Stack: adds another page. A command.

editor.childPageTabs.full.en: {max, plural, one {# page is the most} other {# pages is the most}}
editor.childPageTabs.full.context: Tooltip of the disabled plus button after the page tabs of a Stack, when the stack has as many pages as it can have: no more can be added.

params.max: The most pages a Stack can have. A number, 12.

editor.childPageTabs.label.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs, one per page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages). A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.childPageTabs.menuRename.context: Item of the menu of a page tab of a Stack: opens the dialog to change the page’s name and icon. A command; the dots say a dialog follows.

editor.childPageTabs.menuWhen.context: Item of the menu of a page tab of a Stack: opens the dialog where the person sets when the page is shown (always, or only while conditions hold). A command; the dots say a dialog follows.

editor.childPageTabs.moveLeft.context: Item of the menu of a page tab of a Stack: moves the page one place to the left among the pages, for people who don’t drag tabs. A command.

editor.childPageTabs.moveRight.context: Item of the menu of a page tab of a Stack: moves the page one place to the right among the pages, for people who don’t drag tabs. A command.

editor.childPageTabs.options.context: Screen reader label of the small menu button on a page tab of a Stack: it opens the menu of that page (name, when to show, move, remove).

params.page: The name of the page. The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.childPageTabs.removePage.context: Red item of the menu of a page tab of a Stack: removes the page and the tiles on it, after a confirmation. A command; the dots say a dialog follows.

editor.childPageTabs.shows.context: Tooltip of the small eye icon on a page tab of a Stack: the page is not always shown, and this says when it is, such as "Shown while someone is home".

params.when: A phrase that says when the page is shown, built from its settings, such as "while someone is home". Still English.

editor.childTileMenu.configure.context: Item of the menu of a tile inside a widget (for example a tile on a page of a Stack): opens the settings of that tile. A command; the dots say a dialog follows.

editor.childTileMenu.moveToPage.context: Item of the menu of a tile on a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages). It opens a submenu that lists the other pages, to move the tile to one of them. A command.

editor.childTileMenu.remove.context: Red item of the menu of a tile inside a widget, with a keyboard shortcut at its right. It removes the tile (an undo is offered afterwards). A command.

editor.childTileMenu.style.context: Item of the menu of a tile inside a widget (for example a tile on a page of a Stack): opens the style panel for that tile (colours, corners, borders). A command; the dots say a dialog follows.

editor.childTileMenu.takeOut.context: Item of the menu of a tile inside a widget (for example on a page of a Stack): takes the tile out of the widget and puts it back on the dashboard itself. A command.

editor.childTileProblems.outside.en: Outside the widget’s grid: drag it back inside, or make the widget bigger.
editor.childTileProblems.outside.context: Short warning marked on a tile inside a widget (for example a page of a Stack) in the tiles editor: the tile sits outside the widget’s grid, because the widget was made smaller after the tile was placed. It tells the person how to fix it: drag the tile back inside, or make the widget bigger. Nothing is moved on its own.

editor.childTileProblems.overlap.context: Short warning marked on a tile inside a widget (for example a page of a Stack) in the tiles editor: it sits on top of another tile of the same page.

editor.childTileProblems.summary.en: {count, plural, one {# tile can’t be drawn as it is.} other {# tiles can’t be drawn as they are.}}
editor.childTileProblems.summary.context: Warning line (with a warning icon) in the settings of a widget that holds tiles, such as a Stack, under the line that says how many tiles it holds: some of those tiles can’t be drawn, for example because a device is gone or a tile sits outside the widget’s grid.

params.count: How many tiles can’t be drawn. A number, at least 1.

editor.childTiles.firstPage.context: Name given to the first page of a Stack (or of another widget with pages) when Tiledash makes that page itself, for example when tiles are stacked as one page. It is saved as the page’s name, which the owner can change later. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages, swiped or tabbed through.

editor.childTiles.tile.context: Name given to the page of a Stack for a tile that has no name of its own (and whose widget is not known), when each tile gets a page of its own. It is saved as the page’s name, which the owner can change later. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.childTiles.widget.context: Name of a widget that holds tiles (such as a Stack) when the owner gave it no name and its type is not known any more. It stands where the widget’s name would be, in the title of the tiles window and in the Put into menu.

editor.childTilesDialogs.removeCan.en: The tiles go with the page. This can’t be undone.
editor.childTilesDialogs.removeCan.context: Text of the confirmation dialog for removing a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages): the tiles on the page are removed with it, and it can’t be undone.

editor.childTilesDialogs.removeConfirm.context: Red button of the confirmation dialog for removing a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages). A command.

editor.childTilesDialogs.removeLast.en: It is the last page, and a widget with pages keeps at least one.
editor.childTilesDialogs.removeLast.context: Text of the dialog for removing a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages) when it is the only page left: it can’t be removed, because such a widget always keeps at least one page. The Remove page button is disabled. "It" is the page.

editor.childTilesDialogs.removeTitle.en: {count, plural, =0 {Remove {page}?} one {Remove {page} and its tile?} other {Remove {page} and its # tiles?}}
editor.childTilesDialogs.removeTitle.context: Title of the confirmation dialog for removing a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages). It says how many tiles go with the page, when there are any. The text under it says this can’t be undone.

params.count: How many tiles are on the page. A number, 0 or more.
params.page: The name of the page. The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.childTilesDialogs.whenTitle.context: Title of the dialog where the person sets when a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages) is shown: always, or only while conditions hold, for example someone is home.

params.page: The name of the page. The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.childTilesDialogs.whenTitleNoPage.context: Title of the dialog where the person sets when a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages) is shown, for the moment its name is not known. Rarely seen.

editor.childTilesEditor.description.en: Place the tiles where they go, the way they sit on this widget. Drag to move, the corner to resize.
editor.childTilesEditor.description.context: Text under the title of the window where the tiles inside a widget are placed: the window shows the widget’s own grid, tiles are dragged to move them, and a tile’s corner is dragged to resize it.

editor.childTilesEditor.done.context: Button in the footer of the tiles window. It closes the window; changes are already saved. A command.

editor.childTilesEditor.saved.context: Small note at the left of the footer of the tiles window: every change is saved at once, so there is no Save button.

editor.childTilesEditor.title.context: Title of the window where the tiles inside a widget are placed (for example the pages of a Stack), when the widget has only one Tiles setting.

params.title: The widget’s name on the dashboard, such as "Ground floor". The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.childTilesEditor.titleOfSetting.context: Title of the window where the tiles inside a widget are placed, when the widget has more than one Tiles setting: the setting’s name, then the widget’s name, such as "Rooms in Ground floor".

params.label: The name of the Tiles setting, such as "Rooms". A widget’s own label, still English.
params.title: The widget’s name on the dashboard. The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.childTilesPane.addPage.context: Small button next to the notice that there is no room on a page of a Stack: adds another page. A command.

editor.childTilesPane.addTiles.context: Main button in the bar over the grid of the tiles window: opens the widget picker to add tiles to the page being edited. A command.

editor.childTilesPane.atLimit.en: {max, plural, one {# tile is the most in one widget.} other {# tiles is the most in one widget.}}
editor.childTilesPane.atLimit.context: Notice in the bar over the grid when the widget holds as many tiles as it can: no more can be added. The Add tiles button is disabled.

params.max: The most tiles one widget can hold. A number.

editor.childTilesPane.count.en: {count, plural, one {{count} tile on this {kind, select, page {page} other {grid}}} other {{count} tiles on this {kind, select, page {page} other {grid}}}}
editor.childTilesPane.count.context: Line in the bar over the grid of the tiles window: how many tiles are on the page being edited, or on the grid of a widget without pages. The number is shown in bold (the b tag).

params.count: How many tiles are there. A number, 0 or more.
params.kind: What the tiles sit on: page (a page of a Stack or similar widget) or grid (a widget without pages). Not shown; it picks the word.

editor.childTilesPane.emptyGrid.context: Empty state in the grid of a widget that holds tiles without pages, when it has no tiles yet.

editor.childTilesPane.emptyPage.context: Empty state in the grid of a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages) that has no tiles yet.

editor.childTilesPane.noRoomLeft.context: Notice in the bar over the grid of a widget that holds tiles without pages, when the grid has no free spot for another tile.

editor.childTilesPane.noRoomOnPage.context: Notice in the bar over the grid of a page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages) when the page has no free spot for another tile. An Add a page button may follow it.

editor.childTilesPane.shows.context: Line with an eye icon in the bar over the grid, when the page being edited is not always shown: it says when it is, such as "Shown while someone is home".

params.when: A phrase that says when the page is shown, built from its settings, such as "while someone is home". Still English.

editor.childTilesPane.total.context: Small text after the count in the bar over the grid: how many tiles the whole widget holds, over all its pages, out of the most it can hold. For example "· 14 of 60".

params.max: The most tiles the widget can hold. A number.
params.total: How many tiles the widget holds in all. A number.

editor.childTilesView.pagesAndTiles.en: {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}}, {tiles, plural, =0 {no tiles yet} one {# tile} other {# tiles}}
editor.childTilesView.pagesAndTiles.context: Bold line at the top of the Tiles field in the settings of a widget with pages, such as a Stack: how many pages it has, then how many tiles they hold together, or that there are none yet. For example "3 pages, 14 tiles". A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

params.pages: How many pages the widget has. A number, at least 1.
params.tiles: How many tiles all the pages hold together. A number, 0 or more.

editor.childTilesView.tiles.en: {tiles, plural, =0 {No tiles yet} one {# tile} other {# tiles}}
editor.childTilesView.tiles.context: Bold line at the top of the Tiles field in the settings of a widget that holds tiles without pages: how many tiles it holds, or that it holds none yet.

params.tiles: How many tiles the widget holds. A number, 0 or more.

editor.colorSwatches.name.en: {colour, select, accent {Accent} lit {Lit} cool {Cool} good {Good} warn {Warn} danger {Danger} text {Text} surface {Surface} canvas {Canvas} chart1 {Chart 1} chart2 {Chart 2} chart3 {Chart 3} chart4 {Chart 4} chart5 {Chart 5} other {Chart 6}}
editor.colorSwatches.name.context: Tooltip and screen reader label of one swatch: the name of a colour of the theme. Accent is the theme’s highlight colour; Lit is the colour of something switched on, such as a lamp; Cool is a cold, blue tone; Good, Warn and Danger are the colours for fine, careful and bad; Text is the colour of text; Surface and Canvas are the colours of cards and of the dashboard behind them; Chart 1 to Chart 6 are the colours of the series in charts.

params.colour: Which colour: accent, lit, cool, good, warn, danger, text, surface, canvas, chart1 to chart6.

editor.configSections.chart.context: Name of the tab of a widget’s settings with the settings of a small history chart on the tile. Also a heading, a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in.

editor.configSections.content.context: Name of the first tab of a widget’s settings: what the tile shows, such as its devices or its text. Also a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor, and the first choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in. Also named inside a help text of the Layout tab ("Add values on the Content tab first"), where it must be the same word.

editor.configSections.layout.context: Name of the tab of a widget’s settings where the person arranges how the parts of the tile are placed. Also a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor, and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in.

editor.configSections.live.context: Name of the tab of a Floor plan tile’s settings with what the live plan shows (drawn from the plan, following the devices): furniture, the rooms’ readings, light glow, the heat map. Also a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in.

editor.configSections.look.context: Name of the tab of a widget’s settings where the person chooses how the tile looks: its design (the look), colours and decimals. Also a heading, a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in.

editor.configSections.map.context: Name of the tab of a widget’s settings with the settings of a map behind the tile. Also a heading, a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in.

editor.configSections.picture.context: Name of the tab of a Floor plan tile’s settings for when it shows a picture of the level made in the floor planner: day or night, and the rings that show where to tap. Also a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in.

editor.configSections.tap.context: Name of the tab of a widget’s settings where the person chooses what happens when the tile is tapped or clicked. Also a small tag on a setting in the widget code editor and a choice in the list of tabs a setting can sit in. Short for the action of tapping, not a water tap.

editor.copyTo.copy.en: Copy to {count, plural, one {# dashboard} other {# dashboards}}
editor.copyTo.copy.context: The main button of the dialog that copies a tile to other dashboards, with how many are ticked, such as "Copy to 3 dashboards".

params.count: How many dashboards are ticked.

editor.copyTo.dashboards.context: Screen reader label of the list of dashboards to tick in the dialog that copies a tile. Not visible as text.

editor.copyTo.description.en: A copy goes at the bottom of each dashboard you pick, its own tile there from then on.
editor.copyTo.description.context: Line under the title of the dialog that copies a tile to other dashboards. Each picked dashboard gets its own copy, which can then be changed apart from the original.

editor.copyTo.none.en: There are no other dashboards on this Homey.
editor.copyTo.none.context: Shown in the dialog that copies a tile when the account has no other dashboard.

editor.copyTo.title.context: Title of the dialog that copies a tile to other dashboards. {tile} is the tile’s name, such as "Navigation".

params.tile: The name of the tile being copied.

editor.cornerControl.allCorners.context: Small text next to the radius slider while all four corners are picked, so the slider changes all of them.

editor.cornerControl.bottomLeft.context: Name of the bottom left corner of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that corner, and a word in the list of picked corners.

editor.cornerControl.bottomRight.context: Name of the bottom right corner of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that corner, and a word in the list of picked corners.

editor.cornerControl.groupLabel.context: Screen reader label of the little tile whose four corners are buttons: the picked corners are the ones the slider changes. Not shown.

editor.cornerControl.mixed.context: Small text next to the radius slider while the selected tiles have corners that differ.

editor.cornerControl.radiusLabel.context: Screen reader label of the slider for how round the picked corners are, in pixels. Not shown.

editor.cornerControl.topLeft.context: Name of the top left corner of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that corner, and a word in the list of picked corners.

editor.cornerControl.topRight.context: Name of the top right corner of the tile: the tooltip and screen reader label of the button for that corner, and a word in the list of picked corners.

editor.cssHooks.add.context: Screen reader label of one chip: tapping it adds an empty CSS rule for that class name to the tile’s CSS. It names the class and says what it reaches.

params.selector: The CSS class name or selector, such as .big or :host. Code, not translated.
params.what: A short description of what the class name reaches, such as "Small text". Translated.

editor.cssHooks.listLabel.context: Screen reader label of the list of chips with CSS class names a tile’s CSS can style. Not shown.

editor.dashboard.addHeading.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while no tile is selected. It adds a heading (a line of text with an optional row of summaries that sits between tiles) to the dashboard. A noun.

editor.dashboard.addStack.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while no tile is selected. It adds a stack (one tile that shows several pages of tiles, swiping or tabbing between them). A noun.

editor.dashboard.addSummaries.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while no tile is selected. It adds a row of summaries (small live figures like "3 lights on") without a heading text. A noun.

editor.dashboard.addWidget.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while no tile is selected. It opens the picker to add a widget (a type of tile) to the dashboard. A noun, short for "add a widget".

editor.dashboard.clearSelection.context: Name of the small × button at the end of the edit toolbar while tiles are selected. It deselects all tiles. Appears as a tooltip and is read out by screen readers.

editor.dashboard.done.context: Blue button at the top right while editing a dashboard. It leaves edit mode; the changes are saved already.

editor.dashboard.duplicate.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected. It makes a copy of each selected tile next to the original.

editor.dashboard.hideOn.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected and a screen size other than the desktop is being edited. It hides the selected tiles on that size only, such as "Hide on Phone".

params.size: The name of the screen size being edited, such as Phone or Tablet. Already translated.

editor.dashboard.hintFixed.en: Click a tile to change or hide it
editor.dashboard.hintFixed.context: Grey hint at the end of the edit toolbar, shown while no tile is selected on a screen size whose layout follows the desktop and cannot be moved by hand. It says tiles can be changed or hidden by clicking them.

editor.dashboard.hintInStack.en: Drag to move · corner to resize · Escape to go back
editor.dashboard.hintInStack.context: Grey hint at the end of the edit toolbar while a stack is being edited where it is. It explains how to work with its tiles: drag a tile to move it, drag its corner to resize it, and press Escape to go back to the whole dashboard. The dots separate three short instructions.

editor.dashboard.hintMovable.en: Drag to move · corner to resize · drag on empty space to select
editor.dashboard.hintMovable.context: Grey hint at the end of the edit toolbar, shown while no tile is selected. It explains how to work with tiles with a mouse or finger: drag a tile to move it, drag its corner to resize and drag over empty space to select several. The dots separate three short instructions.

editor.dashboard.inStack.context: Status at the left of the floating edit toolbar while a stack is being edited where it is on the dashboard (its tiles can be moved and resized; the rest of the dashboard is faded). A stack is one tile that shows several pages of tiles.

editor.dashboard.newStack.context: First choice of the "Put into" menu. It makes a new stack (one tile that shows several pages of tiles) and puts the selected tiles in it. The other choices are existing widgets that can hold tiles.

editor.dashboard.pasteStyle.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected and a style was copied before. It gives the selected tiles the copied look.

editor.dashboard.putInto.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected. It opens a menu of widgets (such as stacks) that can hold tiles, to move the selected tiles into one of them. Followed by an arrow.

editor.dashboard.remove.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected. It removes the selected tiles from the dashboard (an undo is offered afterwards).

editor.dashboard.removeEverywhere.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected and a screen size other than the desktop is being edited. It removes the selected tiles from the dashboard on every screen size, not only this one.

editor.dashboard.stackAddTiles.context: Button in the edit toolbar while a stack is being edited where it is. It opens the widget picker to add tiles to the page of the stack that is shown.

editor.dashboard.stackDone.context: Button in the edit toolbar while a stack is being edited where it is. It goes back to editing the whole dashboard (the dashboard stays in edit mode).

editor.dashboard.stackOnePage.context: First choice of the menu of "Stack these". It makes a stack with one page that holds all the selected tiles together.

editor.dashboard.stackPageEach.context: Second choice of the menu of "Stack these". It makes a stack with one page for every selected tile.

editor.dashboard.stackThese.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected. It makes a stack (one tile that shows several pages of tiles, swiping or tabbing between them) out of the selected tiles. It opens a small menu to choose between one page and one page each.

editor.dashboard.style.context: Button in the edit toolbar, shown while tiles are selected. It opens the panel to change how the selected tiles look (colours, borders, size of text). A noun, not a verb.

editor.dashboard.summariesAdd.context: Small button beside the dashboard name while editing, when the dashboard has no summaries yet. It opens the dialog to add summaries (small live figures like "3 lights on").

editor.dashboard.summariesEdit.context: Small button beside the dashboard name while editing, when the dashboard already has summaries (small live figures like "3 lights on"). It opens the dialog to change them.

editor.dashboard.titleHidden.context: Grey note above the dashboard name while the dashboard is edited. The dashboard is set to hide its name and summaries when it is not being edited (for a sleep screen), so the person knows why they will not see them later.

editor.dashboardGrid.describe.en: {selected, select, yes {{label}, selected.} other {{label}.}} {width} by {height}, column {column}, row {row}. Arrows move, Shift and arrows resize.
editor.dashboardGrid.describe.context: Description of a tile in edit mode, read out by screen readers when it is focused. It gives the name of the tile, whether it is selected, its size in grid cells (width by height), its place (column and row) and the keyboard help: the arrow keys move the tile, Shift with the arrow keys resizes it. Not visible as text.

params.column: The column of the tile's left edge, counted from 1.
params.height: The height of the tile in grid cells.
params.label: The name of the tile. Not translated.
params.row: The row of the tile's top edge, counted from 1.
params.selected: "yes" while the tile is selected, "no" otherwise.
params.width: The width of the tile in grid cells.

editor.dashboardGrid.hiddenNow.context: Small label on a tile in edit mode that is not shown on the screen right now, followed by a dot and why (a short reason such as a condition that is not met). Starts with a small crossed-out eye.

params.reason: Why the tile is hidden, already a short phrase in the language of the page.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuArrange.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode, only on a widget that holds other tiles (such as a Stack, which shows tiles on pages). It opens a window to place, add and remove the tiles inside it and its pages. The dots mean a window follows.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuArrangeSetting.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode, on a widget that holds tiles in more than one group, one item per group, such as "Arrange Rooms…". It opens a window to place, add and remove the tiles of that group. The dots mean a window follows.

params.label: The name the widget gives that group of tiles, such as Rooms. Written by the widget’s maker, not translated.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuConfigure.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode. It opens the settings of the tile (which device it shows, what it looks like). The dots mean a panel follows.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuCopyStyle.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode. It remembers the look of the tile so it can be pasted onto other tiles. A command.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuCopyTo.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode. It opens a dialog to tick other dashboards, each of which gets a copy of the tile (for example a navigation bar).

editor.dashboardGrid.menuDuplicate.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode, with a keyboard shortcut at its right. It makes a copy of the tile next to it.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuHideOn.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode while a screen size other than the desktop is edited. It hides the tile on that size only, such as "Hide on Phone".

params.size: The name of the screen size being edited, such as Phone or Tablet. Already translated.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuMakeYours.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode. It makes a copy of the built-in widget that the person can edit as their own widget (with its own template and style). On the Free plan it carries a "Pro" badge. The dots mean an editor follows.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuPasteStyle.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode, greyed out until a style was copied. It gives the tile the look that was copied. A command.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuRemove.context: Red item of the menu of a tile in edit mode, with a keyboard shortcut at its right. It removes the tile from the dashboard (an undo is offered afterwards).

editor.dashboardGrid.menuRemoveEverySize.context: Red item of the menu of a tile in edit mode while screen sizes (desktop, tablet, phone) are in use. It removes the tile from the dashboard on every screen size, not only the one being edited.

editor.dashboardGrid.menuStyle.context: Item of the menu of a tile in edit mode. It opens the panel to change how the tile looks (colours, borders, text size). A noun. The dots mean a panel follows.

editor.dashboardGrid.options.context: Name of the small pencil button on a tile in edit mode that opens the menu of the tile, read out by screen readers and shown as a tooltip. It starts with the name of the tile, such as "Kitchen light options".

params.label: The name of the tile. Not translated.

editor.dashboardName.copyName.context: The name suggested for a copy of a dashboard, filled into the name field for the person to change, such as "Home copy".

params.name: The name of the dashboard that is copied. Not translated.

editor.dashboardName.createGroup.context: Blue button in the footer of the dialog that makes a new group (a folder for dashboards) in the sidebar. A command.

editor.dashboardName.duplicate.context: Blue button in the footer of the dialog that duplicates a dashboard. It makes the copy. A command.

editor.dashboardName.duplicateDescriptio.en: A copy of {name} with all its tiles, headings and settings.
editor.dashboardName.duplicateDescriptio.context: Text under the title of the dialog that duplicates a dashboard. It says what the copy holds: everything of the original. A tile is a box on the dashboard; a heading is a line of text between tiles.

params.name: The name of the dashboard that is copied. Not translated.

editor.dashboardName.groupDescription.en: A folder for dashboards in the sidebar. Drag dashboards onto it to put them in.
editor.dashboardName.groupDescription.context: Text under the title of the dialog that makes a new group in the sidebar. A group is a folder; dashboards are dragged onto it in the sidebar.

editor.dashboardName.iconLabel.context: Label above the row of icons to choose from in the dialog for name and icon, and the name of that row for screen readers. The icon shows beside the name.

editor.dashboardName.moreIcons.context: Name of the search list of all icons that opens below the row of suggested icons, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.dashboardName.nameLabel.context: Label of the text field for the name of a dashboard, a group or a page, in the dialog for name and icon.

editor.dashboardName.nameTooLong.context: Red message under the name field of a page when the name is too long. It says the longest name allowed.

params.max: The most characters a name may have, a number such as 40.

editor.dashboardName.pageDescription.context: Text under the title of the dialog that names a page of a stack (a tile that shows several pages of tiles). The name and icon appear on the tab that selects the page.

editor.dashboardName.previewSidebar.context: Small grey heading above a preview in the dialog for the name and icon of a dashboard or group. The preview shows its row in the sidebar as it will look.

editor.dashboardName.previewTab.context: Small grey heading above a preview in the dialog that names a page of a stack. The preview shows the page’s tab as it will look.

editor.dashboardName.titleDuplicate.context: Title of the dialog that makes a copy of a dashboard: the person gives the copy a name and an icon. A command.

editor.dashboardName.titleEdit.context: Title of the dialog that changes the name and the icon of a dashboard. Opened from the dashboard menu.

editor.dashboardName.titleGroup.context: Title of the dialog that changes the name and icon of an existing group (a folder for dashboards) in the sidebar. A noun.

editor.dashboardName.titleNewGroup.context: Title of the dialog that makes a new group (a folder for dashboards) in the sidebar. The person gives it a name and an icon.

editor.dashboardName.titlePage.en: Name and icon of the page
editor.dashboardName.titlePage.context: Title of the dialog that changes the name and icon of one page of a stack (a tile that shows several pages of tiles, swiping or tabbing between them). The name and icon show on the page’s tab.

editor.dashboardName.untitled.context: Shown in the preview row instead of the name while the name field is still empty.

editor.dashboardNaming.duplicateFailed.context: Red text in the dialog that duplicates a dashboard when making the copy failed.

editor.dashboardNaming.limitReached.context: Title of an amber message (toast) when a new dashboard (a copy, or one from the wizard) does not fit the person’s plan. A text about the plan’s limit follows below it, with a button that leads to the plans.

editor.dashboardNaming.made.context: Green message (toast) after a dashboard was duplicated. The quotes are around the name of the new copy.

params.name: The name of the new dashboard, the copy. Not translated.

editor.dashboardNaming.saveFailed.en: Couldn’t save the name and icon.
editor.dashboardNaming.saveFailed.context: Red text in the dialog for name and icon when saving the new name and icon of a dashboard failed.

editor.dashboardPage.addFailed.context: Red message (toast) when adding a widget (a type of tile) to the dashboard failed.

editor.dashboardPage.copiedTo.en: Copied to {count, plural, one {# dashboard} other {# dashboards}}
editor.dashboardPage.copiedTo.context: Green message (toast) after a tile was copied to other dashboards with "Copy to other dashboards…". {count} is how many got a copy.

params.count: How many dashboards got a copy.

editor.dashboardPage.copyFailed.en: Couldn’t copy the tile to every dashboard ({count} done).
editor.dashboardPage.copyFailed.context: Red message (toast) when copying a tile to other dashboards failed part way. {count} is how many dashboards already got their copy.

params.count: How many dashboards got a copy before it failed.

editor.dashboardPage.deleteBody.en: Its tiles are removed with it. Your devices and flows are not touched.
editor.dashboardPage.deleteBody.context: Text of the confirmation dialog before a dashboard is deleted. It says the tiles of the dashboard go with it, and reassures that the devices and flows (automations) of the Homey are not changed.

editor.dashboardPage.deleteConfirm.context: Red button of the confirmation dialog before a dashboard is deleted. It confirms and deletes the dashboard. A command.

editor.dashboardPage.deleteFailed.context: Red message (toast) when deleting the dashboard failed.

editor.dashboardPage.deleteTitle.context: Question that is the title of the confirmation dialog before a dashboard is deleted. The quotes are around the name of the dashboard.

params.name: The name of the dashboard. Not translated.

editor.dashboardPage.headingSaveFailed.context: Red message (toast) when saving a heading (a line of text with an optional row of summaries between tiles) failed.

editor.dashboardPage.installedFromCommun.context: Green message (toast) after a widget from the community (where people share widgets) was installed by adding it to the dashboard from the add-widgets window. A button "View" follows it.

params.title: The widget’s name, such as "EV charger". Not translated.

editor.dashboardPage.nothingToAdd.context: Amber message (toast) when the person confirmed the widget picker without having chosen any widget, so nothing was added.

editor.dashboardPage.reloadFailed.context: Red message (toast) after the person pressed Reload on the warning that the dashboard was changed elsewhere, and loading the newest version failed.

editor.dashboardPage.removeFailed.context: Red message (toast) when removing tiles from the dashboard failed.

editor.dashboardPage.removed.en: {inside, plural, =0 {{count, plural, one {Tile removed} other {{count, number} tiles removed}}} one {{count, plural, one {Tile and the tile inside it removed} other {{count, number} tiles and the tile inside them removed}}} other {{count, plural, one {Tile and the {inside, number} tiles inside it removed} other {{count, number} tiles and the {inside, number} tiles inside them removed}}}}
editor.dashboardPage.removed.context: Title of the message (toast) after tiles were removed from the dashboard, with an Undo button. It says how many tiles were removed and, when a removed tile was a stack or other widget that holds tiles of its own, how many tiles inside it went with it.

params.count: How many tiles were removed from the dashboard, at least 1.
params.inside: How many tiles inside the removed tiles went with them, 0 when none.

editor.dashboardPage.startFailed.context: Red message (toast) when choosing which dashboard the app opens with failed.

editor.dashboardPage.startOff.context: Message (toast) after the person stopped this dashboard from being the one the app opens with, so the app opens on the devices page again.

params.page: The name of the devices page, "Devices". Already translated.

editor.dashboardPage.startOn.en: {name} opens when you start the app
editor.dashboardPage.startOn.context: Message (toast) after the person made this dashboard the one the app opens with when it starts. It begins with the name of the dashboard.

params.name: The name of the dashboard. Not translated.

editor.dashboardPage.styleBody.en: How the selected tiles look, on top of the theme. The dashboard follows as you go.
editor.dashboardPage.styleBody.context: Description under the title of the style dialog. It says the choices here change the look of the selected tiles on top of the theme, and that the dashboard behind the dialog updates while the person chooses.

editor.dashboardPage.styleDone.context: Button at the foot of the style dialog. It closes the dialog; the changes are applied already.

editor.dashboardPage.styleTitle.context: Title of the dialog in which the person changes how the selected tiles look (colours, borders, text size). A noun.

editor.dashboardPage.summariesSaveFailed.context: Red message (toast) when saving the summaries next to the dashboard name (small live figures like "3 lights on") failed.

editor.dashboardPage.themeFailed.context: Red message (toast) when changing the theme of the dashboard failed.

editor.dashboardPage.themeSameAsApp.context: Name of the theme choice in the dashboard settings when the dashboard has no theme of its own: it follows the theme of the app. After the dot comes the name of the theme the app has now.

params.theme: The name of the theme the app has now, with its mode, such as "Tonal · Automatic". Already in the language of the page.

editor.dashboardPage.thisTile.context: Name used for a tile that has no name of its own, in the style panel and its settings, such as in "Style of this tile". A tile is a box on the dashboard.

editor.dashboardPage.undo.context: Button on the message (toast) after tiles were removed. It puts them back where they were, with their settings and style.

editor.dashboardPage.viewInCommunity.context: Button in the message "… installed from the community": opens the widget’s page in the community. A command.

editor.dashboardPage.widgetsAdded.en: {count, plural, one {Widget added} other {# widgets added}}
editor.dashboardPage.widgetsAdded.context: Green message (toast) after one or more widgets (types of tiles) were added to the dashboard from the picker.

params.count: How many widgets were added, at least 1.

editor.dashboardPins.changeFailed.context: Red message (toast) when showing a dashboard in the sidebar or hiding it from there failed. The dashboard stays as it was.

editor.dashboardPins.hidden.context: Title of a message (toast) after a dashboard was hidden from the sidebar. The quotes are around the name of the dashboard.

params.name: The name of the dashboard. Not translated.

editor.dashboardPins.hiddenHint.context: Text under the message that a dashboard was hidden from the sidebar. It says the dashboard is not gone: the switcher, the search window opened with the ⌘K key combination, still lists it.

editor.dashboardPins.shown.context: Message (toast) after a dashboard was set to show in the sidebar. The quotes are around the name of the dashboard.

params.name: The name of the dashboard. Not translated.

editor.dashboardSettings.aroundDashboard.context: Label of the setting for the room between the dashboard’s edge and its tiles (the margin), on the Spacing tab. Shown above a row of choices and a slider.
Name of the row of choices (Theme, None, Small, Large) for the room around the dashboard, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.dashboardSettings.aroundDashboard.en: Space around the dashboard, in pixels
editor.dashboardSettings.aroundDashboard.context: Name of the slider that sets the room around the dashboard in pixels, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.dashboardSettings.betweenTiles.context: Label of the setting for the room (the gap) between the tiles of the dashboard, on the Spacing tab. Shown above a row of choices and a slider.

editor.dashboardSettings.betweenTilesCho.context: Name of the row of choices (Theme, None, Tight, Normal, Roomy) for the room between tiles, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.dashboardSettings.betweenTilesPix.context: Name of the slider that sets the room between tiles in pixels, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.dashboardSettings.betweenTouching.context: Label of the setting for the line drawn where two touching tiles meet, and the name of its row of choices for screen readers. Shown only when there is no room between tiles.

editor.dashboardSettings.caption.context: Small caption under the preview in the dashboard settings dialog. It says the room between tiles and the room around the dashboard that the preview shows, both in pixels (px), such as "12 px between tiles · 16 px around".

params.gap: The room between tiles in pixels, a number.
params.margin: The room around the dashboard in pixels, a number.

editor.dashboardSettings.description.en: How this dashboard is laid out. The preview, and the dashboard behind, follow every change.
editor.dashboardSettings.description.context: Text under the title of the dashboard settings dialog. Every change shows at once in the preview inside the dialog and on the dashboard behind it, and is undone unless saved.

editor.dashboardSettings.fitToScreen.context: Label of a switch on the Layout tab, also its name for screen readers. When on, the whole dashboard is scaled to fit the screen.

editor.dashboardSettings.fitToScreenHint.en: Scaled to fit the screen, centred, without scrolling.
editor.dashboardSettings.fitToScreenHint.context: Help text under the Fit to screen switch: the dashboard is made smaller or larger to fill the screen, centred, so nobody needs to scroll.

editor.dashboardSettings.freePlacement.context: Label of a switch on the Layout tab, also its name for screen readers. When on, tiles stay exactly where the person puts them, with gaps allowed.

editor.dashboardSettings.freePlacementHi.en: Tiles stay where you put them, instead of rising to the top.
editor.dashboardSettings.freePlacementHi.context: Help text under the Free placement switch. Without it, tiles move up to close any gaps; with it they stay where they were dropped.

editor.dashboardSettings.gapNone.context: Choice in the row for the room between tiles: no room at all, tiles touch. A short word on a segmented button.

editor.dashboardSettings.gapNormal.context: Choice in the row for the room between tiles: the usual room. A short word on a segmented button, between Tight and Roomy.

editor.dashboardSettings.gapRoomy.context: Choice in the row for the room between tiles: a generous room. A short word on a segmented button, the largest choice.

editor.dashboardSettings.gapTheme.context: First choice in the row for the room between tiles: use the room the theme asks for, followed by that room in pixels, such as "Theme · 12". The theme is the set of colours, type and corners the dashboard uses.

params.gap: The theme’s own room between tiles in pixels, a number such as 12.

editor.dashboardSettings.gapTight.context: Choice in the row for the room between tiles: a small room. A short word on a segmented button, between None and Normal.

editor.dashboardSettings.leadLayout.en: How the tiles fill the screen, where they can go, and the title.
editor.dashboardSettings.leadLayout.context: Short line at the top of the Layout tab of the dashboard settings dialog (tabs above the settings): fitting the dashboard to the screen, placing tiles freely, and its title.

editor.dashboardSettings.leadLook.context: Short line at the top of the Look tab of the dashboard settings dialog (tabs above the settings): the colour theme of this dashboard.

editor.dashboardSettings.leadPopups.en: What opens over the dashboard by itself when something happens.
editor.dashboardSettings.leadPopups.context: Short line at the top of the Popups tab of the dashboard settings dialog (tabs above the settings): popups that open on their own on an event, such as the doorbell’s camera when it rings.

editor.dashboardSettings.leadSpacing.en: The room between the tiles, and around them.
editor.dashboardSettings.leadSpacing.context: Short line at the top of the Spacing tab of the dashboard settings dialog (tabs above the settings), saying what is in it.

editor.dashboardSettings.marginLarge.context: Choice in the row for the room around the dashboard: a large margin. A short word on a segmented button, the largest choice.

editor.dashboardSettings.marginNone.context: Choice in the row for the room around the dashboard: no room, the tiles reach the edge. A short word on a segmented button.

editor.dashboardSettings.marginSmall.context: Choice in the row for the room around the dashboard: a small margin. A short word on a segmented button, between None and Large.

editor.dashboardSettings.marginTheme.context: First choice in the row for the room around the dashboard: use the room the theme asks for. A short word on a segmented button. The theme is the set of colours, type and corners.

editor.dashboardSettings.oneShape.context: Label of a switch on the Spacing tab, also its name for screen readers. When on, tiles that touch square off the corners they share, so a group of tiles looks like one shape.

editor.dashboardSettings.oneShapeFlush.en: Their inner corners square off; the outer ones stay round.
editor.dashboardSettings.oneShapeFlush.context: Help text under the switch for touching tiles, shown while there is no room between tiles. The corners where tiles meet become square; the outer corners stay round.

editor.dashboardSettings.oneShapeSpaced.en: Tiles side by side square off the corners they share; the outer corners of the group stay round.
editor.dashboardSettings.oneShapeSpaced.context: Help text under the switch for touching tiles, shown while there is some room between tiles. Tiles that sit next to each other get square corners where they meet; the outer corners of the group stay round.

editor.dashboardSettings.seamLine.context: Choice for the border between two touching tiles: draw a thin line where they meet. A short phrase on a segmented button.

editor.dashboardSettings.seamNone.context: Choice for the border between two touching tiles: draw nothing where they meet. A short phrase on a segmented button.

editor.dashboardSettings.seamsHint.en: Drawn once where two tiles meet, never doubled; or none at all.
editor.dashboardSettings.seamsHint.context: Help text under the choice for the line between touching tiles. A line is drawn once where two tiles meet, not once for each tile, or left out.

editor.dashboardSettings.showTitle.context: Label of a switch on the Layout tab, also its name for screen readers. When on, the dashboard’s name and summaries show above its tiles.

editor.dashboardSettings.showTitleHint.en: The dashboard’s name and summaries above its tiles.
editor.dashboardSettings.showTitleHint.context: Help text under the Show the title switch. Summaries are small live figures such as "3 lights on".

editor.dashboardSettings.tabLayout.context: Name of the second tab of the dashboard settings dialog. It holds fit to screen, free placement and showing the title.

editor.dashboardSettings.tabLook.context: Name of the third tab of the dashboard settings dialog. It holds the theme (colours, type and corners) of the dashboard.

editor.dashboardSettings.tabPopups.context: Name of the fourth tab of the dashboard settings dialog. It holds popups that open over the dashboard on their own when something happens, such as the doorbell’s camera when it rings.

editor.dashboardSettings.tabSpacing.context: Name of the first tab of the dashboard settings dialog. It holds the room between tiles and around the dashboard.

editor.dashboardSettings.themeChange.context: Small button beside the name of the dashboard’s theme on the Look tab. It opens the dialog to pick another theme.

editor.dashboardSettings.themeHint.context: Help text under the name of the dashboard’s theme on the Look tab. It says what a theme is made of: colours, the type (fonts) and the shape of the corners.

editor.dashboardSettings.title.context: Title of the dialog that changes how one dashboard is laid out, and the name of its row of tabs (Spacing, Layout, Look) read out by screen readers.

editor.dashboardSettingsSave.saveFailed.context: Red message (toast) when saving the dashboard settings (spacing, layout, title) failed. The dashboard goes back to the settings it had.

editor.dashboardTheme.apply.context: Blue button in the footer of the theme dialog. It keeps the picked theme for this dashboard and closes the dialog. A command.

editor.dashboardTheme.description.en: How this dashboard looks. The dashboard behind shows your choice.
editor.dashboardTheme.description.context: Text under the title of the theme dialog. While the person picks a theme, the dashboard behind the dialog already shows it.

editor.dashboardTheme.title.context: Title of the dialog that picks how one dashboard looks: its theme (colours, type and corners). Opened from the dashboard settings.

editor.decimalsPicker.auto.context: First option of a row of buttons (a segmented control) that sets how many decimals a number on a tile shows. Auto means Tiledash picks what reads well for the size of the number. The other options show the number as it would read, such as "2.7".

editor.devicesPicker.hasNone.context: Reason shown in small warning text under a picked device that no longer fits the tile, because the tile needs at least one of several things and the device has none of them any more. It lists them, such as "Has none of On/Off or Dim any more".

params.capabilities: What the tile needs one of, as a list in the language’s style, such as "On/Off or Dim". Already translated where possible.

editor.devicesPicker.lacks.context: Reason shown in small warning text under a picked device that no longer fits the tile, because the device lost something the tile needs. It lists what is missing, such as "No longer has Smoke Alarm and Temperature".

params.capabilities: What the device lost, as a list in the language’s style, such as "Smoke Alarm and Temperature". Already translated where possible.

editor.devicesPicker.modeEvery.context: Second option of a two-option switch (segmented control) in a tile’s settings: the tile shows every device of the Homey that fits what it needs, including devices added later. The other option is "Pick devices".

editor.devicesPicker.modeLabel.context: Screen reader label of the two-option switch "Pick devices / Every device that fits". Not visible as text. It names what the setting holds, as the widget words it.

params.noun: The name of the setting in lowercase, such as "smoke detectors" or "lights". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.devicesPicker.modePick.context: First option of a two-option switch (segmented control) in a tile’s settings: the person picks the devices one by one, in an order. The other option is "Every device that fits".

editor.devicesPicker.note.en: {label} you add to Homey later show up by themselves.
editor.devicesPicker.note.context: Note with an info icon under the list of devices a tile shows when it takes every device that fits. It says that devices added to the Homey (the smart-home hub) later appear by themselves. It starts with the name of the setting, such as "Smoke detectors".

params.label: The name of the setting as the widget words it, such as "Smoke detectors". Not translated by this message.

editor.devicesPicker.overflow.en: {fitting, number} fit; the tile shows the first {max, number}.
