editor.devicesPicker.overflow.context: First sentence of the note under the list when more devices fit than the tile can show, such as "14 fit; the tile shows the first 12." The note continues with another sentence.

params.fitting: How many devices fit. A number.
params.max: How many the tile shows at most. A number.

editor.devicesPicker.removedName.context: Name shown on a row of the picked devices in place of a device that no longer exists on the Homey (the smart-home hub). Under it a reason is shown. A status, not a command.

editor.devicesPicker.removedReason.context: Reason shown in small warning text under a picked device that no longer exists on the Homey (the smart-home hub).

editor.devicesPicker.wrongKind.en: No longer the right kind of device
editor.devicesPicker.wrongKind.context: Reason shown in small warning text under a picked device that no longer fits the tile, when no more specific reason is known: the device changed so it is not the kind of device the tile needs any more.

editor.energyExample.charge.context: Title of the battery charge reading of the made-up home battery of the example Energy flow tile: how full the battery is, as a percentage.

editor.energyExample.power.context: Title of the electrical power reading of the made-up devices of the example Energy flow tile (grid, solar, battery): the power in watts.

editor.energySettings.addChargeReading.context: Quiet button under the charge readings of the battery or car: it opens a picker to add a reading of how full the battery is.

editor.energySettings.addReading.context: Quiet button under the readings of a part: it opens a picker to add a power reading or variable. A reading is a measurement of a device.

editor.energySettings.batteryChargeHint.context: Small grey text under the charge readings of the home battery: with more batteries their charge is averaged, not added.

editor.energySettings.batteryChargeTitle.context: Small title above the charge readings of the home battery: how full the battery is, as a percentage.

editor.energySettings.batteryHint.en: Positive means charging. More batteries add up.
editor.energySettings.batteryHint.context: Small grey text under the readings of the Home battery part: a positive power means the battery is charging; with more batteries the powers are added together.

editor.energySettings.batteryTitle.context: Name of the part of the Energy flow for the battery of the home that stores electricity.

editor.energySettings.carChargeHint.en: Shows as a ring round the car.
editor.energySettings.carChargeHint.context: Small grey text under the charge readings of the car: the charge is drawn as a ring around the car in the flow.

editor.energySettings.carChargeTitle.context: Small title above the charge readings of the car: how full the car’s battery is, as a percentage.

editor.energySettings.carHint.en: The charger’s power, or the car’s.
editor.energySettings.carHint.context: Small grey text under the readings of the Car part: it takes the power of the charger, or of the car itself.

editor.energySettings.carTitle.context: Name of the part of the Energy flow for the electric car and its charger.

editor.energySettings.countAsReports.context: Screen reader label of the button on a reading’s row that undoes the reversing: the reading is counted as the meter reports it. Shown while the reading is reversed.

editor.energySettings.countOtherWay.context: Screen reader label of the button on a reading’s row that reverses it: for a meter that counts the other way round (positive and negative swapped).

editor.energySettings.followPart.context: Button on an energy part (solar, grid…) of a house that was given readings of its own: makes it follow the account’s energy meters again.

editor.energySettings.fromMeters.context: Small badge in the header of a part, or beside a charge title, when its readings come from the person’s energy meters (set in the Energy settings) and not from this tile.

editor.energySettings.gridHint.en: Positive means taking from the grid. Reverse a meter that counts the other way.
editor.energySettings.gridHint.context: Small grey text under the readings of the Grid part: a positive power means electricity is taken from the grid; a meter that counts the other way can be reversed with the button of its row.

editor.energySettings.gridTitle.context: Name of the part of the Energy flow for the electricity grid (the public network). Also named in a note about parts that are set on the tile itself.

editor.energySettings.nothingPicked.en: Nothing picked: this part is left out.
editor.energySettings.nothingPicked.context: Grey text under the header of a part with no readings: without a reading, this part is left out of the flow.

editor.energySettings.pick.context: Quiet button at the end of an empty row on the Today tab: it opens a picker to choose the daily reading for that total. A verb.

editor.energySettings.remove.context: Screen reader label of the button on a reading’s row that removes that reading.

editor.energySettings.showPart.en: Show {part, select, grid {grid} solar {solar} battery {home battery} other {car}}
editor.energySettings.showPart.context: Screen reader label of the switch in the header of a part that shows or hides that part in the flow. Not visible as text. It says which part: grid, solar, home battery or car.

params.part: Which part: grid, solar, battery (the home battery) or car. A select value, not shown; each branch is the name of that part as used after "Show".

editor.energySettings.solarHint.context: Small grey text under the readings of the Solar part: with more than one inverter (the device that turns solar power into mains power) their power is added together.

editor.energySettings.solarTitle.context: Name of the part of the Energy flow for solar panels.

editor.energySettings.tabParts.context: First tab of the Energy flow settings: the parts of the flow (grid, solar, home battery, car), each with its readings.

editor.energySettings.tabToday.context: Second tab of the Energy flow settings: the totals for today.

editor.energySettings.tabsLabel.context: Screen reader label of the two tabs (Parts, Today) in the settings of the Energy flow widget. Not visible as text.

editor.energySettings.todayExported.context: Name of a row on the Today tab: the total energy sent back to the grid today, along the bottom of a large tile.

editor.energySettings.todayIntro.en: Totals for today along the bottom of a large tile, from your meters’ daily readings. Leave one empty to leave it out.
editor.energySettings.todayIntro.context: Introduction on the Today tab: the three totals (solar, used, to the grid) are shown along the bottom of a large tile, taken from the daily readings of the person’s meters; a row left empty is left out.

editor.energySettings.todaySolar.context: Name of a row on the Today tab: the total energy the solar panels made today, along the bottom of a large tile.

editor.energySettings.todayUsed.context: Name of a row on the Today tab: the total energy the home used today, along the bottom of a large tile.

editor.entryGestures.addDouble.context: Small button with a plus icon under an entry: it adds a setting for what a double tap on the entry does.

editor.entryGestures.addHold.context: Small button with a plus icon under an entry: it adds a setting for what holding (a long press on) the entry does.

editor.entryGestures.doubleOf.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what a double tap on one entry does. For example: Double tap: Living room lamp.

params.name: What the entry is called: its own name (such as a button’s name) or a short phrase like "this value". Not translated further.

editor.entryGestures.holdOf.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what holding (a long press on) one entry does. For example: Hold: Living room lamp.

params.name: What the entry is called: its own name (such as a button’s name) or a short phrase like "this value". Not translated further.

editor.entryGestures.tapOf.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what a single tap on one entry does. For example: Tap: Living room lamp.

params.name: What the entry is called: its own name (such as a button’s name) or a short phrase like "this value". Not translated further.

editor.entryGestures.thisEntry.context: A short name for a list entry, used when the host gives none, in lower case: it goes into labels such as "Tap: this entry". Not a sentence.

editor.eventPopups.add.context: Button under the list on the Popups tab of a dashboard’s settings.

editor.eventPopups.asFull.context: Choice of how a popup opens, read after what opens: covering the whole dashboard. Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.asPopup.context: Choice of how a popup opens, read after what opens: in the middle of the dashboard. For example "Open Upstairs as a popup". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.asSide.context: Choice of how a popup opens, read after what opens: as a panel along the right edge of the dashboard. Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.becomes.context: Choice in a dropdown of a popup’s trigger, read after the name of a value and before one of its choices or a text: it changes to that. For example "Alarm becomes Triggered". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.choiceLabel.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown with the choices of a value (for example the modes of an alarm) in a popup’s trigger. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.empty.context: Shown on the Popups tab of a dashboard’s settings while none are set up.

editor.eventPopups.full.en: A dashboard has at most {max} popups.
editor.eventPopups.full.context: Shown instead of the Add button on the Popups tab once a dashboard has the most popups it can have. {max} is a number, such as 8.

params.max: The most popups a dashboard can have.

editor.eventPopups.goesAbove.context: Choice in a dropdown of a popup’s trigger, read after the name of a number value and before a number: it rises past that number. For example "Power goes above 3000". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.goesBelow.context: Choice in a dropdown of a popup’s trigger, read after the name of a number value and before a number: it falls below that number. For example "Battery goes below 20". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.inputNumber.context: Screen reader label of the number field after "goes above" or "goes below" in a popup’s trigger. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.inputText.context: Screen reader label of the text field after "becomes" in a popup’s trigger, for a value without a list of choices. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.intro.en: Open something over this dashboard when it happens, wherever the dashboard shows. A sleeping wall panel wakes up for it.
editor.eventPopups.intro.context: Short explanation at the top of the Popups tab in a dashboard’s settings. The popups set here open on their own, for example the doorbell’s camera when someone rings.

editor.eventPopups.kindCamera.context: Choice of what a popup opens: a camera, big and live.

editor.eventPopups.kindDashboard.context: Choice of what a popup opens: another dashboard of the account.

editor.eventPopups.kindDevice.context: Choice of what a popup opens: a device’s controls and readings.

editor.eventPopups.look.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown on a popup’s card that picks how it opens: as a popup, a side panel or full screen. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.noCameras.context: Greyed hint beside "A camera" in the dropdown of what a popup opens, when the Homey has no camera to show.

editor.eventPopups.noDashboards.context: Greyed hint beside "A dashboard" in the dropdown of what a popup opens, when the account has no other dashboard.

editor.eventPopups.open.context: Label at the start of the second line of a popup’s card, before what opens: a camera, a device or a dashboard. Reads as "Open Front door camera".

editor.eventPopups.openKind.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown on a popup’s card that picks what opens: a camera, a device or a dashboard. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.remove.context: Screen reader label of the bin button on a popup’s card. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.target.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown on a popup’s card that picks which camera, device or dashboard opens. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.testLabel.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown after the picked value of a popup: turns on, turns off, goes above, goes below or becomes. Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.turnsOff.context: Choice in a dropdown of a popup’s trigger, read after the name of a yes/no value: it changes to no, or off. For example "Garage door contact turns off". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.turnsOn.context: Choice in a dropdown of a popup’s trigger, read after the name of a yes/no value: it changes to yes, or on. For example "Front door bell turns on" (someone rings). Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.eventPopups.valueLabel.context: Screen reader label of the button that picks the value a popup waits for (a device’s reading, a variable, who is home). Not visible as text.

editor.eventPopups.when.context: Label at the start of the first line of a popup’s card, before the value that sets it off (for example a doorbell) and how it changes. Reads as "When Front door bell turns on".

editor.everySize.detail.en: {phone}, {tablet} and {desktop} show the same tile; only where it sits can differ.
editor.everySize.detail.context: Second sentence of the small note at the top of a tile’s settings and style tabs, after the bold "Applies to every size." It explains that the tile itself is the same on all three screen sizes, and only its place on the grid can differ per size.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.phone: The name of the Phone size. A name, already translated.
params.tablet: The name of the Tablet size. A name, already translated.

editor.everySize.title.context: Bold first sentence of a small note at the top of a tile’s settings and style tabs. It says the settings below are the same on all three screen sizes (Phone, Tablet and Desktop); only where the tile sits can differ per size. The note’s second sentence follows it.

editor.favouriteColours.removed.context: Title of the message (toast) after a colour was taken off the favourite colours, with an Undo button.

editor.favouriteColours.saveFailed.context: Red message (toast) when saving a change to the favourite colours failed. The list is back to how it was.

editor.favouriteColours.undo.context: Button on the message "Favourite colour removed": puts the colour back among the favourites, in its place.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.about.context: Line under a picture in the list: its style (already in the person’s language), the view (2D seen from above, 2.5D at an angle) and how far it is turned.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.auto.en: The one you use on tiles
editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.auto.context: First choice in the list of pictures: leave it to the picture chosen in the floor planner with "Use on tiles".

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.autoHint.context: Line under the first choice: it changes when another picture is chosen there.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.chooseFir.en: Pick a floor plan and its level first.
editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.chooseFir.context: Shown instead of the list while the tile has no floor plan.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.make.en: Make one in the floor planner
editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.make.context: Link to the floor planner, where pictures are made.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.none.en: No picture of this level yet. Make one in the floor planner.
editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.none.context: Shown instead of the list when the level has no pictures.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.outOfDate.context: Small tag on a picture: the level changed since it was made.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.room.context: Line under a picture made of one room up close.

editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.versions.en: {versions, select, dayNight {Day and night} day {Day} other {Night}}
editor.floorPlanPictureSetting.versions.context: Small tag on a picture: which versions it has.

editor.floorPlanSetting.gone.en: The plan this tile showed is gone. Choose another.
editor.floorPlanSetting.gone.context: Shown under the floor plan dropdown when the plan the tile showed was deleted.

editor.floorPlanSetting.level.context: Label of the dropdown that picks a level of the floor plan (a floor of the house: ground floor, first floor).

editor.floorPlanSetting.none.en: No floor plans of this Homey yet. Draw your house under Floor plans first.
editor.floorPlanSetting.none.context: Shown in a tile’s settings instead of the floor plan dropdowns while the person has no floor plan. "Floor plans" is the name of a page in the sidebar.

editor.floorPlanSetting.paused.context: Hint beside a floor plan in the dropdown when it is paused (the account has more plans than its subscription allows) and a tile can’t show it.

editor.floorPlanSetting.plan.context: Label of the dropdown that picks one of the person’s floor plans for a tile.

editor.floorPlanSetting.show.context: Label of the dropdown that picks whether the tile shows the whole level of the floor plan or one room of it.

editor.floorPlanSetting.showHint.en: One room fills the tile and the rooms around it fade.
editor.floorPlanSetting.showHint.context: Line under the dropdown "Show" of a floor plan setting.

editor.floorPlanSetting.wholeLevel.context: Choice in the dropdown "Show": the tile shows the whole level of the floor plan.

editor.followDesktop.description.en: {size}’s own arrangement is thrown away. It shows {kind, select, phone {{desktop}’s tiles in one column} other {{desktop}’s arrangement}} again, and follows every move made on {desktop}.
editor.followDesktop.description.context: First part of the explanation in the confirmation dialog for following Desktop again on one screen size. It says that what the person arranged for this size is lost, what the size will show instead and that later moves on Desktop reach it. "Desktop’s tiles in one column" is for Phone, whose tiles are stacked in reading order; "Desktop’s arrangement" is for Tablet, which shows the Desktop layout as it is. If tiles are hidden on the size, a second sentence follows after a space.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.kind: Which size this is: phone for Phone, other for Tablet. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.size: The name of the size that would follow Desktop again, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.followDesktop.follow.context: Red button in the confirmation dialog for following Desktop again: it throws away the arrangement of this size so that it shows the Desktop layout again.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.followDesktop.hidden.en: {count, plural, one {The tile hidden on {size} stays hidden.} other {The # tiles hidden on {size} stay hidden.}}
editor.followDesktop.hidden.context: Second sentence of the explanation in the confirmation dialog for following Desktop again, shown only when tiles are hidden on that size. It says they stay hidden afterwards.

params.count: How many tiles are hidden on the size. A number, at least 1.
params.size: The name of the size that would follow Desktop again, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.followDesktop.keep.context: Button in the confirmation dialog for following Desktop again: it closes the dialog and keeps the arrangement the person made for this size. The safe choice.

params.size: The name of the size that was arranged, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.followDesktop.title.context: Title of a confirmation dialog in edit mode. The person has arranged one screen size (Phone or Tablet) by hand and asks it to follow the main layout, Desktop, again. The title asks whether to do that.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.size: The name of the size that would follow Desktop again, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.headingSettings.add.context: Button with a plus icon that opens a menu to add a summary (such as "Lights on" or a reading) to the list.

editor.headingSettings.addGesture.en: {gesture, select, hold {Add hold} double {Add double tap} other {Add tap}}
editor.headingSettings.addGesture.context: Small button with a plus icon on the Tap tab: it adds the setting for what holding (a long press) or double tapping the summary pill does.

params.gesture: Which gesture: "hold" or "double" (a double tap). Not shown.

editor.headingSettings.addReading.context: Last item of the Add menu, after the ready-made summaries: it adds a summary that shows one reading, such as a device’s temperature, an energy value or a variable. The dots mean the person picks which one next.

editor.headingSettings.alignCentre.context: Choice of the segmented control "Alignment": the heading’s title is placed in the middle of the row.

editor.headingSettings.alignLeft.context: Choice of the segmented control "Alignment": the heading’s title is placed at the left (the start) of the row.

editor.headingSettings.alignment.context: Label of the choice between Left and Centre: where the heading’s title sits. Also its screen reader label.

editor.headingSettings.caption.context: Label of the text field for a heading’s caption: small text shown after the title.

editor.headingSettings.captionHint.en: Small text after the title. Optional.
editor.headingSettings.captionHint.context: Help text under the field "Caption". Optional means the person may leave it empty.

editor.headingSettings.captionPlaceholde.context: Example shown faintly in the empty caption field: a floor of a house, in lower case, to show what a caption can be.

editor.headingSettings.changeIcon.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the round button that shows the summary’s icon and opens the icon picker.

editor.headingSettings.dashboardSummarie.context: Title of the dialog that sets up the summaries shown under the dashboard’s name, about everything on the dashboard. A summary is a small pill with a live fact, such as "3 lights on".

editor.headingSettings.decimals.context: Label above the picker for how many digits after the decimal point a number shows. Also its screen reader label.

editor.headingSettings.descriptionHeadin.en: A title for the tiles below it, with live facts about them.
editor.headingSettings.descriptionHeadin.context: Description under the title of the dialog for a heading: a title over the tiles below it, with live facts (summaries) about those tiles.

editor.headingSettings.descriptionTitle.en: Live facts under the dashboard’s name, about everything on it.
editor.headingSettings.descriptionTitle.context: Description under the title of the dialog for the dashboard’s own summaries: what summaries are and where they appear. "Live facts" are small pills that count or show things, such as "3 lights on".

editor.headingSettings.empty.en: Show totals, counts or alarms next to the title, like power use, lights on or whether a smoke detector went off.
editor.headingSettings.empty.context: Help text shown while the list of summaries is empty: examples of what summaries can show. A summary is a small pill with a live fact.

editor.headingSettings.fieldReadingPick.context: Orange note under the reading picker while no reading is chosen yet: the summary needs one to be saved.

editor.headingSettings.gestureDouble.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what a double tap on a summary pill does. A noun.

editor.headingSettings.gestureHold.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what holding a summary pill (a long press) does. A noun.

editor.headingSettings.gestureTap.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what a single tap on a summary pill does. A noun.

editor.headingSettings.heading.context: Title of the dialog when the heading’s own title is shown, and the name of its first tab, which holds the title, caption and alignment. A heading is a title above a group of tiles.

editor.headingSettings.headingSettings.context: Screen reader label of the two tabs of the dialog (Heading and Summaries). Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.icon.context: Screen reader label of the icon picker in the popover of a summary’s icon.

editor.headingSettings.label.context: Placeholder and screen reader label of the field for the pill’s text label, used when the summary has no standard label to show faintly.

editor.headingSettings.looks.context: Label above the icon button and the label field of the Look tab: how the pill looks. Plural, as in "the looks".

editor.headingSettings.moveDown.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a summary one step down in the list.

editor.headingSettings.moveUp.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a summary one step up in the list.

editor.headingSettings.name.context: Label of the text field for the name of a heading that shows no title: a name only the person sees, to tell the row apart while editing.

editor.headingSettings.nameHint.en: Not shown on the dashboard; it names the row while editing.
editor.headingSettings.nameHint.context: Help text under the field "Name" of a heading that shows no title: the name is for the editing screen only. "The row" is the heading’s row of summaries.

editor.headingSettings.namePlaceholder.context: Example shown faintly in the empty name field of a heading without a title: a name for a row of summaries.

editor.headingSettings.noLabel.context: Label of a checkbox on a summary that shows one reading: when ticked the pill shows only the value, without a text label.

editor.headingSettings.nothingMatches.context: Line shown in the list of devices when the search finds none. The search text is repeated between quotes.

params.query: What the person typed in the search box. Not translated.

editor.headingSettings.onlyYes.context: Label of a checkbox on a summary that shows a yes/no variable: when ticked the pill is only shown while the variable is yes, and hidden otherwise.

editor.headingSettings.pickAtLeastOne.context: Orange note under the list of devices while none is ticked: the summary needs at least one to be saved.

editor.headingSettings.pickDevices.context: Orange note on the row of a summary that counts devices but has none chosen yet: it cannot be saved until at least one is picked.

editor.headingSettings.pickReading.context: Orange note on the row of a summary that shows one reading but has none chosen yet: it cannot be saved until one is picked.

editor.headingSettings.pickedCount.context: Small line under the list of devices: how many are ticked out of how many can be picked. For example "3 of 12 picked".

params.picked: How many devices are ticked. A number.
params.total: How many devices can be picked. A number.

editor.headingSettings.preview.context: Screen reader name of the preview beside a heading’s settings: the heading drawn as it will show on the dashboard, with its summaries live. Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.readingTapDevices.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill that shows one device’s reading does: open that device.

editor.headingSettings.readingTapHistory.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill that shows one device’s reading does: open a chart of how that reading changed over time. "Its" is the reading’s.

editor.headingSettings.readingTapSwitch.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill that shows one device’s reading does: switch that device on or off. "It" is the device.

editor.headingSettings.remove.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the small trash button at the end of a summary’s row: it removes the summary.

editor.headingSettings.room.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown that chooses the room whose devices a summary counts. Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.rowHostEnergy.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows an energy value, such as the power of the grid: what the value is, then where it comes from (the Energy tab of the value picker).

params.label: The name of the value, such as "Grid power". Comes from the Homey’s energy data; not translated here.

editor.headingSettings.rowHostMissing.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows an energy value this Homey does not have (for example the energy settings changed).

editor.headingSettings.rowHostPrices.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows an electricity or gas price: what the value is, then where it comes from (the Prices tab of the value picker).

params.label: The name of the value, such as "Price now". Comes from the Homey’s energy data; not translated here.

editor.headingSettings.rowReading.context: Name of a summary’s row in the list when it shows one reading that has not been chosen yet. A noun.

editor.headingSettings.rowReadingGone.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows a reading of a device that has been removed from the Homey or no longer has that reading.

editor.headingSettings.rowReadingOf.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows one reading of a device: what is read, then which device. For example "Temperature · Living room thermostat".

params.device: The name of the device. Not translated.
params.title: What is read, such as "Temperature". Comes from the device’s data; not translated here.

editor.headingSettings.rowVariable.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows a Logic variable of the Homey: the variable’s name, then that it is a variable. For example "Washing machine on · Variable".

params.name: The name of the variable, as set in the Homey. Not translated.

editor.headingSettings.rowVariableGone.context: Name of the row of a summary that shows a Logic variable that has been removed from the Homey.

editor.headingSettings.scopeDashboard.context: Choice of the segmented control "Which devices" in the dialog of the dashboard’s own summaries: the summary counts every device on the dashboard.

editor.headingSettings.scopeDevices.context: Choice of the segmented control "Which devices": the summary counts only devices the person ticks one by one.

editor.headingSettings.scopeRoom.context: Choice of the segmented control "Which devices": the summary counts only the devices of one room of the house. A dropdown for the room follows.

editor.headingSettings.scopeSection.context: Choice of the segmented control "Which devices" in the dialog of a heading: the summary counts the devices of the tiles under this heading (until the next heading).

editor.headingSettings.searchLabel.context: Screen reader label of the search box above the list of devices. Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.searchPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the search box above the list of devices a summary can count. Typing narrows the list by device or room name.

editor.headingSettings.settingsOfSummary.context: Screen reader label of the group of three small tabs (Reading or Devices, Look, Tap) of an opened summary. Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.showTitle.context: Label of a switch: whether the heading shows its title text. Also the switch’s screen reader label.

editor.headingSettings.showTitleHint.en: Off: just the summaries, as a row of live facts.
editor.headingSettings.showTitleHint.context: Small help text under the switch "Show the title". "Off" is the state of that switch. Without the title the heading is only the row of summaries (small pills with live facts).

editor.headingSettings.summaries.context: Title of the dialog when the heading shows no title, the name of the tab that holds the list of summaries, and the heading of that list for screen readers. A summary is a small pill with a live fact, such as "3 lights on".

editor.headingSettings.tabDevices.context: Name of the first small tab of an opened summary that counts devices, where it is chosen which devices. Also the label above its content.

editor.headingSettings.tabLook.context: Name of the second small tab of an opened summary: how the pill looks (icon, label, number of decimals). A noun.

editor.headingSettings.tabReading.context: Name of the first small tab of an opened summary that shows one reading (a device’s value, an energy value or a variable), where the reading is picked. Also the label above its content. A noun.

editor.headingSettings.tabTap.context: Name of the third small tab of an opened summary: what happens when the pill is tapped, held or double tapped. A noun.

editor.headingSettings.tapChart.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill that shows an energy or price value does: open that value’s chart.

editor.headingSettings.tapDashboard.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill does: open another dashboard.

editor.headingSettings.tapDefault.context: Small grey hint beside the choice of a tap action that is what the pill does when nothing is changed.

editor.headingSettings.tapDetails.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill does: open a list with the details of what it shows.

editor.headingSettings.tapDevices.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill does: open a list of the devices it counts. The summary counts several devices.

editor.headingSettings.tapFlow.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill does: start a Flow of the Homey. Flow is the Homey feature for automations and stays as it is.

editor.headingSettings.tapHistory.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill does: open a chart of how its value changed over time.

editor.headingSettings.tapNone.context: Choice of what tapping (or holding, or double tapping) a summary pill does: nothing at all.

editor.headingSettings.tapSwitch.context: Choice of what tapping a summary pill does: switch all the devices it counts on or off together. "Them" are the devices of the summary.

editor.headingSettings.title.context: Label of the text field for the heading’s title, which is shown above the tiles.

editor.headingSettings.useDefaultIcon.context: Small button in the icon picker popover that goes back to the icon the summary has by itself, shown while a different icon is chosen.

editor.headingSettings.whenYes.context: Label above a field on a summary that shows a yes/no variable: what the pill says while the variable is yes (true).

editor.headingSettings.whenYesAria.context: Screen reader label of the field "When it is yes": the word the pill shows while the variable is yes. Read as a short sentence start. Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.whichDevices.context: Screen reader label of the choice between "This section" (or "This dashboard"), "A room" and "Devices": which devices the summary counts. Not visible as text.

editor.headingSettings.yesPlaceholder.context: Example shown faintly in the empty field "When it is yes": the standard word shown while a yes/no variable is yes.

editor.hiddenTiles.heading.context: Small grey line under the name of a heading tile in the tray of hidden tiles: what kind of tile it is. A heading is a bar across the dashboard with a title and optional summaries.

editor.hiddenTiles.mood.context: Small grey line under the name of a mood tile in the tray of hidden tiles: what kind of tile it is. A mood is a Homey scene of devices that a tap can switch on.

editor.hiddenTiles.summaries.context: Name of a heading tile in the tray of hidden tiles when it shows only its row of summaries (totals, counts and alarms) and no title text. Also the small grey line under it. A heading is a bar across the dashboard with a title and optional summaries.

editor.hiddenTiles.widget.context: Small grey line under the name of a widget tile in the tray of hidden tiles: what kind of tile it is. A widget is a tile with a design, such as a clock or a weather tile.

editor.hiddenTray.noteEmpty.en: Nothing hidden. A tile’s menu has Hide on {size} for what you don’t need on {device, select, phone {a phone} tablet {a tablet} other {a big screen}}; it stays on the other sizes.
editor.hiddenTray.noteEmpty.context: Small grey note under the empty tray of hidden tiles. It says no tile is hidden on this screen size, and how to hide one: the menu of a tile has an item that hides it on this size only, and the tile stays on the other sizes. <em> is the name of that menu item, "Hide on" followed by the size: use the same wording as the item, which reads "Hide on Phone" in English. The device in the sentence is the kind of screen the size is meant for: a phone for Phone, a tablet for Tablet, a big screen for Desktop.

params.device: The size itself: phone, tablet or desktop. Not shown; it picks the wording (desktop gives "a big screen").
params.size: The name of the screen size being edited, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.hiddenTray.noteHidden.en: Still on {others}. Show puts a tile back where it was on {size}.
editor.hiddenTray.noteHidden.context: Small grey note under the tray of hidden tiles when at least one tile is in it. It says the tiles are still on the other two screen sizes, and what the Show button does. <em> is the name of the Show button after each tile: use the same word as that button.

params.others: The other two screen sizes, as a list, such as "Tablet and Desktop". Already translated.
params.size: The name of the screen size being edited, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.hiddenTray.show.context: Small button after a tile in the tray of hidden tiles. It puts the tile back on the screen size, where it was. The tray’s note below quotes this word.

editor.hiddenTray.title.context: Small heading of the tray under the canvas in edit mode, and the screen reader label of the tray. It lists the tiles hidden on the screen size being edited, Phone or Tablet. The number of tiles follows it in a badge.

params.size: The name of the screen size being edited, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.historyExample.grid.context: Name of the first line of the example power chart: the power taken from the electricity grid. Short, as a legend label.

editor.historyExample.power.context: Title of the example history chart tile, and the title of its readings, in the add-widgets window preview: the electrical power in watts.

editor.historyExample.solar.context: Name of the second line of the example power chart: the power from solar panels. Short, as a legend label.

editor.houseGeneration.acceptAll.context: Button that accepts all the placed spots as they are.

editor.houseGeneration.another.context: Button that opens the questions again to refine the side’s picture (say what should change) or make a new one, for a credit.

editor.houseGeneration.ask.context: Beside the thumbs up and down on a generated picture.

editor.houseGeneration.beforeRefining.context: Name of the side’s picture a refinement started from (one the owner uploaded), listed with the tries to go back to.

editor.houseGeneration.credits.context: How many credits the person has, in the editor’s top bar.

params.count: How many credits.

editor.houseGeneration.deleteTry.context: Button that deletes a try’s picture (not the one in use).

editor.houseGeneration.dialogTitle.context: Title of the dialog that asks a few questions and then generates the side’s picture.

editor.houseGeneration.error.en: {error, select, busy {A picture is being made already.} limit {That’s enough pictures for today; try again tomorrow.} off {Making pictures isn’t available here.} photo {That photo couldn’t be read. Try another (PNG, JPEG or WebP).} other {The picture couldn’t be started.}}
editor.houseGeneration.error.context: Why generating a picture couldn’t start.

params.error: busy, limit, off, photo or failed.

editor.houseGeneration.failed.context: Under a try that failed (its credit came back).

editor.houseGeneration.failedText.en: {status, select, refused {The image model wouldn’t make it from this photo or prompt. Your credit is back.} other {Something went wrong making it. Your credit is back.}}
editor.houseGeneration.failedText.context: Text of that note: refused by the model’s safety rules, or another failure.

editor.houseGeneration.failedTitle.context: Title of the note that a generation failed.

editor.houseGeneration.givenBack.context: Under a try whose credit an admin gave back, with the admin’s reason.

params.reason: The admin’s reason, as they wrote it.

editor.houseGeneration.glad.context: Beside the thumbs after a thumbs up.

editor.houseGeneration.good.context: Accessible name of the thumbs up.

editor.houseGeneration.inUse.context: Under the try that is the side’s picture now.

editor.houseGeneration.making.context: Shown on the side while its picture is being generated.

editor.houseGeneration.makingHint.en: About half a minute. You can leave this page: it carries on.

editor.houseGeneration.notGood.context: Accessible name of the thumbs down.

editor.houseGeneration.note.context: Placeholder of the free text after a thumbs down.

editor.houseGeneration.pending.context: Under a try that is still being made.

editor.houseGeneration.proposedText.en: Check each one: drag it where it belongs, or drop it.
editor.houseGeneration.proposedText.context: Text of the note "We placed your spots", after a generation.

editor.houseGeneration.proposedTitle.context: Title of the note after a generation: spots were placed on the picture for the person.

editor.houseGeneration.reason.en: {reason, select, not-my-house {Doesn’t look like my house} parts {Parts missing or wrong} strange {Strange bits} style {Not the style I chose} other {Cut off or badly framed}}
editor.houseGeneration.reason.context: What went wrong with a generated picture, each a chip to pick.

editor.houseGeneration.refine.context: Button beside “Replace picture” over a side’s picture: opens the questions to say what should change in it (the image model then changes only that, for a credit).

editor.houseGeneration.refined.context: Name of a try that refined the side’s picture (instead of its style); what was asked shows on hover.

editor.houseGeneration.send.context: Sends the thumbs down with its reasons.

editor.houseGeneration.thanks.en: Thanks. We look at every thumbs down; when the picture is our mess, you get the credit back.
editor.houseGeneration.thanks.context: Shown after sending a thumbs down.

editor.houseGeneration.triesHint.en: Every try stays here. Using another keeps the spots you placed; check they still fit.

editor.houseGeneration.triesTitle.context: Heading over the side’s generated pictures, every one kept.

editor.houseGeneration.useTry.context: Accessible name of a try: makes it the side’s picture.

editor.houseGeneration.way.context: Way to get a side’s picture: generated in Tiledash for a credit (the main way).

editor.houseGeneration.wayCost.context: Badge on "Make it in Tiledash": what it costs and how many credits the person has.

params.count: How many credits the person has.

editor.houseGeneration.wayHint.en: From a photo of your house, or a few answers about it, in the style you choose. Its spots come placed for you.

editor.houseGeneration.whatWrong.context: Heading over the reasons after a thumbs down.

editor.houseGeneration.writePrompt.en: Write a prompt for your own ChatGPT or Gemini
editor.houseGeneration.writePrompt.context: Link inside "Upload a picture" that opens the prompt generator.

editor.housePrompt.balance.en: {count, plural, one {You have # credit} other {You have # credits}}
editor.housePrompt.balance.context: How many credits the person has, beside the generate button.

params.count: How many credits.

editor.housePrompt.buy.context: Button shown instead of generating when no credits are left; opens where to buy them.

editor.housePrompt.car.context: Label of a free text field for the electric car’s make, model and colour.

editor.housePrompt.carHint.en: Make, model and colour, in English: a white Skoda Enyaq…
editor.housePrompt.carHint.context: Line under that field: the text goes into the English prompt as typed. Filled in from the Homey when its car app says the make.

editor.housePrompt.consent.en: Your photos and pictures are sent to our image model’s provider to make the picture. Tiledash keeps your photos for 30 days, so we can check the result, then deletes them.
editor.housePrompt.consent.context: Shown under the generate button when photos go with it: generating means agreeing to this.

editor.housePrompt.description.context: Label of a free text field describing the house: its walls, windows, colours…

editor.housePrompt.descriptionHint.en: In English, as much as you like: the walls, the windows, the colours, a porch…
editor.housePrompt.descriptionHint.context: Line under that field: the text goes into the English prompt as typed.

editor.housePrompt.english.en: In English: image models do best with it

editor.housePrompt.enlarge.context: Label of the small button on a style’s example picture that shows it larger.

params.name: The style’s name.

editor.housePrompt.extrasOwn.en: You attach these in your own chat too, after the photo of this side.
editor.housePrompt.extrasOwn.context: Line under that heading when the prompt is for the person’s own chat.

editor.housePrompt.extrasTitle.en: Photos from other sides or angles
editor.housePrompt.extrasTitle.context: Heading over extra photos of the house, each saying what it shows.

editor.housePrompt.floors.context: Label of the choice of how many floors the house has.

editor.housePrompt.generate.context: Button that generates the picture in Tiledash, spending one credit.

editor.housePrompt.generating.context: The generate button while the picture is being made (about half a minute).

editor.housePrompt.helpHint.en: These aren’t made into pictures. They only show the AI more of your house, so this side comes out right.
editor.housePrompt.helpHint.context: Line under “Extra help for the AI”: those photos and pictures are only looked at, never drawn.

editor.housePrompt.helpTitle.context: Heading of an optional part: more photos and the other sides’ pictures, only for the image model to look at.

editor.housePrompt.known.context: Badge beside a tick box that was ticked because the person’s Homey has such a device.

editor.housePrompt.mainPhoto.context: Heading over the photo of the side being made: the one the picture is made from.

editor.housePrompt.mainPhotoOwn.en: You attach it first in your own chat.
editor.housePrompt.mainPhotoOwn.context: Line under that heading when the prompt is for the person’s own chat.

editor.housePrompt.makeHere.context: Heading of having the picture generated in Tiledash, for a credit, on the last step.

editor.housePrompt.makeHereHint.en: {photo, select, yes {With this prompt and your photos. Its spots come placed for you, and a failed try gives your credit back.} other {With this prompt. Its spots come placed for you, and a failed try gives your credit back.}}

params.photo: yes when photos go with it, else no.

editor.housePrompt.making.context: Card at the top of the second step naming the one side of the house this run makes a picture of (a label, not something happening now).

params.side: The side’s name, as the person named it (“Garden side”).

editor.housePrompt.makingHint.en: One picture per run: this side. For another side, open it and run this again.
editor.housePrompt.makingHint.context: Line on the “Making: {side}” card: one run makes one side’s picture.

editor.housePrompt.open.context: Link under "Upload a picture" in the house editor that opens the prompt generator.

editor.housePrompt.photoPreparing.context: A photo row while the browser makes the photo smaller before sending it.

editor.housePrompt.photoRemove.context: Button that takes a photo off the list.

editor.housePrompt.photoRetry.context: Link under a failed photo upload: sends the same file again.

editor.housePrompt.photoSending.context: A photo row while the photo is being sent.

editor.housePrompt.photoTitle.en: Do you have a photo of this side?

editor.housePrompt.photoUpload.context: Button in an empty photo row: picks a photo of the house and uploads it.

editor.housePrompt.pickStyle.context: Button under a style’s larger picture: picks that style.

editor.housePrompt.roofSide.context: Which roof side has the solar panels: the front, the back or both.

editor.housePrompt.step.context: The steps of the prompt generator, shown as a row at the top.

editor.housePrompt.style.en: {style, select, soft-3d {Tiledash soft 3D} modern-dark {Modern dark} clay {Clay miniature} flat {Flat illustration} photoreal {True to life} blueprint {Blueprint} neon-twin {Digital twin} cyberpunk {Cyberpunk night} watercolour {Painted} low-poly {Low-poly} voxel {Voxel blocks} pixel-art {Pixel art} other {Line drawing}}

editor.housePrompt.styleGroup.context: Heading over a group of styles, by the dashboards they suit.

editor.housePrompt.styleGroupHint.en: {group, select, light {Daylight and true colours, on light themes and e-ink.} dark {Night, glow and bright lines, on dark themes.} other {Like a game, on any dashboard.}}

editor.housePrompt.tips.context: The photo tips, as four short sentences.

editor.housePrompt.title.en: Write a prompt for your own chat

editor.housePrompt.type.context: Label of the choice of the house’s kind.

editor.houseSetting.gone.en: This tile’s house is gone. Pick another.

editor.houseSetting.navigationChoice.context: The ways to move between sides: swipe sideways with nothing on the tile, dots under the house, or tabs with the sides’ names.

editor.houseSetting.navigationHint.context: Line under the choice of how to move between sides, saying what the chosen way looks like.

editor.houseSetting.none.en: No houses for this Homey yet: make one from a picture of your home, or start from a Tiledash house.

editor.houseSetting.onHouseHint.context: Line under the "On the house" list.

editor.houseSetting.part.en: {part, select, solar {Solar} grid {Grid} home {House} battery {Battery} car {Car} other {Today’s totals}}
editor.houseSetting.part.context: An energy part pointed out on the house: the solar panels, the grid, what the house uses, the home battery, the car, or today’s totals of energy under the house.

editor.houseSetting.partWhere.en: {part, select, solar {Solar panels} grid {Grid connection} home {The house} battery {Home battery} car {Car} other {Under the house}}
editor.houseSetting.partWhere.context: Where on the house an energy part points, under its name.

params.part: solar, grid, home, battery, car or today.

editor.houseSetting.paused.context: Under a house that is paused (the account has more houses than its subscription allows) and that a tile can’t show.

editor.houseSetting.rotate.context: Label of the choice of how often the tile turns to the next side by itself.

editor.houseSetting.sides.context: How many sides (front, back, garden side: each its own picture) a house has, under its name.

params.count: How many sides.

editor.houseSetting.sidesLabel.context: Label of the list of which sides of the house the tile shows, in their order.

editor.houseSetting.valuesGroup.context: Heading over the house’s own values (a temperature upstairs, the pool) in the "On the house" list.

editor.houseSpots.addInstead.context: Button on a reading taken off a value: makes it added again.

editor.houseSpots.addReading.context: Button that adds a reading to a value, added up with the others.

editor.houseSpots.addValue.context: Button adding a value to a spot.

editor.houseSpots.decimals.context: Label of how many decimals a value shows.

editor.houseSpots.decimalsAuto.context: Choice of decimals: as many as read well.

editor.houseSpots.hint.en: Open a spot to see what it shows and place it on the picture. Every tile showing this house shows the same.

editor.houseSpots.homeHint.en: Worked out from your grid, solar, battery and car, so it needs no reading of its own.

editor.houseSpots.homeTitle.context: In the open spot "The house": the power the house uses.

editor.houseSpots.label.context: Label of a value’s label field.

editor.houseSpots.labelPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of a value’s label field.

editor.houseSpots.newValue.context: A value without a label yet.

editor.houseSpots.noHomeyTitle.context: Shown over the spots of a house that belongs to no Homey yet.

editor.houseSpots.notPlaced.context: In an open spot that isn’t placed on the side shown.

params.elsewhere: yes when it is placed on another side, else no.

editor.houseSpots.otherHomeyText.en: Switch to that Homey to change what its spots show.
editor.houseSpots.otherHomeyText.context: Under "This house belongs to another Homey".

editor.houseSpots.otherHomeyTitle.en: This house belongs to another Homey
editor.houseSpots.otherHomeyTitle.context: Shown over the spots of a house whose Homey isn’t the one open in the app now.

editor.houseSpots.partState.en: {state, select, off {Not shown} meters {From your meters} other {Chosen readings}}
editor.houseSpots.partState.context: Under an energy spot’s name (solar, grid, battery, car): left off the house, following the account’s energy meters, or readings chosen for this house.

editor.houseSpots.placeIt.context: Button in an open spot: then a tap on the picture places it.

editor.houseSpots.placedHere.en: On this side: drag its pin to move it.
editor.houseSpots.placedHere.context: In an open spot that is placed on the side shown.

editor.houseSpots.summary.context: Under a spot’s name: how many values it shows.

editor.houseSpots.todayTitle.context: The row of today’s energy totals, shown under the house.

editor.houseSpots.todayWhere.context: Where today’s totals show, under their row’s name.

editor.houseSpots.valueCount.context: How many values a spot shows of how many it may.

editor.houseSpots.valuesHere.context: Heading over a spot’s own values; "Also here" on an energy spot, whose part is shown above them.

editor.houses.addSide.context: Button that adds a side (another picture of the house).

editor.houses.defaultName.context: The name a new house starts with.

editor.houses.deleteSide.context: Menu item that deletes the side.

editor.houses.deleteTitle.context: Title of the question before deleting a house.

editor.houses.description.context: Line under the title of the houses page.

editor.houses.empty.en: No houses yet. Make one to put your own home on the Energy house.
editor.houses.empty.context: Shown on the houses page while the person has none.

editor.houses.full.en: Your plan holds {max, plural, one {# house} other {# houses}}.
editor.houses.full.context: Shown instead of making a new house when the person has as many as their plan holds.

editor.houses.getPicture.context: Heading over the ways to get this side’s picture.

editor.houses.houseName.context: Label of the house’s name field in the editor.

editor.houses.keepMine.context: Saves the house as it is here over the other changes.

editor.houses.limit.context: How many houses the person has of how many their plan holds, beside the page’s title.

editor.houses.moveEarlier.context: Menu item that moves the side one place earlier.

editor.houses.moveLater.context: Menu item that moves the side one place later.

editor.houses.newHouse.context: Button that makes a new house and opens it in the editor.

editor.houses.newSide.en: {side, select, front {Front} back {Back} left {Left side} right {Right side} other {Other…}}
editor.houses.newSide.context: Menu under “Add a side”: which side of the house to add. The first four become its name; Other adds one to name yourself (a basement, a pool side).

params.side: front, back, left, right or other.

editor.houses.noHomey.context: Choice for a house tied to none of the person’s Homeys (its tiles can be on any).

editor.houses.open.context: Button that opens a house in the editor.

editor.houses.ownCount.context: How many own spots the house has of how many it may.

params.count: How many.
params.max: How many it may have.

editor.houses.ownPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the field that adds a spot of the person’s own.

editor.houses.paused.context: Under a house that is paused: the account has more houses than its plan holds, so it shows nowhere and can’t be changed.

editor.houses.pausedText.context: Text of the note in the editor that the house is paused.

editor.houses.pausedTitle.context: Title of the note in the editor for a paused house.

editor.houses.previewTheme.context: The looks the preview can show: a dark theme, a light one, or an e-ink screen.

editor.houses.removeOwn.context: Button that deletes one of the person’s own spots from the house.

editor.houses.rename.context: Menu item that renames the side.

editor.houses.replace.context: Button that gives the side another picture.

editor.houses.reset.context: Button that makes the crop the whole picture again.

editor.houses.sideMenu.context: Accessible name of the button that opens a side’s menu.

editor.houses.sideName.context: The name a new side starts with: the first is the front, then the back, then the garden side.

editor.houses.sides.context: How many sides (each its own picture: front, back, garden side) a house has.

params.count: How many sides.

editor.houses.sidesLabel.context: Label of the row of the house’s sides in the editor.

editor.houses.spotName.en: {spot, select, solar {Solar panels} grid {Grid connection} home {The house} battery {Home battery} car {Car} charger {Charger} meter {Meter cupboard} upstairs {Upstairs} heat-pump {Heat pump} garage {Garage} other {Garden}}
editor.houses.spotName.context: The places of a house values can point at.

editor.houses.spotState.context: Whether a spot is placed on this side, on others (named), or nowhere.

editor.houses.spotsTitle.context: Heading of the list of places values can point at.

editor.houses.status.en: {status, select, saved {Saved} saving {Saving…} offline {Offline: saves when back} other {Not saved yet}}
editor.houses.status.context: What the editor’s top bar says about saving the house.

editor.houses.takeOff.context: Button that takes a spot off this side.

editor.houses.takeTheirs.context: Drops the changes here and shows the house as saved elsewhere.

editor.houses.title.context: Title of the page that lists the person’s own houses, and the editor’s way back to it.

editor.houses.tryAgain.context: Button that reads the houses again.

editor.houses.upload.context: Way to get the side’s picture: one the person made themselves.

editor.houses.uploadAnother.context: Button in the dialog of a failed upload: picks another file to upload.

editor.houses.uploadFailed.context: Title of the dialog when uploading a side’s picture failed; the dialog says why under it.

editor.houses.uploadHint.en: One you made yourself. You place its spots.

editor.houses.uploadProblem.en: {problem, select, type {Tiledash takes PNG, JPEG and WebP pictures, and this browser couldn’t turn this file into one. Save it as a PNG or JPEG and try again.} unreadable {This file couldn’t be opened as a picture. It may be damaged, or in a format this browser can’t read, such as HEIC. Save it as a PNG or JPEG and try again.} too-big {A picture can be at most {limit} MB, and this one is bigger even made smaller. Try a smaller picture.} too-large {A picture can have at most {limit} million pixels. Try a smaller picture.} limit {Your account keeps {limit} pictures at most, and it has that many. Delete one you no longer use, then try again.} space {Your pictures take all the room your account has ({limit} MB together). Delete one you no longer use, then try again.} offline {Tiledash couldn’t be reached. Check your connection and try again.} other {Something went wrong on our side while keeping it. Try again in a moment.}}
editor.houses.uploadProblem.context: Why uploading a side’s picture failed and what to do, in the dialog "The picture couldn’t be uploaded". PNG, JPEG, WebP and HEIC are file types and are not translated.

params.limit: The limit that was hit: megabytes, millions of pixels, or a number of pictures.
params.problem: type, unreadable, too-big, too-large, limit, space, offline or failed.

editor.iconPicker.categoryPeople.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of people and gestures.

editor.iconPicker.categoryShopping.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of shops, carts and commerce.

editor.iconPicker.categorySystem.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of interface and system symbols.

editor.iconPicker.categoryTechnology.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of technology, computers and code.

editor.iconPicker.categoryText.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of text editing and typography.

editor.iconPicker.categoryTravel.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of maps, places and travel.

editor.iconPicker.categoryWeather.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker under All icons: the library category of weather.

editor.iconPicker.grid.context: Screen reader label of the grid of icons, when the picker has no name of its own. A group of choices where one icon is picked. Not visible as text.

editor.iconPicker.groupDevices.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons of devices, such as a lamp or a thermostat.

editor.iconPicker.groupHomey.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of Homey’s own icons, such as a Flow or a mood. Homey is the smart-home hub: keep the name.

editor.iconPicker.groupLeisure.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons for free-time things, such as a pool, music or a hot tub.

editor.iconPicker.groupOutdoor.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons for things outside the house, such as the garden or a gate.

editor.iconPicker.groupPeople.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons for people and family members.

editor.iconPicker.groupReadings.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons for readings and states of a device, such as power, battery or motion.

editor.iconPicker.groupRooms.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons for rooms of a home, such as a kitchen or a bedroom.

editor.iconPicker.groupSymbols.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of general symbols, such as a star, an arrow or a check mark.

editor.iconPicker.groupWeather.context: Chip (small round button) in the icon picker: the group of icons for weather, such as sun, rain and wind.

editor.iconPicker.groups.context: Screen reader label of the row of chips (small round buttons) that picks which group of icons the grid shows: Devices, Rooms, Weather and so on. Not visible as text.

editor.iconPicker.loadFailed.context: Message in the icon grid when the full icon library could not be loaded (a network problem). A "Try again" button follows it.

editor.iconPicker.morePhosphor.context: Small divider line inside the icon grid while searching, between the icons Tiledash offers by name and the other icons of the Phosphor library that match. Phosphor is the name of the icon library: keep it.

editor.iconPicker.noMatch.en: No icons match “{query}”. Try one word, like pool, music or dog.
editor.iconPicker.noMatch.context: Message in the icon grid when the search finds nothing. The icon search only knows English icon names, so keep the three example words "pool", "music" and "dog" in English.

params.query: What the person typed in the search box. Not translated.

editor.iconPicker.searchIcons.context: Screen reader label of the search box above the icon grid, when the picker has no name. Not visible as text.

editor.iconPicker.searchNamed.context: Screen reader label of the search box above the icon grid, when the picker has a name, such as "Search icon" or "Search heading icon". Not visible as text.

params.label: What the picker is for, lowercased, such as "icon". Already translated.

editor.iconPicker.searchPlaceholder.context: Placeholder in the search box above the icon grid. The two example words are search words: the icon search only knows English icon names, so keep "pool" and "music" in English.

editor.iconPicker.showMore.context: Button at the end of the icon grid that shows more icons. The grid shows a page of icons at a time.

params.count: How many more icons it shows, such as 120. A number.

editor.itemStyling.copied.context: Title of the message (toast) after the style of a tile was copied, from the tile’s menu or the style panel.

editor.itemStyling.copiedHint.en: Paste it on other tiles from their menu.
editor.itemStyling.copiedHint.context: Text under the message "Style copied": how to use the copied style, with the paste item in the menu of another tile.

editor.itemStyling.pasted.en: {count, plural, one {Style pasted} other {Style pasted on # tiles}}
editor.itemStyling.pasted.context: Title of the green message (toast) after a copied style was pasted on one or more tiles.

params.count: How many tiles the style was pasted on, at least 1.

editor.layoutBlocks.deviceGoneLine.context: Small grey line under the name of a picture placed on a tile when it is one of a device’s own pictures but that device can no longer be found: which kind of picture and where on the tile it sits.

params.image: The kind of picture, such as "Album art", "Snapshot" or "Photo". Already translated.
params.where: The name of the spot on the tile, such as "Top right" or "Centre". Already translated.

editor.layoutBlocks.deviceLine.context: Small grey line under the name of a picture placed on a tile when it is one of a device’s own pictures: which picture, of which device, and where on the tile it sits. For example "Album art of Kitchen speaker · Top right".

params.device: The name of the device. Not translated.
params.image: The kind of picture, such as "Album art", "Snapshot" or "Photo". Already translated.
params.where: The name of the spot on the tile, such as "Top right" or "Centre". Already translated.

editor.layoutBlocks.iconLine.context: Small grey line under the name of a picture placed on a tile when it is an icon of the library: what it is and where on the tile it sits.

params.where: The name of the spot on the tile, such as "Top right" or "Centre". Already translated.

editor.layoutBlocks.picture.context: Kind of picture shown in the small grey line of a placed device picture when its kind can no longer be found. It stands for "Picture of …".

editor.layoutBlocks.sectionEmpty.context: Small grey line under the name of a folded section of a tile that holds no values yet. A section is a part of a tile that folds open and closed under a heading.

editor.layoutBlocks.sectionValues.en: Section · {count, plural, one {# value} other {# values}}
editor.layoutBlocks.sectionValues.context: Small grey line under the name of a folded section of a tile: what it is and how many values are in it. A section is a part of a tile that folds open and closed under a heading. A value is one of the readings or texts shown on the tile.

params.count: How many values the section holds. A number, at least 1.

editor.layoutBlocks.tabEmpty.context: Small grey line under the name of a folded tab of a tile that holds no values yet. A tab is one of several panes of a tile that the person switches between.

editor.layoutBlocks.tabValues.en: Tab · {count, plural, one {# value} other {# values}}
editor.layoutBlocks.tabValues.context: Small grey line under the name of a folded tab of a tile: what it is and how many values are in it. A tab is one of several panes of a tile that the person switches between. A value is one of the readings or texts shown on the tile.

params.count: How many values the tab holds. A number, at least 1.

editor.layoutBlocks.tooBig.en: Pictures can be at most 10 MB.
editor.layoutBlocks.tooBig.context: Red line under the Upload button when the chosen picture is larger than 10 megabytes (MB).

editor.layoutBlocks.uploadLine.context: Small grey line under the name of a picture placed on a tile when it is a picture the person uploaded: the picture’s name and where on the tile it sits.

params.name: The name of the uploaded picture, as the person named it, or "Uploaded picture" when it is gone. Not translated further.
params.where: The name of the spot on the tile, such as "Top right" or "Centre". Already translated.

editor.layoutBlocks.uploadedPicture.context: Name shown for an uploaded picture placed on a tile when the picture itself can no longer be found, for example after it was deleted.

editor.layoutBlocks.wrongType.en: Pictures can be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
editor.layoutBlocks.wrongType.context: Red line under the Upload button when the chosen file is not a picture format that can be used. PNG, JPEG and WebP are file types and are not translated.

editor.layoutEditor.addPicture.context: Button with a plus icon that adds a picture or an icon to the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.addSection.context: Button with a plus icon that adds a section (values that fold open and closed under a heading) to the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.addTab.context: Button with a plus icon that adds a tab (a pane of the tile that is switched to) to the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.lookDots.context: Choice of the segmented control "Tabs look": the tabs show as small dots with no names, like the pages of a photo gallery.

editor.layoutEditor.lookPill.context: Choice of the segmented control "Tabs look": each tab is a rounded pill, the chosen one filled. Describes the shape.

editor.layoutEditor.lookUnderline.context: Choice of the segmented control "Tabs look": the chosen tab has a line under its name.

editor.layoutEditor.moveDown.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a section or tab one step down in the list.

editor.layoutEditor.moveUp.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a section or tab one step up in the list.

editor.layoutEditor.newSection.context: The name a new section of a tile gets when the person adds one, before they type another. It is saved as the section’s name and shown as its heading on the tile. One short word.

editor.layoutEditor.newTab.context: The name a new tab of a tile gets when the person adds one, before they type another: the first is "Tab 1", the next "Tab 2". It is saved as the tab’s name and shown on the tile.

params.number: The number of the tab, counting from 1. A number.

editor.layoutEditor.pictureDevice.context: Name of a placed picture in the list when it is one of a device’s own pictures, such as a speaker’s album art or a camera’s snapshot.

editor.layoutEditor.pictureIcon.context: Name of a placed picture in the list when it is an icon of the library (not a photo).

editor.layoutEditor.pictureUpload.context: Name of a placed picture in the list when it is a picture the person uploaded themselves.

editor.layoutEditor.picturesHint.en: Put an icon, a device’s own picture or one of yours anywhere on the tile, in front of the values or behind them.
editor.layoutEditor.picturesHint.context: Small help text under the heading "Pictures and icons". "One of yours" is a picture the person uploaded. A value is one of the readings or texts shown on the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.picturesTitle.context: Heading of the second part of the Layout tab, above the pictures and icons placed on the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.remove.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the small trash button at the end of a row (a section, tab, picture or icon): it removes that row from the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.secondTab.en: Add a second tab to switch between them.
editor.layoutEditor.secondTab.context: Small note with an info icon, shown while the tile has only one tab: a single tab has nothing to switch to, so a second one is needed. "Them" are the tabs.

editor.layoutEditor.sectionsHint.en: Fold some values away under a heading, or split them over tabs to tap or swipe between.
editor.layoutEditor.sectionsHint.context: Small help text under the heading "Sections and tabs": what a section (values that fold away under a heading) and a tab (values split over panes) are for. A value is one of the readings or texts shown on the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.sectionsTitle.context: Heading of the first part of the Layout tab, above the sections and tabs of the tile.

editor.layoutEditor.tabBar.context: Label of a choice between Top and Bottom: where the bar with the tabs sits on the tile. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutEditor.tabsAtBottom.context: Choice of the segmented control "Tab bar": the tabs of a tile sit in a bar along its bottom edge.

editor.layoutEditor.tabsAtTop.context: Choice of the segmented control "Tab bar": the tabs of a tile sit in a bar along its top edge.

editor.layoutEditor.tabsLook.context: Label of a choice between Pill, Underline and Dots: how the tabs of a tile look. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutGroup.addIcon.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the small round button with a plus, shown while a section or tab has no icon yet. It opens the icon picker.

editor.layoutGroup.changeIcon.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the small round button that shows the icon of a section or tab and opens the icon picker.

editor.layoutGroup.icon.context: Label above the small button that picks an icon for a section or tab. Also the screen reader label of the icon picker in its popover.

editor.layoutGroup.name.context: Label of the text field for the name of a section or tab, which the tile shows as its heading or tab name.

editor.layoutGroup.noIcon.context: Small button in the icon picker popover that takes the icon of a section or tab away again.

editor.layoutGroup.noValues.en: Add values on the {tab} tab first.
editor.layoutGroup.noValues.context: Small help text shown instead of the value chips when the tile has no values at all yet: they are made on the first tab of the tile’s settings, which is called Content.

params.tab: The name of the first tab of the tile’s settings, already translated (English: "Content"). It must be the same word as that tab’s label.

editor.layoutGroup.onePlace.en: A value sits in one place: picking it here takes it out of another.
editor.layoutGroup.onePlace.context: Second sentence of the help text under the value chips: a value can be in only one section or tab, so ticking it here removes it from the one it was in.

editor.layoutGroup.placedIn.context: Small text at the end of a value chip that is not ticked here because it already sits in another section or tab: it says which one. For example "in Details". Lower case.

params.name: The name of the other section or tab, as the person named it. Not translated.

editor.layoutGroup.remembers.en: Each screen remembers whether it is open.
editor.layoutGroup.remembers.context: Small help text under a section’s settings: a screen (a phone, a wall panel) keeps its own open or closed state of the section.

editor.layoutGroup.sectionExplain.en: These fold away under the heading.
editor.layoutGroup.sectionExplain.context: First sentence of the help text under the value chips of a section: the ticked values fold away under the section’s heading. Followed by the sentence about a value sitting in one place.

editor.layoutGroup.sectionPlaceholder.context: Example shown faintly in the empty name field of a section, to suggest what the name could be. One short word.

editor.layoutGroup.showsWhileClosed.context: Label of a dropdown: which of the section’s values the folded section shows next to its name. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutGroup.startClosed.context: Choice of the segmented control "Starts" for a section: the section is folded shut when the dashboard opens.

editor.layoutGroup.startOpen.context: Choice of the segmented control "Starts" for a section: the section is unfolded when the dashboard opens.

editor.layoutGroup.starts.context: Label of a choice between Closed and Open: how a section starts when the dashboard opens. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutGroup.summaryNothing.context: Choice in the dropdown "Shows while closed": the folded section shows only its name, no value.

editor.layoutGroup.tabExplain.en: These show while this tab is chosen; the rest of the tile stays.
editor.layoutGroup.tabExplain.context: First sentence of the help text under the value chips of a tab: the ticked values show only while this tab is the chosen one, and everything else on the tile stays visible. Followed by the sentence about a value sitting in one place.

editor.layoutGroup.tabPlaceholder.context: Example shown faintly in the empty name field of a tab, to suggest what the name could be, such as a tab for the readings of today. One short word.

editor.layoutGroup.valuesIn.context: Label above the chips of the tile’s values: the person ticks the ones that belong in this section or tab.

editor.layoutGroup.valuesInSection.context: Screen reader label of the group of value chips of a section, which the person ticks to put values in it.

editor.layoutGroup.valuesOnTab.context: Screen reader label of the group of value chips of a tab, which the person ticks to put values on it.

editor.layoutPicture.changeIcon.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the round button that shows the placed icon and opens the icon picker.

editor.layoutPicture.chooseDevice.context: Placeholder of the dropdown that picks the device whose own picture is placed, shown while none is chosen.

editor.layoutPicture.colour.context: Screen reader label of the colour swatches that colour a placed icon.

editor.layoutPicture.delete.context: Red button that really deletes the uploaded picture from the account. Answers the question "Delete … from your pictures?".

editor.layoutPicture.deleteConfirm.en: Delete {name} from your pictures? Tiles showing it show an icon instead.
editor.layoutPicture.deleteConfirm.context: Question shown after the person starts deleting an uploaded picture from their account, before it happens. Answered with the buttons Delete and Keep. Tiles that use the picture show an icon after it is deleted.

params.name: The name of the uploaded picture, as the person named it. Not translated.

editor.layoutPicture.deleteFailed.en: The picture could not be deleted.
editor.layoutPicture.deleteFailed.context: Red line shown when deleting an uploaded picture from the account failed and the server gave no reason of its own.

editor.layoutPicture.deletePicture.context: Small button that starts deleting the chosen uploaded picture from the account. The dots mean the person is asked to confirm first.

editor.layoutPicture.describeIt.context: Label of a text field where the person describes a picture in words, for people who use a screen reader.

editor.layoutPicture.describePlaceholder.en: For screen readers, e.g. “The car on the drive”
editor.layoutPicture.describePlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the text field "Describe it": what it is for, with an example description of a picture (a car parked on a drive) in quotes.

editor.layoutPicture.device.context: Label of the dropdown that picks the device whose own picture is placed. Also its screen reader label.
