editor.layoutPicture.devicePicturesHint.en: Pictures the Homey keeps for a device, like a speaker’s album art or a camera’s snapshot. They follow the device: new album art shows by itself.
editor.layoutPicture.devicePicturesHint.context: Small help text under the choice of a device picture: what these pictures are, and that the tile always shows the newest one.

editor.layoutPicture.fit.context: Label of a choice between Whole and Fill: how the picture fits its box. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutPicture.fitFill.context: Choice of the segmented control "Fit": the picture fills its box completely and its edges may be cut off.

editor.layoutPicture.fitWhole.context: Choice of the segmented control "Fit": the whole picture is shown, with empty space at its edges if its shape differs from the box.

editor.layoutPicture.icon.context: Screen reader label of the icon picker in the popover of a placed icon.

editor.layoutPicture.iconAndColour.context: Label above the icon button and the colour swatches of a placed icon.

editor.layoutPicture.keep.context: Button that keeps the uploaded picture after all, answering the question "Delete … from your pictures?".

editor.layoutPicture.layer.context: Label of a choice between In front and Behind: whether the picture is drawn over or under the tile’s values. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutPicture.layerBehind.context: Choice of the segmented control "Layer": the picture is drawn under the tile’s values. Also named in a help text under the controls, which uses the same word.

editor.layoutPicture.layerFront.context: Choice of the segmented control "Layer": the picture is drawn over the tile’s values. Also named in a help text under the controls, which uses the same word.

editor.layoutPicture.layerHint.en: Behind, it sits under the values and takes no taps; in front, a tap on it does what tapping the tile does.
editor.layoutPicture.layerHint.context: Small help text under the picture’s position, size and layer settings. "Behind" and "in front" are the two choices of the Layer control and must use the same words as them, the first starts the sentence, the second is in lower case in the middle of it.

editor.layoutPicture.noDevicePictures.en: None of this Homey’s devices has a picture of its own. Upload one instead.
editor.layoutPicture.noDevicePictures.context: Small help text shown when no device of the Homey keeps pictures. "Upload one instead" points at the choice named Upload in the control "Shows", where a picture is uploaded by hand.

editor.layoutPicture.picture.context: Label above the pictures to choose from, a device’s own pictures or the uploaded ones. Also the screen reader label of the device’s pictures.

editor.layoutPicture.position.context: Label of the small nine-spot picker that says where on the tile the picture sits. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutPicture.shows.context: Screen reader label of the segmented control with Icon, Device picture and Upload: what the placed picture shows. Not visible as text.

editor.layoutPicture.size.context: Label of the slider that sets how big the picture is on the tile. Also its screen reader label.

editor.layoutPicture.sizeValue.context: Reading beside the size slider: how much of the tile’s width the picture takes, such as "40% wide".

params.value: The size as a whole number from 8 to 100. A number.

editor.layoutPicture.sourceDevice.context: Choice of the segmented control "Shows": the placed picture is one of a device’s own pictures, such as a speaker’s album art or a camera’s snapshot.

editor.layoutPicture.sourceIcon.context: Choice of the segmented control "Shows": the placed picture is an icon of the library.

editor.layoutPicture.sourceUpload.context: Choice of the segmented control "Shows": the placed picture is one the person uploaded themselves. A noun here, not a verb.

editor.layoutPicture.upload.context: Label of the small tile with an upload icon at the end of the uploaded pictures: it opens the file chooser to add a picture. A verb here.

editor.layoutPicture.uploadFailed.en: The picture could not be uploaded.
editor.layoutPicture.uploadFailed.context: Red line shown when uploading a picture failed and the server gave no reason of its own.

editor.layoutPicture.uploadHint.en: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 10 MB. Kept with your account and only shown on your own dashboards.
editor.layoutPicture.uploadHint.context: Small help text under the uploaded pictures: which file types can be uploaded, the size limit, and that the pictures are private to the person’s account. PNG, JPEG and WebP are file types and are not translated; MB is megabytes.

editor.layoutPicture.uploadedPictures.context: Screen reader label of the group of the pictures the person uploaded, from which one is chosen. Not visible as text.

editor.layoutPicture.uploading.context: Label of the small upload tile while a picture is being sent to the account. The dots mean it is in progress.

editor.layoutPictureSources.albumArt.context: Name of the picture a media device, such as a speaker, keeps of the music that is playing: the cover of the album. Shown as a label under a small thumbnail.

editor.layoutPictureSources.photo.context: Name of the picture a device, such as a car, keeps of itself. Shown as a label under a small thumbnail.

editor.layoutPictureSources.picture.context: Name of a device picture whose own name is empty. Shown as a label under a small thumbnail.

editor.layoutPictureSources.snapshot.context: Name of the picture a camera keeps of what it sees now. Shown as a label under a small thumbnail.

editor.mapExample.car.context: Made-up name of the example car on the example map. A person would name their car like this in their Homey.

editor.mapExample.phone.context: Made-up name of the example phone on the example map. A person would name their phone like this in their Homey.

editor.mapExample.title.context: Title of the example Map tile in the add-widgets window preview: a map with the places of a few devices.

editor.mapPinPicker.failed.en: The map can’t load here; search for the place instead.
editor.mapPinPicker.failed.context: Orange text under the small map when the map could not be loaded (no connection, or blocked). It points to the other way of choosing a place: searching by name.

editor.mapPinPicker.hint.en: Tap the map to drop the pin.
editor.mapPinPicker.hint.context: Small grey help text under the small map: tapping or clicking the map puts the pin at that spot.

editor.modelSetting.add.context: Link beside My models that opens the page where the person adds a 3D model.

editor.modelSetting.change.context: Link on the chosen model that opens the list to pick another.

editor.modelSetting.community.context: Heading of the 3D models the person installed from the Community (the app’s shared library of things people made).

editor.modelSetting.communityEmpty.en: Models you install from the Community show here.
editor.modelSetting.communityEmpty.context: Under From the Community while the person installed none.

editor.modelSetting.done.context: Link on the chosen model that closes the list of models again.

editor.modelSetting.front.context: Button on the 3D view stage: turn the model to be seen from the front.

editor.modelSetting.gone.context: Under the chosen model when it was deleted, uninstalled or blocked since, so the tile can’t show it.

editor.modelSetting.how.en: Drag to turn it any way, even upside down. Shift-drag or twist with two fingers to roll it; scroll or pinch to zoom. The arrow keys turn it too.
editor.modelSetting.how.context: Help under the 3D view stage, on how to turn the model.

editor.modelSetting.isometric.context: Button on the 3D view stage: turn the model to the isometric view (from the front left, a little above), the one a new tile starts at.

editor.modelSetting.kit.context: Heading of the models that come with the app (furniture and devices). Tiledash is the product name.

editor.modelSetting.mine.context: Heading of the person’s own 3D models in the list.

editor.modelSetting.noModel.context: On the 3D view stage while the tile has no model to turn.

editor.modelSetting.nothing.context: Under the search field when no model’s name has what was typed.

editor.modelSetting.pick.context: The model setting’s button while no model is chosen yet.

editor.modelSetting.reset.context: Button on the 3D view stage: back to the isometric view at normal size.

editor.modelSetting.search.context: Placeholder of the search field above the list of models.

editor.modelSetting.top.context: Button on the 3D view stage: turn the model to be seen from right above.

editor.openModes.dashboardPage.context: Choice in the "Open as" dropdown that appears once a tap opens another dashboard: the dashboard replaces the current page, as a normal visit would. The other choices are popup, side panel and full screen.

editor.openModes.devicePage.context: Choice in the "Open as" dropdown of a tap that opens a device: it goes to the Devices page of the app, where the device is shown, instead of opening over the dashboard. "Devices" is the name of that page.

editor.openModes.full.context: Choice in the "Open as" dropdown of a tap that opens a dashboard: it covers the whole screen until it is closed.

editor.openModes.popup.context: Choice in the "Open as" dropdown of a tap that opens a dashboard or a device: it opens in a window over the current page.

editor.openModes.side.context: Choice in the "Open as" dropdown of a tap that opens a dashboard or a device: it slides in from the side of the screen, over the current page.

editor.orderedPick.add.en: Add {noun, select, device {a device} flow {a flow} mood {a mood} dashboard {a dashboard} other {one}}
editor.orderedPick.add.context: Label of the button that opens the search over what can be added to the list. It names what the list holds: device, Flow (an automation of the Homey), mood (a scene) or dashboard. A command.

params.noun: What the list holds: device, flow, mood or dashboard. A code, not translated; the message has a branch for each.

editor.orderedPick.allPicked.en: Every {noun, select, device {device} flow {flow} mood {mood} dashboard {dashboard} other {item}} that fits is picked.
editor.orderedPick.allPicked.context: Line in the list of what can still be added, when everything that fits is already picked. It names what the list holds: device, Flow (an automation of the Homey), mood (a scene) or dashboard.

params.noun: What the list holds: device, flow, mood or dashboard. A code, not translated; the message has a branch for each.

editor.orderedPick.atLeast.context: Part of the small count line next to the Add button: the least the list must hold, such as "at least 2". Only shown when it is more than one. Lowercase, as it follows a middle dot.

params.min: The least the list must hold. A number.

editor.orderedPick.atMost.context: Part of the small count line next to the Add button: the most the list can hold, such as "at most 8". Lowercase, as it follows a middle dot.

params.max: The most the list can hold. A number.

editor.orderedPick.atMostFull.context: Label of the disabled Add button when the list is full: the most it can hold is reached, for example "At most 8".

params.max: The most the list can hold. A number.

editor.orderedPick.count.en: {noun, select, device {{count, plural, one {# device} other {# devices}}} flow {{count, plural, one {# flow} other {# flows}}} mood {{count, plural, one {# mood} other {# moods}}} dashboard {{count, plural, one {# dashboard} other {# dashboards}}} other {{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}}}
editor.orderedPick.count.context: First part of the small count line next to the Add button: how many are picked, such as "3 devices". More parts follow after a middle dot, such as "at least 2" and "at most 8". It names what the list holds: device, Flow (an automation of the Homey), mood (a scene) or dashboard.

params.count: How many are picked. A number.
params.noun: What the list holds: device, flow, mood or dashboard. A code, not translated; the message has a branch for each.

editor.orderedPick.doneAdding.context: Small button under the search list that closes it again, after one or more were added. A command.

editor.orderedPick.moveDown.context: Screen reader label of a small icon button (an arrow down) on a row of the picked list: it moves that row one place down. Not visible as text.

params.name: The name of the picked device, flow, mood or dashboard. Not translated.

editor.orderedPick.moveUp.context: Screen reader label of a small icon button (an arrow up) on a row of the picked list: it moves that row one place up. Not visible as text.

params.name: The name of the picked device, flow, mood or dashboard. Not translated.

editor.orderedPick.noMatch.context: Line in the list of what can still be added when the search finds nothing.

editor.orderedPick.noneYet.en: {noun, select, device {No devices picked yet.} flow {No flows picked yet.} mood {No moods picked yet.} dashboard {No dashboards picked yet.} other {Nothing picked yet.}}
editor.orderedPick.noneYet.context: Text shown instead of the picked list while nothing is picked. It names what the list holds: devices, Flows (automations of the Homey), moods (scenes) or dashboards.

params.noun: What the list holds: device, flow, mood or dashboard. A code, not translated; the message has a branch for each.

editor.orderedPick.remove.context: Screen reader label of a small icon button (a cross) on a row of the picked list: it takes that row out of the list. Not visible as text.

params.name: The name of the picked device, flow, mood or dashboard. Not translated.

editor.orderedPick.removedName.context: Name shown on a row of the picked list in place of a device, flow, mood or dashboard that no longer exists on the Homey (the smart-home hub). Under it a reason is shown. A status, not a command.

editor.orderedPick.removedReason.context: Reason shown in small warning text under a row of the picked list that no longer exists on the Homey (the smart-home hub).

editor.orderedPick.searchPlaceholder.en: Search {noun, select, device {devices} flow {flows} mood {moods} dashboard {dashboards} other {items}}
editor.orderedPick.searchPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the search box that opens after "Add", over the devices, flows, moods or dashboards that are not picked yet.

params.noun: What the list holds: device, flow, mood or dashboard. A code, not translated; the message has a branch for each.

editor.ownSettings.andMore.context: Last sentence of the text on a tile that cannot be drawn because settings have not been chosen: how many other settings still need a choice besides the one named in the title.

params.count: How many other settings need a choice. A number, at least one.

editor.ownSettings.chartNote.en: Energy and prices chart as their own bars, {time}: no chart type, range or detail to choose.
editor.ownSettings.chartNote.context: Small note with an info icon on the Chart tab of a tile that charts energy and prices. They draw as their own bars for a set time, so the choices of chart type, range and detail are left out.

params.time: What the bars cover, such as "per hour for today". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.chooseAgain.context: Title shown on a tile that cannot be drawn because the device, flow or mood that was chosen is gone or no longer fits, such as "Choose the charger again". The tile also says why below it.

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.chooseAnother.context: Short sentence added after a warning under a required setting whose chosen device, flow or mood is gone or no longer fits: the person must choose a different one.

editor.ownSettings.chooseAnotherOrEmpty.en: Choose another, or leave it empty.
editor.ownSettings.chooseAnotherOrEmpty.context: Short sentence added after a warning under an optional setting whose chosen device, flow or mood is gone or no longer fits: the person can choose a different one or leave the setting empty.

editor.ownSettings.chooseDeviceFirst.context: Small grey line in place of a dropdown of readings when the device that the readings belong to has not been chosen yet. "Its" refers to the setting’s device, chosen in another field above.

editor.ownSettings.chooseMore.context: Title shown on a tile that cannot be drawn because fewer are chosen than it needs, such as "Choose more smoke detectors". The tile also says why below it.

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, in the plural, such as "smoke detectors". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.chooseNeeded.context: Title shown on a tile that cannot be drawn yet because a required setting has not been chosen, such as "Choose a charger" or "Choose smoke detectors". The tile also says why below it.

params.kind: "many" for a setting that holds several things (a list), else "one".
params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.chooseReading.context: Grey text in an empty dropdown that picks one reading (capability) of a device, such as its temperature or whether it is on.

editor.ownSettings.fitCount.en: {count, plural, one {One device fits.} other {# devices fit.}}
editor.ownSettings.fitCount.context: Small grey line under a device dropdown saying how many devices of the Homey fit what the widget needs. A sentence about what is needed follows it, such as "Needs a socket.".

params.count: How many devices fit. A number, at least one.

editor.ownSettings.goneChosen.en: The {noun} chosen before is no longer on this Homey.
editor.ownSettings.goneChosen.context: Warning under a setting (in amber) when the device, flow or mood that was chosen before no longer exists on the Homey. "Chosen before" means picked earlier. A short sentence follows: "Choose another."

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.goneShowed.en: The {noun} it showed is no longer on this Homey.
editor.ownSettings.goneShowed.context: Text on a tile that cannot be drawn because the device, flow or mood it showed is no longer on the Homey. "It" is the tile.

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.iconChange.context: Screen reader label of the button that opens the icon picker for an icon setting, not visible as text. It names the setting and says the button changes it, such as "Icon: change".

params.label: The name of the setting, such as "Icon". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.iconChangeButton.context: Text on the button of an icon setting that already has an icon chosen: it opens the icon picker to choose another.

editor.ownSettings.iconPickButton.context: Text on the button of an icon setting that has no icon chosen yet: it opens the icon picker.

editor.ownSettings.keptInZone.context: Small grey line under a device setting that is kept to a room (zone) setting: the devices listed are those in the chosen room.

params.zone: The name of the room (zone), such as "Garage". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.keptInZoneNested.en: In {zone} and the rooms inside it.
editor.ownSettings.keptInZoneNested.context: Small grey line under a device setting that is kept to a zone and the rooms inside it: the devices listed are those in the chosen zone, such as a floor, and in all the rooms in it.

params.zone: The name of the zone, such as "Ground floor". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.leftEmpty.context: Small grey text beside the choice "None" in a dropdown of an optional setting: the setting stays empty.

editor.ownSettings.less.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the − button of a number stepper in the settings of a tile. It makes the number smaller. The label says what the number is for, such as "Less Brightness".

params.label: The name of the setting, such as "Brightness". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.listFew.en: The tile needs at least {min, number} {noun}; {count, plural, one {# is} other {# are}} chosen now.
editor.ownSettings.listFew.context: Warning under a list setting (a setting that holds several devices, flows or moods) when fewer are chosen than the tile needs. For example "The tile needs at least 3 smoke detectors; 1 is chosen now."

params.count: How many are chosen now. A number.
params.min: The smallest number the tile needs. A number.
params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, in the plural, such as "smoke detectors". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.listGone.en: None of the {noun} chosen before are on this Homey any more. Choose others.
editor.ownSettings.listGone.context: Warning under a list setting (a setting that holds several devices, flows or moods) when none of the ones chosen earlier exist on the Homey any more. For example "None of the smoke detectors chosen before are on this Homey any more. Choose others."

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, in the plural, such as "smoke detectors". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.listMismatch.en: None of the {noun} chosen before fit any more. Choose others.
editor.ownSettings.listMismatch.context: Warning under a list setting (a setting that holds several devices) when the ones chosen earlier still exist but none fits what the widget needs any more. For example "None of the smoke detectors chosen before fit any more. Choose others."

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, in the plural, such as "smoke detectors". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.listPartly.en: {lost, plural, one {# of the {noun} chosen before is no longer on this Homey or no longer fits; the tile shows the other {kept, number}. Remove it below.} other {# of the {noun} chosen before are no longer on this Homey or no longer fit; the tile shows the other {kept, number}. Remove them below.}}
editor.ownSettings.listPartly.context: Warning under a list setting (a setting that holds several devices, flows or moods) when some of the ones chosen earlier are gone or no longer fit, but others still work. For example "2 of the smoke detectors chosen before are no longer on this Homey or no longer fit; the tile shows the other 3. Remove them below." The list with the faulty ones is below it.

params.kept: How many chosen ones still work, which the tile shows. A number.
params.lost: How many of the chosen ones are gone or no longer fit. A number, at least one.
params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, in the plural, such as "smoke detectors". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.mismatchClass.context: Warning under a device setting when the chosen device changed to another kind of device than the widget needs, such as "Garage socket is no longer a light.". The device was chosen earlier and has changed since.

params.deviceKind: The kind of device the widget needs, in lower case, such as "light". Already translated where possible.
params.name: The name of the device, such as "Garage socket". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.mismatchKind.en: {name} is no longer the right kind.
editor.ownSettings.mismatchKind.context: Warning under a device setting when the chosen device no longer fits what the widget needs and nothing more specific is known: it is not the right kind of device any more. The device was chosen earlier and has changed since.

params.name: The name of the device, such as "Garage socket". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.mismatchLacks.context: Warning under a device setting when the chosen device lost an ability the widget needs, such as "Garage socket no longer has Charging.". The device was chosen earlier and has changed since.

params.capabilities: What the device lost, as a list in the language’s style, such as "Charging and Power". Already translated where possible.
params.name: The name of the device, such as "Garage socket". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.mismatchNone.context: Warning under a device setting when the chosen device has none of the abilities the widget needs one of, such as "Garage socket has none of On/Off or Dim any more.". The device was chosen earlier and has changed since.

params.capabilities: What the widget needs one of, as a list in the language’s style, such as "On/Off or Dim". Already translated where possible.
params.name: The name of the device, such as "Garage socket". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.more.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the + button of a number stepper in the settings of a tile. It makes the number larger. The label says what the number is for, such as "More Brightness".

params.label: The name of the setting, such as "Brightness". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.needsAllAny.en: Needs {subject, select, class {a {classes}} other {a device}} with {all} and {any}.
editor.ownSettings.needsAllAny.context: Small grey line under a device setting that says what the widget needs: a kind of device that has certain abilities and at least one of several others, such as "Needs a device with On/Off and Dim or Temperature.".

params.all: The abilities it must have, as a list in the language’s style, such as "On/Off and Dim". Already translated where possible.
params.any: The abilities of which at least one must be there, as a list in the language’s style, such as "Temperature or Humidity". Already translated where possible.
params.classes: The kinds of device it takes, in lower case, as a list in the language’s style, such as "light or socket". Already translated where possible.
params.subject: "class" when the widget needs a kind of device (the list in "classes"), else "device".

editor.ownSettings.needsAny.en: Needs {subject, select, class {a {classes}} other {a device}} with {any}.
editor.ownSettings.needsAny.context: Small grey line under a device setting that says what the widget needs: a kind of device that has at least one of several abilities, such as "Needs a device with Temperature or Humidity.".

params.any: The abilities, of which at least one must be there, as a list in the language’s style, such as "Temperature or Humidity". Already translated where possible.
params.classes: The kinds of device it takes, in lower case, as a list in the language’s style, such as "light or socket". Already translated where possible.
params.subject: "class" when the widget needs a kind of device (the list in "classes"), else "device".

editor.ownSettings.needsDevice.context: Small grey line under an empty or filled device setting that says what kind of device the widget needs, such as "Needs a socket." or "Needs a device." (any device).

params.classes: The kinds of device it takes, in lower case, as a list in the language’s style, such as "light or socket". Already translated where possible.
params.subject: "class" when the widget needs a kind of device (the list in "classes"), else "device".

editor.ownSettings.needsOne.en: This widget needs one: pick it in the tile’s settings.
editor.ownSettings.needsOne.context: Second part of the text on a tile that cannot be drawn because a required setting has not been chosen. "One" is a single thing, such as a device. It points to the settings of the tile.

editor.ownSettings.needsThem.en: This widget needs them: pick them in the tile’s settings.
editor.ownSettings.needsThem.context: Second part of the text on a tile that cannot be drawn because a required setting that holds several things (such as readings) has not been chosen. "Them" are those things. It points to the settings of the tile.

editor.ownSettings.needsWith.en: Needs {subject, select, class {a {classes}} other {a device}} with {all}.
editor.ownSettings.needsWith.context: Small grey line under a device setting that says what the widget needs: a kind of device that has certain abilities, such as "Needs a device with On/Off and Dim.". An ability is a capability of the device (a thing it can do or measure).

params.all: The abilities it must have, as a list in the language’s style, such as "On/Off and Dim". Already translated where possible.
params.classes: The kinds of device it takes, in lower case, as a list in the language’s style, such as "light or socket". Already translated where possible.
params.subject: "class" when the widget needs a kind of device (the list in "classes"), else "device".

editor.ownSettings.none.context: Choice in a dropdown of an optional setting that leaves it empty: no device, flow, mood or dashboard is chosen. A small grey text "Left empty" is shown beside it.

editor.ownSettings.noneFit.context: Bold line in the field of a device setting when no device of the Homey fits what the widget needs, such as "No charger on this Homey". A sentence about what is needed follows it, and a full stop is added to the line when it is used in another message.

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.noneFitInZone.context: Bold line in the field of a device setting that is kept to a room (zone) setting, when no device in that room fits what the widget needs, such as "No charger in Garage".

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.
params.zone: The name of the room (zone), such as "Garage". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.noneFitInZoneNested.en: No {noun} in {zone} and the rooms inside it
editor.ownSettings.noneFitInZoneNested.context: Bold line in the field of a device setting that is kept to a room (zone) and the rooms inside it, when no device there fits what the widget needs, such as "No charger in Ground floor and the rooms inside it".

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.
params.zone: The name of the room or zone, such as "Ground floor". Not translated.

editor.ownSettings.optional.context: Small label in the top right of a setting of a tile that may be left empty, such as a device that is not needed.

editor.ownSettings.peopleUnknown.en: Tiledash may not see who lives in your home yet. Log in again and allow it.
editor.ownSettings.peopleUnknown.context: Warning under a person setting when Tiledash cannot read the people of the home from the Homey. The person has to log in again and give Tiledash the permission to see them.

editor.ownSettings.personAsleep.context: Small grey word next to a person in a list of the people of the home: the person is asleep now.

editor.ownSettings.personAway.context: Small grey word next to a person in a list of the people of the home: the person is not at home now.

editor.ownSettings.personHome.context: Small grey word next to a person in a list of the people of the home: the person is at home now. A status, not a place to go to.

editor.ownSettings.placeholderAgain.context: Grey text in a dropdown of a setting whose chosen device, flow or mood is gone or no longer fits: it asks to choose a different one.

editor.ownSettings.placeholderChoose.context: Grey text in an empty dropdown of a setting, such as "Choose a charger" or "Choose a flow".

params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.ownSettings.sizeLarge.context: Last of three options (segmented control) of a size setting of a widget. The others are "Small" and "Medium".

editor.ownSettings.sizeMedium.context: Middle of three options (segmented control) of a size setting of a widget. The others are "Small" and "Large".

editor.ownSettings.sizeSmall.context: First of three options (segmented control) of a size setting of a widget. The others are "Medium" and "Large".

editor.ownSettings.useDefault.context: Small button next to an icon setting that has an icon chosen: it removes the choice so the widget’s own icon is used again.

editor.ownSettings.worksWithoutIt.context: Sentence at the end of the note under a device setting when no device of the Homey fits: the setting is optional, so the tile still works without one. "It" is the device the setting asks for.

editor.ownSettings.worksWithoutThem.context: Sentence at the end of the note under a list setting when no device of the Homey fits: the setting is optional, so the tile still works without any. "Them" are the devices the setting asks for.

editor.panelScreen.byWidth.context: First choice of the Layout control in the wall panel setup: the panel shows the screen size that fits the width of its own screen, as any screen does. The other choices force one size: Phone, Tablet or Desktop.

editor.panelScreen.layout.context: Label above the control in the wall panel setup that picks which screen size (layout) the panel shows. Also the screen reader label of the control.

editor.panelScreen.thisPanel.context: Label of the marker on the width ruler in the wall panel setup: it marks where the panel’s own screen falls, followed by its width in pixels, such as "This panel · 1180 px".

editor.panelSize.autoArranged.en: Like any screen: the size its width picks, again when it turns. Here that is {size}; it shows {dashboard, select, named {{name}} other {the dashboard}} as arranged for {size}.
editor.panelSize.autoArranged.context: Hint line under the Layout control in the wall panel setup, while the choice is By width. It explains that the panel shows the screen size its width picks, and that this picks again when the screen is turned. It then says which size this screen gets and that the panel’s dashboard has an arrangement of its own for that size, which it shows.

params.dashboard: Whether the dashboard’s name is known: named when it is, anything else when it is not. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.name: The name of the wall panel’s dashboard, such as Home. Written by the person, not translated. Only used when the dashboard is named.
params.size: The name of the screen size the panel shows. A name, already translated.

editor.panelSize.autoFollows.en: Like any screen: the size its width picks, again when it turns. Here that is {size}; {size} follows {desktop} on {dashboard, select, named {{name}} other {the dashboard}}, so it shows {kind, select, phone {{desktop}’s tiles in one column} other {{desktop}’s arrangement}}.
editor.panelSize.autoFollows.context: Hint line under the Layout control in the wall panel setup, while the choice is By width. It explains that the panel shows the screen size its width picks, and that this picks again when the screen is turned. It then says which size this screen gets and that this size has no arrangement of its own on the panel’s dashboard, so it shows the main layout, Desktop: for Phone its tiles in one column, for Tablet its arrangement as it is.

params.dashboard: Whether the dashboard’s name is known: named when it is, anything else when it is not. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.kind: Which size the panel shows: phone for Phone, other for Tablet. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.name: The name of the wall panel’s dashboard, such as Home. Written by the person, not translated. Only used when the dashboard is named.
params.size: The name of the screen size the panel shows. A name, already translated.

editor.panelSize.eachScreen.en: Each screen shows the size its width picks.
editor.panelSize.eachScreen.context: Hint line under the Layout control in the wall panel setup, shown while the choice is By width and the width of the screen is not known yet (a panel that has not connected). Each screen shows the screen size that fits its own window width.

editor.panelSize.forcedArranged.en: Always {size}, whatever the screen’s width. It shows {dashboard, select, named {{name}} other {the dashboard}} as arranged for {size}.
editor.panelSize.forcedArranged.context: Hint line under the Layout control in the wall panel setup, while one screen size is chosen: the panel always shows that size, whatever the width of its screen. It then says that the panel’s dashboard has an arrangement of its own for that size, which it shows.

params.dashboard: Whether the dashboard’s name is known: named when it is, anything else when it is not. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.name: The name of the wall panel’s dashboard, such as Home. Written by the person, not translated. Only used when the dashboard is named.
params.size: The name of the screen size the panel shows. A name, already translated.

editor.panelSize.forcedFollows.en: Always {size}, whatever the screen’s width. {size} follows {desktop} on {dashboard, select, named {{name}} other {the dashboard}}, so it shows {kind, select, phone {{desktop}’s tiles in one column} other {{desktop}’s arrangement}}.
editor.panelSize.forcedFollows.context: Hint line under the Layout control in the wall panel setup, while one screen size is chosen: the panel always shows that size, whatever the width of its screen. It then says that this size has no arrangement of its own on the panel’s dashboard, so it shows the main layout, Desktop: for Phone its tiles in one column, for Tablet its arrangement as it is.

params.dashboard: Whether the dashboard’s name is known: named when it is, anything else when it is not. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.kind: Which size the panel shows: phone for Phone, other for Tablet. Not shown; it picks the wording.
params.name: The name of the wall panel’s dashboard, such as Home. Written by the person, not translated. Only used when the dashboard is named.
params.size: The name of the screen size the panel shows. A name, already translated.

editor.peopleValues.everyone.context: Heading of the first group in the People tab: values about the whole household, such as how many people are home.

editor.peopleValues.failedText.en: Your Homey didn’t answer. Try again in a moment.
editor.peopleValues.failedText.context: Text under the note title when the Homey did not answer the request for its people.

editor.peopleValues.failedTitle.context: Bold title of a note in the People tab when the Homey did not answer the request for its people.

editor.peopleValues.forbiddenText.en: Tiledash may not see who lives in your home yet. Log in again and allow it (homey.user.readonly).
editor.peopleValues.forbiddenText.context: Text under the note title when Tiledash has no permission to read the Homey’s people. Logging in again asks the Homey for that permission. Keep the permission name in brackets exactly as it is: homey.user.readonly.

editor.peopleValues.forbiddenTitle.context: Bold title of a note in the People tab when Tiledash has no permission to read the Homey’s people.

editor.peopleValues.loadingTitle.context: Bold title shown in the People tab while the Homey is still being asked who lives in the home.

editor.peopleValues.nothingText.en: No one on this Homey, or this place takes neither a number nor yes or no.
editor.peopleValues.nothingText.context: Text under the note title "Nothing that fits": either the Homey has no people, or the place where the value is picked only takes values that are neither a number nor yes/no.

editor.peopleValues.nothingTitle.context: Bold title of a note in the People tab when there is nothing to pick: no people, or none of their values fit this place.

editor.peopleValues.people.context: Heading of the second group in the People tab: each person of the household with their own values, such as home or asleep.

editor.pickerPurpose.dashboardButton.en: {count, plural, =0 {Add widget} one {Add widget} other {Add # widgets}}
editor.pickerPurpose.dashboardButton.context: Main button of the add-widgets window when it adds to a dashboard. It says how many widgets are ticked ("Add 3 widgets"); with none or one ticked it says "Add widget". A command.

params.count: How many things are ticked. A number.

editor.pickerPurpose.dashboardText.en: Tick what you want on this dashboard.
editor.pickerPurpose.dashboardText.context: First sentence of the text under the title of the add-widgets window when it adds to a dashboard. "Tick" means to check the checkboxes in the list. A sentence follows it.

editor.pickerPurpose.dashboardTitle.context: Title of the window where the person ticks devices, flows, moods and widgets to put on the dashboard. A command.

editor.pickerPurpose.howToPick.en: Each gets the widget that fits it best; pick another look on the right.
editor.pickerPurpose.howToPick.context: Second sentence of the text under the title of the add-widgets window. It follows another sentence (such as "Tick what you want on this dashboard.") and says that each ticked thing gets the widget that fits it best, and that another look (another widget for it) can be picked in the right half of the window.

editor.pickerPurpose.pageButton.en: {count, plural, =0 {Add tile to the page} one {Add tile to the page} other {Add # tiles to the page}}
editor.pickerPurpose.pageButton.context: Main button of the window that adds tiles to one page of a stack, when the page has no name. It says how many tiles are ticked ("Add 3 tiles to the page"). A command.

params.count: How many things are ticked. A number.

editor.pickerPurpose.pageButtonNamed.en: {count, plural, =0 {Add tile to {name}} one {Add tile to {name}} other {Add # tiles to {name}}}
editor.pickerPurpose.pageButtonNamed.context: Main button of the window that adds tiles to one page of a stack, when the page has a name. It says how many tiles are ticked ("Add 3 tiles to Kitchen"). A command.

params.count: How many things are ticked. A number.
params.name: The name of the page. Not translated.

editor.pickerPurpose.pageText.en: Tick what goes on this page.
editor.pickerPurpose.pageText.context: First sentence of the text under the title of the window that adds tiles to one page of a stack. "Tick" means to check the checkboxes in the list. A sentence follows it.

editor.pickerPurpose.pageTitle.context: Title of the window that adds tiles to one page of a stack (a tile that shows several pages of tiles), when the page has no name. A command.

editor.pickerPurpose.pageTitleNamed.context: Title of the window that adds tiles to one page of a stack (a tile that shows several pages of tiles). The page has a name. A command.

params.name: The name of the page. Not translated.

editor.pickerPurpose.stackButton.en: {count, plural, =0 {Stack tile} one {Stack tile} other {Stack # tiles}}
editor.pickerPurpose.stackButton.context: Main button of the window that makes a stack (a tile that shows several pages of tiles). It says how many are ticked ("Stack 3 tiles"). A command.

params.count: How many things are ticked. A number.

editor.pickerPurpose.stackText.en: Tick what goes in the stack: each becomes a page of it.
editor.pickerPurpose.stackText.context: First sentence of the text under the title of the window that makes a stack. "Tick" means to check the checkboxes in the list. Each ticked thing becomes one page of the stack. A sentence follows it.

editor.pickerPurpose.stackTitle.context: Title of the window where the person ticks what becomes the pages of a new stack (a tile that shows several pages of tiles). A command.

editor.pickerPurpose.tilesButton.en: {count, plural, =0 {Add tile} one {Add tile} other {Add # tiles}}
editor.pickerPurpose.tilesButton.context: Main button of the window that adds tiles into a widget. It says how many tiles are ticked ("Add 3 tiles"); with none or one ticked it says "Add tile". A command.

params.count: How many things are ticked. A number.

editor.pickerPurpose.tilesText.en: Tick what goes into this widget.
editor.pickerPurpose.tilesText.context: First sentence of the text under the title of the window that adds tiles into a widget. "Tick" means to check the checkboxes in the list. A sentence follows it.

editor.pickerPurpose.tilesTitle.context: Title of the window where the person ticks what goes into one widget as tiles (a widget with a list of tiles, such as a stack). A command.

editor.placeLocation.both.context: Label of the field for the option One text, where one variable holding both coordinates is picked, and its screen reader label: the one text holds a latitude and a longitude.

editor.placeLocation.bothHint.en: A text holding both, as location apps and flows write it: 52.37, 4.89
editor.placeLocation.bothHint.context: Help text under the One text field: the value is one text with latitude and longitude, written like the example by location apps and by Homey flows. Keep the example numbers and its comma as they are.

editor.placeLocation.bothPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the One text field before anything is picked: it asks for a variable that holds both coordinates in one text.

editor.placeLocation.introFound.en: The device’s own latitude and longitude, now {lat}, {lon}. Choose Two numbers to use other values.
editor.placeLocation.introFound.context: Help text when the option The device is chosen and the device reports its location: what the device says right now. “Two numbers” is the name of the second option of the switch above; write it exactly as that option.

params.lat: The latitude now, such as 52.3731, or a dash when it is not a number. Not translated.
params.lon: The longitude now, such as 4.8936, or a dash when it is not a number. Not translated.

editor.placeLocation.introNone.en: This device doesn’t say where it is by itself: choose Two numbers or One text.
editor.placeLocation.introNone.context: Help text when the option The device is chosen but the device reports no location by itself. “Two numbers” and “One text” are the names of the other two options of the switch above; write them exactly as those options.

editor.placeLocation.latitude.context: Label of the field where the latitude (the north-south coordinate) is picked, and its screen reader label.

editor.placeLocation.latitudePlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the latitude field before anything is picked: it asks for a reading or variable that holds the latitude.

editor.placeLocation.locationFrom.context: Label of the three-way switch that chooses where the place’s coordinates come from, and its screen reader label. It continues with the options: The device, Two numbers, One text.

editor.placeLocation.longitude.context: Label of the field where the longitude (the east-west coordinate) is picked, and its screen reader label.

editor.placeLocation.longitudePlaceholde.context: Placeholder of the longitude field before anything is picked: it asks for a reading or variable that holds the longitude.

editor.placeLocation.modeDevice.context: First option of the switch: the coordinates come from the place’s device itself. Only offered for a place that is a device. Another message refers to this by name.

editor.placeLocation.modeOne.context: Third option of the switch: the coordinates are in one text value that holds both. Another message refers to this option by name: keep them the same.

editor.placeLocation.modeTwo.context: Second option of the switch: the coordinates are two numbers, a latitude and a longitude, each picked from a reading or a variable. Two other messages refer to this option by name: keep them the same.

editor.placeLocation.name.context: Label of the field for the name of a place of its own (one that is not a device): the name its pin shows.

editor.placeLocation.namePlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the name field of a place: the name shown on its pin on the map.

editor.placeLocation.swappedText.en: The latitude is {lat}, which is more than 90, so it can only be a longitude. Try the other way round.
editor.placeLocation.swappedText.context: Text of the orange warning: the value used as latitude is more than 90, which a latitude can never be, so the two are probably swapped.

params.lat: The value now used as latitude, such as 115.86. Not translated.

editor.placeLocation.swappedTitle.context: Bold title of an orange warning when the picked latitude is beyond 90 degrees: latitude and longitude are probably the wrong way round.

editor.placeLocation.tapNothing.context: First choice of the dropdown "A tap on the pin": tapping the pin does nothing. The other choices open a dashboard.

editor.placeLocation.tapOnPin.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what happens when the pin of a place of its own is tapped on the map, and its screen reader label.

editor.placeLocation.tapOpen.context: A choice of the dropdown "A tap on the pin": tapping the pin opens that dashboard. One choice per dashboard.

params.name: The name of the dashboard, chosen by the person. Not translated.

editor.placesEditor.addDevice.context: Button under the list of places: it opens a search to add a device that says where it is, or any device.

editor.placesEditor.addFromValues.context: Second, quieter button under the list of places: it adds a place that is not a device, whose latitude and longitude are read from picked values (readings or variables).

editor.placesEditor.atMost.context: Text of the disabled add button once the list is full: no more places or devices can be added. It names the limit.

params.max: The most places the list takes, a whole number such as 20.

editor.placesEditor.chooseWhere.context: Orange line under the name of a place in the list when its latitude or longitude is not chosen yet: the person has to pick where it is.

editor.placesEditor.coordinatesPicked.context: Grey line under the name of a place in the list: where it is now, and that its location is read from two values picked by the person (a latitude and a longitude).

params.lat: The latitude as a number with up to four decimals, such as 52.3731. Not translated.
params.lon: The longitude as a number with up to four decimals, such as 4.8936. Not translated.

editor.placesEditor.coordinatesText.context: Grey line under the name of a place in the list: where it is now, and that its location is read from one text value that holds both coordinates.

params.lat: The latitude as a number with up to four decimals, such as 52.3731. Not translated.
params.lon: The longitude as a number with up to four decimals, such as 4.8936. Not translated.

editor.placesEditor.doneAdding.context: Quiet button that closes the add area and goes back to the list of places.

editor.placesEditor.kindAny.context: Second option of the two-way switch in the add area: every device of the Homey, so the person can pick its readings themselves. Another message refers to this option by name: keep them the same.

editor.placesEditor.kindFound.context: First option of the two-way switch in the add area: only the devices that report where they are by themselves.

editor.placesEditor.locationOf.context: Screen reader label of the edit button of a place in the list: it opens that place’s location settings. Not visible as text.

params.name: The name of the place or of its device. Not translated.

editor.placesEditor.moveDown.context: Screen reader label of the button that moves a place one step down in the list.

editor.placesEditor.moveUp.context: Screen reader label of the button that moves a place one step up in the list.

editor.placesEditor.newPlace.context: Name shown in the list for a place of its own that has no name at all (the person cleared it).

editor.placesEditor.newPlaceName.context: The name a new place of its own gets when the person adds one from values, before they type a name. It is saved as that place’s name and shown on its pin.

editor.placesEditor.noLocation.context: Grey line under the name of a place in the list when its device reports no location at the moment (no valid coordinates).

editor.placesEditor.noOtherLocated.en: No other device says where it is. Choose “Any device” to pick its readings yourself.
editor.placesEditor.noOtherLocated.context: Grey text in the add area when the list is empty while the first option is chosen and nothing is typed: no device reports its own location. “Any device” is the name of the second option of the switch above; write it exactly as that option.

editor.placesEditor.none.context: Grey text where the list of places goes when the person has not added any place yet.

editor.placesEditor.nothingMatches.context: Grey text in the add area when the search matches no device. Said as a short statement.

editor.placesEditor.remove.context: Screen reader label of the button that removes a place from the list.

editor.placesEditor.removedFromHomey.context: Name of a place in the list, and its orange line below it, when its device no longer exists in the Homey.

editor.placesEditor.search.context: Placeholder of the search field in the add area, above the list of devices.

editor.placesEditor.swapped.context: Orange line under the name of a place in the list when its latitude is beyond 90 degrees, so latitude and longitude are probably the wrong way round.

editor.placesEditor.whichDevices.context: Screen reader label of the two-way switch in the add area that chooses which devices are listed. Not visible as text.

editor.presetName.hint.context: Small help text under the name field of a style preset: presets belong to the person and can be used on all of their dashboards.

editor.presetName.label.context: Label above the text field for the name of a style preset.

editor.presetName.placeholder.context: Example shown faintly in the empty name field of a style preset, to suggest what a name could look like: a soft look with frosted glass. A short example name.

editor.presetRow.apply.en: {count, plural, one {Apply {name} to this tile} other {Apply {name} to the # tiles}}
editor.presetRow.apply.context: Screen reader label of a preset’s row, which is a button: it gives the look of the preset to the selected tile or tiles, linked to the preset.

params.count: How many tiles are selected, at least 1.
params.name: The name of the preset, written by the person. Not translated.

editor.presetRow.delete.context: Red button in the confirmation for deleting a preset: delete it for good. Shown after the question "Delete this preset?".

editor.presetRow.deleteBody.en: {tiles, plural, =0 {No tile uses it.} one {The tile using it keeps its look, no longer linked.} other {The # tiles using it keep their look, no longer linked.}}
editor.presetRow.deleteBody.context: Text under the question "Delete this preset?": what happens to the tiles that use the preset. They keep how they look but stop following the preset. When no tile uses it, that is said instead.

params.tiles: How many tiles use the preset, over all dashboards. 0 when none.

editor.presetRow.deleteTitle.context: Question that asks the person to confirm deleting a preset, in bold and as the screen reader label of the confirmation.

params.name: The name of the preset, written by the person. Not translated.

editor.presetRow.keep.context: Button in the confirmation for deleting a preset: do not delete it, keep the preset.

editor.presetRow.markChanged.context: Small mark next to a preset’s name: the selected tiles use this preset but changed something on top of it.

editor.presetRow.markInUse.context: Small mark next to a preset’s name: the selected tiles use this preset, unchanged.

editor.presetRow.menuDelete.context: Item of the menu of a preset, in red: delete the preset. The … says the person is asked to confirm first.

editor.presetRow.menuRename.context: Item of the menu of a preset: change the name of the preset. The … says a name field follows.

editor.presetRow.menuUpdate.en: {count, plural, one {Update from this tile} other {Update from these tiles}}
editor.presetRow.menuUpdate.context: Item of the menu of a preset: the preset takes over the look of the selected tile or tiles, so every tile that uses the preset follows. It is greyed out while the selected tiles look different.

params.count: How many tiles are selected, at least 1.

editor.presetRow.more.context: Screen reader label of the small "…" button on a preset’s row that opens its menu (rename, update, delete). Names the preset first.

params.name: The name of the preset, written by the person. Not translated.

editor.presetRow.rename.context: Button that keeps the new name of a style preset. Primary button of the little form shown after the menu item Rename… was chosen.

editor.presetStatus.backToPreset.context: Button shown when the selected tiles changed something on top of their preset: it drops those changes, so they look like the preset again.

editor.presetStatus.changedHere.context: Small text under the name of a preset when the selected tiles changed things on top of it. It is followed by a list of what they changed, such as "corners, shadow and accent".

params.changes: The list of what was changed, in words, translated.

editor.presetStatus.linked.en: Linked · changes to the preset show here
editor.presetStatus.linked.context: Small text under the name of a preset: the selected tiles follow this preset, so when the preset is changed they change with it. Keep the · between the two parts.

editor.presetStatus.linkedOthers.en: {others, plural, one {Linked · # other tile follows it too} other {Linked · # other tiles follow it too}}
editor.presetStatus.linkedOthers.context: Small text under the name of a preset: the selected tiles follow this preset, and so do this many other tiles, on any dashboard. Keep the · between the two parts.

params.others: How many other tiles, outside the selection, use the preset, at least 1.

editor.presetStatus.mixedDetail.en: The selected tiles use different presets, or some none
editor.presetStatus.mixedDetail.context: Small text under "Mixed presets": some of the selected tiles use one preset, others another, or some use none.

editor.presetStatus.mixedTitle.context: Bold title of the line at the top of the style panel when the selected tiles do not all use the same preset.

editor.presetStatus.unlink.en: {count, plural, one {Unlink, keep this look} other {Unlink, keep their look}}
editor.presetStatus.unlink.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small button: the selected tile or tiles stop following the preset and keep the look they have now.

params.count: How many tiles are selected, at least 1.

editor.presetStatus.updatePreset.context: Button shown when the selected tiles changed something on top of their preset: the preset takes over the look of the tiles, so every tile that uses it follows.

editor.presetToasts.applied.en: {count, plural, one {{name} on # tile} other {{name} on # tiles}}
editor.presetToasts.applied.context: Title of the green message (toast) after a preset was given to the selected tile or tiles, such as "Soft glass on 3 tiles".

params.count: How many tiles got the preset, at least 1.
params.name: The name of the preset. Not translated.

editor.presetToasts.deleteFailed.context: Red message (toast) when deleting a preset failed, when the server gave no reason of its own.

editor.presetToasts.deleted.context: Title of the message (toast) after a preset was deleted.

params.name: The name the preset had. Not translated.

editor.presetToasts.deletedKeep.context: Text under the message "Deleted …": the tiles that used the preset look the same as before, but no longer follow a preset.

editor.presetToasts.fallbackName.context: Stands in for the name of a preset in a message when the preset can no longer be found, at the start of a sentence such as "The preset updated".

editor.presetToasts.renameFailed.context: Red message (toast) when renaming a preset failed, when the server gave no reason of its own.

editor.presetToasts.saveFailed.context: Red message (toast) when saving the look of the selected tiles as a preset failed, when the server gave no reason of its own.

editor.presetToasts.saved.context: Title of the green message (toast) after the look of the selected tiles was saved as a new preset.

params.name: The name the person gave the preset. Not translated.

editor.presetToasts.savedLinked.context: Text under the message "Saved …": the selected tiles are now linked to the new preset, so they follow it when it changes.

editor.presetToasts.updateFailed.context: Red message (toast) when updating a preset from the selected tiles failed, when the server gave no reason of its own.

editor.presetToasts.updated.context: Title of the green message (toast) after a preset took over the look of the selected tiles, such as "Soft glass updated".

params.name: The name of the preset. Not translated.

editor.presetToasts.updatedFollow.en: {count, plural, one {# tile follows it} other {# tiles follow it}}
editor.presetToasts.updatedFollow.context: Text under the message "… updated": how many tiles use the preset and so changed with it, on all dashboards. "It" is the preset.

params.count: How many tiles use the preset, 0 or more.

editor.readingSummary.change.context: Small button beside the value a summary shows: it opens the picker to choose another value.

editor.readingSummary.goneReading.en: That reading is no longer on this Homey. Pick another.
editor.readingSummary.goneReading.context: Line shown when the device reading a summary shows is gone (the device or the reading was removed from the Homey). "Pick another" asks for a new one.

editor.readingSummary.goneValue.en: That value is no longer on this Homey. Pick another.
editor.readingSummary.goneValue.context: Line shown when the energy or price value a summary shows is gone from the Homey. "Pick another" asks for a new one.

editor.readingSummary.goneVariable.en: That variable is no longer on this Homey. Pick another.
editor.readingSummary.goneVariable.context: Line shown when the Logic variable a summary shows has been removed from the Homey. "Pick another" asks for a new one.

editor.readingsEditor.addReading.context: Button with a plus icon that opens the picker for adding a reading to the widget.

editor.readingsEditor.atMost.en: At most {max, plural, one {# reading} other {# readings}}.
editor.readingsEditor.atMost.context: Line that replaces the add button once the widget has as many readings as it can draw. For example: At most 6 readings.

params.max: The most readings the widget draws. A number.

editor.readingsEditor.hint.en: Readings only have a history when they are recorded; the tile says so when one isn’t. More than one draw a line each, or add up to a total or average.
editor.readingsEditor.hint.context: Help text under the list of readings of a history widget: a reading needs recording to have a history, and several readings are drawn as separate lines or combined into a total or an average.

editor.readingsEditor.hintWithHosts.en: Readings only have a history when they are recorded; the tile says so when one isn’t. More than one draw a line each, or add up to a total or average. Energy comes from your Homey’s own reports; prices from those Tiledash keeps.
editor.readingsEditor.hintWithHosts.context: Help text under the list of readings of a history widget when energy and prices can be added: the same as the plain help text, plus where the energy and prices come from (the Homey’s own reports, and prices kept by Tiledash).

editor.readingsEditor.hostEnergy.context: Name of an energy reading in the list of a history widget: the group first, then which energy value. For example: Energy · Solar.

params.name: Which energy value it is, such as "Solar". Taken from the Homey’s English names for now.

editor.readingsEditor.hostPrices.context: Name of a price reading in the list of a history widget: the group first, then which price. For example: Prices · Electricity.

params.name: Which price it is, such as "Electricity". Taken from the Homey’s English names for now.

editor.readingsEditor.moveDown.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a reading one place down in the list.

editor.readingsEditor.moveUp.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small arrow button that moves a reading one place up in the list.

editor.readingsEditor.nameInChart.context: Label of the text field where a reading gets its own name in the chart’s legend and totals.

editor.readingsEditor.namePlaceholder.context: Grey placeholder of the "Name in the chart" field for a reading that has no title of its own.

editor.readingsEditor.none.en: No readings yet. Add one to see its history.
editor.readingsEditor.none.context: Empty-state line where the list of readings would be, before one is added.

editor.readingsEditor.readingOf.context: Name of a reading in the list of a history widget: the device, then which of its readings. For example: Bedroom climate · Temperature.

params.device: The name of the device, or the message "Removed device" when it is gone.
params.reading: The title of the device’s reading, such as "Temperature".

editor.readingsEditor.remove.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small button that removes a reading from the widget.

editor.readingsEditor.removedDevice.context: Name shown in place of a device that no longer exists in the Homey, in the name of a reading in the list.

editor.saveStatus.notSaved.context: Small amber status text at the top right while a dashboard is edited, with a warning icon. The last change could not be saved to the server.

editor.saveStatus.retry.context: Small button next to "Not saved". It tries to save the last change again.

editor.saveStatus.saved.context: Small status text at the top right while a dashboard is edited, with a check mark. All changes are saved on the server.

editor.saveStatus.saving.context: Small status text at the top right while a dashboard is edited, with a pulsing dot. The last change is being saved to the server right now.

editor.screenSize.desktop.context: Name of the largest of the three screen sizes a dashboard can be arranged for: windows 1100 px wide and more, such as a laptop or a computer screen. It is also the main layout: the other sizes follow it until they are arranged. A name, shown on the size switch and the ruler and inserted into many sentences. Use the same word for it everywhere, as for Phone and Tablet.

editor.screenSize.newHere.context: Small badge on a tile, and a tag in the bar over the canvas: the tile was added on another screen size and the rules put it at the end of this one, so it has not been placed by hand here yet.

editor.screenSize.phone.context: Name of the smallest of the three screen sizes a dashboard can be arranged for: windows under 720 px wide, such as a phone held upright. A name, shown on the size switch and the ruler and inserted into many sentences. Use the same word for it everywhere, as for Tablet and Desktop.

editor.screenSize.rangeDesktop.context: Window widths that show the Desktop size, in the bar over the canvas in edit mode: anything from the number of pixels up. px is the CSS pixel unit.

params.px: The width in pixels at which Desktop starts. A plain number, such as 1100.

editor.screenSize.rangePhone.context: Window widths that show the Phone size, in the bar over the canvas in edit mode: anything narrower than the number of pixels. px is the CSS pixel unit.

params.px: The width in pixels at which Tablet starts. A plain number, such as 720.

editor.screenSize.rangeTablet.context: Window widths that show the Tablet size, in the bar over the canvas in edit mode: from one width to another, both in pixels. px is the CSS pixel unit.

params.from: The narrowest width of the size, in pixels. A plain number, such as 720.
params.to: The widest width of the size, in pixels. A plain number, such as 1099.

editor.screenSize.statusArranged.context: Small status word for a screen size, on the size switch and next to the name of the size in the miniature of a dashboard: this size has an arrangement of its own, with tiles moved and resized by hand for it.

editor.screenSize.statusFollowing.context: Small status for a screen size, on the size switch and next to the name of the size in the miniature of a dashboard: this size has no arrangement of its own yet and shows the main layout, Desktop, instead.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.screenSize.statusMain.context: Small grey word next to the name of a screen size in the miniature of a dashboard: this size is the main layout (Desktop), the one the others follow until they are arranged.

editor.screenSize.statusMainLayout.context: Small status line under the name of a screen size on the size switch in edit mode: this size is the main layout (Desktop), the one the other sizes follow until they are arranged.

editor.screenSize.tablet.context: Name of the middle one of the three screen sizes a dashboard can be arranged for: windows 720 to 1099 px wide, such as a tablet or a phone on its side. A name, shown on the size switch and the ruler and inserted into many sentences. Use the same word for it everywhere, as for Phone and Desktop.

editor.settingKinds.addGesture.en: {gesture, select, hold {Add hold} double {Add double tap} other {Add tap}}
editor.settingKinds.addGesture.context: Button that adds what a gesture on the part does.

editor.settingKinds.change.context: Not a gesture: a control on the tile (such as a slider) was changed.

editor.settingKinds.double.context: A gesture on a tile: two taps quickly.

editor.settingKinds.doubleTitle.context: Tooltip of the Double tap gesture chip.

editor.settingKinds.fewer.context: Read out for the − button of a counter.

editor.settingKinds.hold.context: A gesture on a tile: a long press.

editor.settingKinds.holdLabel.context: Read out for what holding a part does.

params.label: The part’s name, such as "Tapping a part".

editor.settingKinds.holdTitle.context: Tooltip of the Hold gesture chip.

editor.settingKinds.more.context: Read out for the + button of a counter.

editor.settingKinds.nothingElse.en: This device has nothing else to show.
editor.settingKinds.nothingElse.context: When a device has no more readings to pick.

editor.settingKinds.range.context: Label of the time range a reading’s history covers, such as 24 hours.

editor.settingKinds.tap.context: A gesture on a tile: a short tap.

editor.settingKinds.tapTitle.context: Tooltip of the Tap gesture chip.

editor.showWhen.add.context: Small word in front of two buttons that add a condition: "Add  A value  The time". It reads as a label for the buttons next to it, not as a button itself.

editor.showWhen.addLabel.context: Screen reader label of the group of two buttons ("A value" and "The time") that add a condition to the tile’s _When to show_ settings. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.addTime.context: Small button after the word "Add" that adds a condition on the time of the day. Reads as "Add: the time".

editor.showWhen.addValue.context: Small button after the word "Add" that adds a condition on a value (a reading of a device, a variable or who is home). Reads as "Add: a value".

editor.showWhen.and.context: Word in a time condition between the two time boxes: "Between 18:00 and 23:00". Lower case.

editor.showWhen.between.context: Word in a time condition, before the first time box: the tile shows between a start time and an end time, such as "Between 18:00 and 23:00". The two time boxes and the word "and" follow.

editor.showWhen.choiceLabel.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown of a condition that picks one of the fixed choices of a value, such as the mode of a thermostat. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.dayFriday.context: Very short name of Friday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.dayMonday.context: Very short name of Monday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.daySaturday.context: Very short name of Saturday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.daySunday.context: Very short name of Sunday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.dayThursday.context: Very short name of Thursday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.dayTuesday.context: Very short name of Tuesday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.dayWednesday.context: Very short name of Wednesday on a small toggle button that chooses the days of a time condition. Two letters.

editor.showWhen.days.context: Screen reader label of the group of small day buttons (Mo, Tu, We…) in a time condition. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.from.context: Screen reader label of the first time box of a time condition: the time the tile starts to show. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.hideHint.en: For widgets that can be empty, like Busy now when nothing runs.
editor.showWhen.hideHint.context: Small help text under the checkbox "Hide while it has nothing to show". "Busy now" is the name of a Tiledash widget that lists what is running now; keep it as it is, or use the translated widget name if there is one.

editor.showWhen.hideTitle.en: Hide while it has nothing to show
editor.showWhen.hideTitle.context: Label of a checkbox in the _When to show_ settings: the tile hides itself while its widget has nothing to show. A small help text follows below it.

editor.showWhen.inputNumber.context: Screen reader label of the box where the person types the number a value is compared with, in a condition. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.inputText.context: Screen reader label of the box where the person types the text a value is compared with, in a condition. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.matchAll.context: First option of a two-option switch (segmented control) over a list of conditions: the tile shows only while every condition holds. The other option is "Any of these".

editor.showWhen.matchAny.context: Second option of a two-option switch (segmented control) over a list of conditions: the tile shows while at least one condition holds. The other option is "All of these".

editor.showWhen.matchLabel.context: Screen reader label of the two-option switch "All of these / Any of these", shown when a tile has more than one condition. Not visible as text. It asks which of the conditions must be true.

editor.showWhen.modeAlways.context: First option of a two-option switch (segmented control) in the _When to show_ settings of a tile: the tile is always visible on the dashboard. The other option is "Only when…".

editor.showWhen.modeLabel.context: Screen reader label of the two-option switch (segmented control) "Always / Only when…" in the _When to show_ settings of a tile. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.modeSome.context: Second option of a two-option switch (segmented control) in the _When to show_ settings of a tile: the tile is only visible while conditions hold, which the person then adds below. The other option is "Always".

editor.showWhen.removeCondition.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button at the end of a condition row. It removes that condition from the tile’s _When to show_ settings.

editor.showWhen.testAbove.context: Choice in a dropdown of a condition, read after the name of a number value, before a number the person types: the value is higher than that number. For example "Temperature is above 21". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.showWhen.testBelow.context: Choice in a dropdown of a condition, read after the name of a number value, before a number the person types: the value is lower than that number. For example "Temperature is below 18". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.showWhen.testIs.context: The only choice in a dropdown of a condition on a value that has a fixed list of choices, read after the name of the value and before a choice picked in the next dropdown. For example "Mode is Away". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.showWhen.testIsExactly.context: The only choice in a dropdown of a condition on a text value, read after the name of the value and before a text the person types. For example "Status is exactly Idle". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.showWhen.testLabel.context: Screen reader label of the dropdown of a condition that chooses how the value is tested, such as "is above" or "is yes (on)". Not visible as text. A test here is a comparison, not an exam.

editor.showWhen.testOff.context: Choice in a dropdown of a condition, read after the name of a value: the value is no, or off. For example "Light is no (off)". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.showWhen.testOn.context: Choice in a dropdown of a condition, read after the name of a value: the value is yes, or on. For example "Light is yes (on)". Lower case, as it continues a phrase.

editor.showWhen.to.context: Screen reader label of the second time box of a time condition: the time the tile stops showing. Not visible as text.

editor.showWhen.valueLabel.context: Screen reader label of the field that picks the value of a condition (a reading of a device, a variable, who is home). Not visible as text.

editor.sizeEditing.arrangeFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when giving a screen size an arrangement of its own did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost. The person can try again.

editor.sizeEditing.arranged.context: Title of a notification (toast) after the person made a screen size, Phone or Tablet, have an arrangement of its own. The text under it says what that means.

params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeEditing.arrangedDetail.en: It starts as it looked. Moving and resizing here now changes {size} only.
editor.sizeEditing.arrangedDetail.context: Text of a notification (toast) after the person made a screen size have an arrangement of its own: the arrangement starts as the size looked until now, and from here moving and resizing tiles changes only this size.

params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeEditing.canvasLabel.context: Screen reader label of the canvas in edit mode that shows the dashboard at the width of a phone or a tablet: the size and the width the canvas is drawn at, in pixels.

params.px: The width of the canvas in pixels. A plain number, such as 390.
params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeEditing.followFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when making a screen size follow the main layout, Desktop, again did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost. The person can try again.

editor.sizeEditing.followed.context: Notification (toast) after the person threw away the arrangement of a screen size: it follows the main layout, Desktop, again.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeEditing.hidden.en: {count, plural, one {Hidden on {size}} other {# tiles hidden on {size}}}
editor.sizeEditing.hidden.context: Title of a notification (toast) after the person hid tiles on one screen size: they are hidden on this size only and stay on the others.

params.count: How many tiles were hidden. A number, at least 1.
params.size: The name of the screen size the tiles were hidden on, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.
