editor.sizeEditing.hiddenDetail.en: Still on {others}. The tray lists {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} to bring back.
editor.sizeEditing.hiddenDetail.context: Text of a notification (toast) after the person hid tiles on one screen size: the tiles are still on the other two sizes, and the tray of hidden tiles under the canvas lists them so they can be brought back.

params.count: How many tiles were hidden. A number, at least 1.
params.others: The other two screen sizes, as a list, such as "Tablet and Desktop". Already translated.

editor.sizeEditing.hideFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when hiding tiles on one screen size (the Hide on Phone or Hide on Tablet button or menu item) did not work. The person can try again.

editor.sizeEditing.keepFailed.en: Couldn’t keep the new tiles there.
editor.sizeEditing.keepFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when keeping the new tiles where the rules put them (the Keep them here button in the bar over the canvas) did not work. The person can try again.

editor.sizeEditing.removed.en: {count, plural, one {Removed from every size} other {# tiles removed from every size}}
editor.sizeEditing.removed.context: Title of a notification (toast) after the person removed tiles from the dashboard while screen sizes are in play: a tile is removed from Phone, Tablet and Desktop alike.

params.count: How many tiles were removed. A number, at least 1.

editor.sizeEditing.removedDetail.en: To keep {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} elsewhere, use Hide on {size} instead.
editor.sizeEditing.removedDetail.context: Text of a notification (toast) after the person removed tiles on Phone or Tablet: removing takes them off every size, and to keep them on the other sizes the person should have used the Hide on button or menu item instead. "Hide on" followed by the size is the exact wording of that button and menu item, which reads "Hide on Phone" in English: use the same wording.

params.count: How many tiles were removed. A number, at least 1.
params.size: The name of the screen size being edited, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeEditing.showFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when putting a hidden tile back on a screen size (the Show button in the tray of hidden tiles) did not work. The person can try again.

editor.sizeMap.hidden.context: Small grey note under the miniature of a dashboard on one screen size: how many tiles are hidden on that size.

params.count: How many tiles are hidden on the size. A number, at least 1.

editor.sizeMap.label.context: Screen reader description of the miniature of a dashboard on one screen size, a picture of small blocks: the size and how many tiles it shows.

params.count: How many tiles the size shows. A number, 0 or more.
params.size: The name of the screen size, such as Phone. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeMap.labelHidden.en: {size}: {count, plural, one {# tile} other {# tiles}}, {hidden, number} hidden
editor.sizeMap.labelHidden.context: Screen reader description of the miniature of a dashboard on one screen size, a picture of small blocks: the size, how many tiles it shows and how many more are hidden on that size.

params.count: How many tiles the size shows. A number, 0 or more.
params.hidden: How many tiles are hidden on the size. A number, at least 1.
params.size: The name of the screen size, such as Phone. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeRuler.label.context: Screen reader description of the ruler of window widths: which screen size a window shows, by its width in pixels. Narrower than the first number is Phone, narrower than the second is Tablet, anything wider is Desktop. px is the CSS pixel unit.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.desktopPx: The width in pixels at which Desktop starts. A plain number, such as 1100.
params.phone: The name of the Phone size. A name, already translated.
params.tablet: The name of the Tablet size. A name, already translated.
params.tabletPx: The width in pixels at which Tablet starts. A plain number, such as 720.

editor.sizeRuler.marker.context: Label of the marker on the width ruler: the screen that falls at that width. px is the CSS pixel unit.

params.screen: What the marked screen is called, such as "This screen" or "This panel". Already translated.
params.width: The width of the screen in pixels. A plain number, such as 1280.

editor.sizeRuler.thisScreen.context: Label of the marker on the width ruler: it marks where the screen the person is using falls, followed by its width in pixels, such as "This screen · 1280 px".

editor.sizeRuler.verdictForced.en: Set to show {forced}; by its width it would show {byWidth}.
editor.sizeRuler.verdictForced.context: Line under the width ruler when a wall panel is set to always show one screen size that is not the one its width would pick. It says which size it is set to show, in bold, and which one it would show by its width.

params.byWidth: The size the width of the screen would pick. A name, already translated.
params.forced: The size the panel is set to show. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeRuler.verdictSet.context: Line under the width ruler when a wall panel is set to always show one screen size, and this is also the one its width would pick. It says which size the panel shows, in bold, because it was set so.

params.size: The size the panel shows. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeRuler.verdictWidth.context: Line under the width ruler when a screen has no size of its own set: it shows the size its width picks. It says which size that is, in bold.

params.size: The size the width of the screen picks. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.arrangedMoves.en: Moving and resizing here changes {size} only.
editor.sizeScope.arrangedMoves.context: Sentence in the bar over the canvas while a size with an arrangement of its own is edited: moving and resizing tiles changes this size and no other.

params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.arrangedTitle.context: Title of the bar over the canvas in edit mode while a screen size that has an arrangement of its own is edited. The width range of the size follows after a dot.

params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.everySize.en: Adding or removing a tile changes every size.
editor.sizeScope.everySize.context: Bold last sentence of the bar over the canvas in edit mode, on every screen size. A tile added or removed shows up or goes away on Phone, Tablet and Desktop alike, unlike moving and resizing.

editor.sizeScope.followingTitle.context: Title of the bar over the canvas in edit mode while a screen size is edited that has no arrangement of its own: it shows the main layout, Desktop, instead. The width range of the size follows after a dot.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.followsPhone.en: It shows {desktop}’s tiles in one column, in reading order. Arrange it to move and resize tiles for phones only.
editor.sizeScope.followsPhone.context: Sentence in the bar over the canvas while the Phone size is edited and has no arrangement of its own: it shows the tiles of the main layout, Desktop, stacked in one column in reading order. It says what the Arrange for phone button does: the person can then move and resize tiles for phones only.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.followsTablet.en: It shows {desktop}’s arrangement at a tablet’s width. Arrange it to move and resize tiles for tablets only.
editor.sizeScope.followsTablet.context: Sentence in the bar over the canvas while the Tablet size is edited and has no arrangement of its own: it shows the arrangement of the main layout, Desktop, at the width of a tablet. It says what the Arrange for tablet button does: the person can then move and resize tiles for tablets only.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.mainMoves.en: Moving and resizing here moves {sizes} too, while {count, plural, one {it follows} other {they follow}} {desktop}.
editor.sizeScope.mainMoves.context: Sentence in the bar over the canvas while the Desktop size is edited and at least one other size has no arrangement of its own: moving and resizing tiles on Desktop also moves them on the sizes that follow it, as long as they do.

params.count: How many sizes follow Desktop. A number, 1 or 2.
params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.
params.sizes: The sizes that follow Desktop, as a list: Phone, Tablet, or Phone and Tablet. Already translated.

editor.sizeScope.mainOnly.en: Moving and resizing here changes {desktop} only: the other sizes are arranged.
editor.sizeScope.mainOnly.context: Sentence in the bar over the canvas while the Desktop size is edited and both other sizes have an arrangement of their own: moving and resizing tiles on Desktop changes nothing on them.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScope.mainTitle.context: Title of the bar over the canvas in edit mode while the Desktop size is edited. Desktop is the main layout: the sizes that have no arrangement of their own follow it. The width range of the size follows after a dot.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScopeBar.arrange.en: Arrange for {size, select, phone {phone} tablet {tablet} other {desktop}}
editor.sizeScopeBar.arrange.context: Button in the bar over the canvas while a screen size without an arrangement of its own is edited. It gives that size an arrangement of its own, starting as it looks now, so tiles can be moved and resized for it only. The word at the end is the kind of device, in lower case.

params.size: Which size: phone, tablet or desktop. Not shown; it picks the device word.

editor.sizeScopeBar.followAgain.context: Button in the bar over the canvas while a screen size with an arrangement of its own is edited. It throws that arrangement away so the size shows the main layout, Desktop, again. The person is asked to confirm first.

params.desktop: The name of the Desktop size. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeScopeBar.fresh.en: {count, plural, one {# tile was added on another size and put at the end of its section. Drag it where it belongs, or} other {# tiles were added on another size and put at the end of their sections. Drag them where they belong, or}}
editor.sizeScopeBar.fresh.context: Notice in the bar over the canvas, after a New here tag: tiles added on another screen size were put at the end of their section by the rules. It tells the person to drag them to the right place, or else keep them where they are: the sentence ends with "or" and goes on in the button after it, "Keep them here". A section is a heading with the tiles under it.

params.count: How many tiles are new on this size. A number, at least 1.

editor.sizeScopeBar.keep.context: Button after the notice about new tiles in the bar over the canvas, which ends with "or". It keeps the new tiles where the rules put them, at the end of their section.

params.count: How many tiles are new on this size. A number, at least 1.

editor.sizeScopeBar.label.context: Screen reader label of the bar over the canvas in edit mode: it is about the layout of one screen size.

params.size: The name of the screen size, Phone or Tablet. A name, already translated.

editor.sizeSwitch.label.context: Screen reader label of the switch in edit mode with a choice for each screen size (Phone, Tablet, Desktop): the size the person arranges the dashboard for.

editor.sizeSwitch.newCount.context: Small badge on a choice of the switch for the screen size being arranged: how many tiles were added on another size and are new here. Short.

params.count: How many tiles are new on the size. A number, at least 1.

editor.sizeSwitch.option.context: Screen reader label of one choice on the switch for the screen size being arranged: the size and its status, such as "Phone, Follows Desktop".

params.size: The name of the screen size. A name, already translated.
params.status: What the size’s arrangement is: Main layout, Arranged or Follows Desktop. Already translated.

editor.sizeSwitch.optionNew.context: Screen reader label of one choice on the switch for the screen size being arranged, when tiles were added on another size and are new here: the size, its status and how many tiles are new, such as "Phone, Follows Desktop, 2 new".

params.count: How many tiles are new on the size. A number, at least 1.
params.size: The name of the screen size. A name, already translated.
params.status: What the size’s arrangement is: Main layout, Arranged or Follows Desktop. Already translated.

editor.sizesGlance.label.context: Screen reader label of the overview that shows the dashboard in miniature on all three screen sizes (Phone, Tablet and Desktop) next to each other.

editor.sizesGlance.title.context: Small heading above the overview that shows the dashboard in miniature on all three screen sizes (Phone, Tablet and Desktop) next to each other. Clicking a miniature switches to that size.

editor.slotPicker.bottomCenter.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the middle of the bottom edge. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.bottomLeft.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the corner at the bottom left. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.bottomRight.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the corner at the bottom right. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.middleCenter.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the very middle of the tile. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.middleLeft.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the middle of the left edge. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.middleRight.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the middle of the right edge. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.topCenter.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the middle of the top edge. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.topLeft.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the corner at the top left. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.slotPicker.topRight.context: Name of one of the nine spots of a tile in the slot picker: the corner at the top right. Screen reader label and tooltip of a dot, not visible text.

editor.stackInPlace.addTiles.context: Button in the empty state of a page of a Stack edited on the dashboard: opens the widget picker to add tiles to the page. A command.

editor.stackInPlace.empty.context: Empty state on a page of a Stack that is edited where it sits on the dashboard, when the page has no tiles yet. A button to add tiles follows it. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.stackThese.failed.context: Red notification (toast) when stacking tiles into a Stack did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost. The person can try again. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.stackThese.heading.en: A heading can’t be stacked. Select tiles only.
editor.stackThese.heading.context: Red notification (toast) when the selection to be stacked holds a heading, which can’t go into a Stack. The person should select tiles only. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.stackThese.nested.en: A widget that holds tiles itself can’t go in a stack.
editor.stackThese.nested.context: Red notification (toast) when the selection to be stacked holds a widget that holds tiles itself (such as another Stack), which can’t go into a Stack. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.stackThese.noRoom.en: There’s no room for these tiles on the stack’s pages.
editor.stackThese.noRoom.context: Red notification (toast) when the tiles to be stacked don’t fit on the pages of the Stack, because the pages are too small for them. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.stackThese.nothing.context: Notification (toast) when the person asks for a Stack but there is no tile to put in it: the selected tiles are gone, or only headings were picked. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.stackThese.tooManyPages.en: A stack holds at most {max, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}}.
editor.stackThese.tooManyPages.context: Notification (toast) when the person tries to stack tiles so that the Stack would need more pages than it can hold (each tile on a page of its own). A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

params.max: The most pages a Stack can have. A number, 12.

editor.stylePanel.accent.context: Heading of the part of the Colour tab where the tile’s accent colour is chosen: the colour of its highlights.

editor.stylePanel.accentHint.en: Sliders, highlights and the glow shadow inside the tile.
editor.stylePanel.accentHint.context: Help text under the heading "Accent": what the accent colour is used for inside the tile.

editor.stylePanel.accentLabel.context: Screen reader label of the row of colour swatches that picks the accent colour. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.alignMixed.context: Small text next to the grid of places while the selected tiles have their content in different places.

editor.stylePanel.alignOwn.context: Small text next to the grid of places: the tile has its own place for its content, not the widget’s default.

editor.stylePanel.alignWidgetDefault.context: Small text next to the grid of places: the content sits where the widget puts it by itself, the tile has no place of its own.

editor.stylePanel.angle.context: Label in front of the slider that turns the direction of a gradient, in degrees. Short.

editor.stylePanel.backToTheme.context: Button at the bottom of the style panel: drops every change of the tile’s own look, so it follows the theme again.

editor.stylePanel.background.context: Heading of the part of the Colour tab where the tile’s background is chosen. Also the screen reader label of its choice buttons (Theme, Colour, Gradient, None).

editor.stylePanel.backgroundColour.context: Choice button of the Background control: a single flat colour. Short. Not the name of the tab.

editor.stylePanel.backgroundColourLabel.context: Screen reader label of the row of colour swatches that picks the background colour. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.border.context: Heading of the part of the Shape tab where the line around the tile is set (style, width and sides).

editor.stylePanel.borderColour.context: Screen reader label of the row of colour swatches that picks the colour of the border. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.cardOff.en: Only its content shows on the dashboard
editor.stylePanel.cardOff.context: Small text under the switch "A card behind it" while it is off: the tile shows no card, only the content.

editor.stylePanel.cardOn.context: Small text under the switch "A card behind it" while it is on: what the card consists of.

editor.stylePanel.cardTitle.context: Label of the switch at the top of the style panel. On, the tile has a card behind its content (background, border, shadow); off, only the content shows on the dashboard. Also its screen reader label.

editor.stylePanel.contentAlignmentLabel.context: Screen reader label of the grid of places where the content can sit. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.contentSits.context: Label above the 3 by 3 grid that sets where the content sits in the tile (top left, middle, bottom right…).

editor.stylePanel.contentSizeLabel.context: Screen reader label of the slider for the size of the tile’s content. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.copyStyle.context: Button at the bottom of the style panel: remembers the look of the tile so it can be pasted on other tiles from their menu.

editor.stylePanel.corners.context: Heading of the part of the Shape tab where the roundness of the tile’s corners is set.

editor.stylePanel.frostedGlass.context: Label of a switch: the tile’s background blurs what is behind it, like frosted glass. Also its screen reader label.

editor.stylePanel.glow.context: Label of a switch: a tile whose device is switched on glows around its edge. Also its screen reader label.

editor.stylePanel.gradient.context: Choice button of the Background control: a background that fades from one colour into another.

editor.stylePanel.gradientAngleLabel.context: Screen reader label of the slider that turns the direction of a gradient. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.gradientEndLabel.context: Screen reader label of the colour swatches that pick the last colour of a gradient. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.gradientFrom.context: Label in front of the colour swatches for the first colour of a gradient: the gradient starts from this colour. Very short.

editor.stylePanel.gradientStartLabel.context: Screen reader label of the colour swatches that pick the first colour of a gradient. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.gradientTo.context: Label in front of the colour swatches for the last colour of a gradient: the gradient ends in this colour. Very short.

editor.stylePanel.none.context: Choice button of the Background and Shadow controls: no background, or no shadow at all.

editor.stylePanel.padding.context: Label above the choice of how much empty space there is between the tile’s edge and its content. Also the screen reader label of the choice buttons.

editor.stylePanel.paddingFlush.context: Choice button of the Padding control: no space at all, the content touches the edge. Short.

editor.stylePanel.paddingNormal.context: Choice button of the Padding control: the usual amount of space around the content. Short.

editor.stylePanel.paddingRoomy.context: Choice button of the Padding control: a lot of space around the content. Short.

editor.stylePanel.paddingTight.context: Choice button of the Padding control: little space around the content. Short.

editor.stylePanel.picture.context: Name of the tab of the style panel between Colour and Content, where a picture from the web is put behind the tile’s content by pasting its web address.

editor.stylePanel.pictureAddress.context: Heading above the text field on the Picture tab where the web address (URL) of the picture is pasted. Short.

editor.stylePanel.pictureFill.context: Choice button: the picture fills the whole tile, and parts of it are cut off if its shape differs.

editor.stylePanel.pictureFit.context: Label in front of the choice of how the picture fits the tile (Fill or Whole). Short.

editor.stylePanel.pictureFitLabel.context: Screen reader label of the choice buttons Fill and Whole. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.pictureHint.en: Paste the web address of a picture to show it behind the content.
editor.stylePanel.pictureHint.context: Note under the picture’s address field: a link to an image on the web (no upload) is shown behind the tile’s content.

editor.stylePanel.pictureLoad.context: Button beside the picture’s address field: shows the picture from the address typed in the field on the selected tiles. A command.

editor.stylePanel.pictureMixed.en: The selected tiles have different pictures. A new address gives them all the same one.
editor.stylePanel.pictureMixed.context: Note under the picture’s address field when several tiles are selected and their pictures differ.

editor.stylePanel.pictureProblem.en: That isn’t a web address. Use one that starts with https://
editor.stylePanel.pictureProblem.context: Note under the picture’s address field when what was typed is not a web address. Keep https:// as it is.

editor.stylePanel.pictureStrengthLabel.context: Screen reader label of the slider for how strongly the picture shows over the tile’s background, from faint to full. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.pictureWhole.context: Choice button: the whole picture shows inside the tile, with empty room beside or above it if its shape differs.

editor.stylePanel.removePicture.context: Button that takes the picture away from the selected tiles.

editor.stylePanel.roundOuter.context: Button under the corners control, shown when several tiles are selected: only the corners on the outside of the group of selected tiles are rounded, the corners where tiles touch stay square.

editor.stylePanel.selection.en: {count, plural, one {Styling # tile · changes show right away} other {Styling # tiles · changes show right away}}
editor.stylePanel.selection.context: Small line at the top of the style panel: how many tiles are selected and that every change shows on the dashboard at once. Keep the · between the two parts.

params.count: How many tiles are selected, at least 1.

editor.stylePanel.shadow.context: Heading of the part of the Shape tab where the shadow under the tile is chosen. Also the screen reader label of its choice buttons.

editor.stylePanel.shadowGlow.context: Choice button of the Shadow control: a coloured glow around the tile instead of a dark shadow. Short.

editor.stylePanel.shadowLifted.context: Choice button of the Shadow control: a stronger shadow that makes the tile look lifted off the dashboard. Short.

editor.stylePanel.shadowSoft.context: Choice button of the Shadow control: a faint, spread-out shadow. Short.

editor.stylePanel.size.context: Label in front of the slider for the size of the tile’s content (a percentage). With "(mixed)" while the selected tiles have different sizes.

params.mixed: "yes" while the selected tiles have different sizes, otherwise "no".

editor.stylePanel.spacing.context: Heading of the part of the Content tab with the padding, where the content sits and its size.

editor.stylePanel.strength.context: Label in front of the slider for how strong the background colour is, from faint to solid (a percentage). Short.

editor.stylePanel.strengthLabel.context: Screen reader label of the slider for how strong the background colour is. Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.tabColour.context: Name of the second tab of the style panel, holding the background, frosted glass, glow and accent colour.

editor.stylePanel.tabContent.context: Name of the tab of the style panel after Picture, holding the padding, where the content sits in the tile and its size.

editor.stylePanel.tabPresets.context: Name of the tab of the style panel where saved looks (presets) are applied, saved and managed.

editor.stylePanel.tabShape.context: Name of the first tab of the style panel, holding corners, border and shadow: the form of the tile.

editor.stylePanel.tabsLabel.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs at the top of the style panel (Shape, Colour, Content…). Not shown.

editor.stylePanel.theme.context: Choice button of the Background and Shadow controls: use what the theme says, no change of the tile’s own. Short.

editor.stylePresetViews.colourName.en: {colour, select, own {own} accent {accent} lit {lit} cool {cool} good {good} warn {warn} danger {danger} text {text} surface {surface} canvas {canvas} chart1 {chart 1} chart2 {chart 2} chart3 {chart 3} chart4 {chart 4} chart5 {chart 5} other {chart 6}}
editor.stylePresetViews.colourName.context: The name of a colour as part of a phrase such as "Accent fill" or "Cool accent", lowercase. Accent is the theme’s highlight colour; lit is the colour of something switched on, such as a lamp; cool is a cold, blue tone; good, warn and danger are the colours for fine, careful and bad; text, surface and canvas are the colours of text, of cards and of the dashboard behind them; chart 1 to chart 6 are the colours of the series in charts. "own" means a colour the person typed as a hex code.

params.colour: Which colour: own, accent, lit, cool, good, warn, danger, text, surface, canvas, chart1 to chart6.

editor.stylePresetViews.defaultName.context: The name suggested for a new preset in its name field, before the person types another: "My preset". Also the base of the next suggestions, "My preset 2".

editor.stylePresetViews.defaultNameNumbe.context: The name suggested for a new preset when "My preset" is already taken: "My preset 2", "My preset 3"…

params.n: The number that makes the name unique, 2 or more.

editor.stylePresetViews.likeTheme.context: Description of a preset that changes nothing: tiles with it look like the theme says.

editor.stylePresetViews.nameRequired.context: Error under the name field of a preset when the name is empty: the person has to type one.

editor.stylePresetViews.nameTaken.en: You have a preset with this name
editor.stylePresetViews.nameTaken.context: Error under the name field of a preset when another preset of the person already has that name (capitals do not matter).

editor.stylePresetViews.nameTooLong.en: {max, plural, one {At most # character} other {At most # characters}}
editor.stylePresetViews.nameTooLong.context: Error under the name field of a preset when the name is too long: it may have at most this many characters.

params.max: The most characters a name may have.

editor.stylePresetViews.notUsed.context: Small line under a preset’s name: no tile uses this preset yet, on any dashboard.

editor.stylePresetViews.partAccent.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile’s accent colour, the colour of its highlights, such as "Cool accent". The first letter is made a capital by the program, so write the text in a form that works either way.

params.colour: The name of the colour, lowercase, translated.

editor.stylePresetViews.partBorder.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile has a border line, either an unbroken one or one made of dashes.

editor.stylePresetViews.partCorners.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: all corners have the same radius, given in pixels. Starts with a capital in English.

params.radius: The corner radius in pixels, a number from 0 to 48.

editor.stylePresetViews.partFill.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile’s background is one flat colour, such as "Accent fill". The first letter is made a capital by the program, so write the text in a form that works either way.

params.colour: The name of the colour, lowercase, translated.

editor.stylePresetViews.partGlass.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the frosted glass effect is on, where the background blurs what is behind it.

editor.stylePresetViews.partGradient.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile’s background fades from one colour into another.

editor.stylePresetViews.partNoBackground.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile has no background at all.

editor.stylePresetViews.partNoBorder.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile has no border line.

editor.stylePresetViews.partNoGlass.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the frosted glass effect is switched off for the tile.

editor.stylePresetViews.partNoGlow.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the glow around a tile whose device is on is switched off.

editor.stylePresetViews.partNoShadow.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile has no shadow.

editor.stylePresetViews.partOwnCorners.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the four corners have different radii, set one by one.

editor.stylePresetViews.partOwnPlace.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the content of the tile sits in a place of its own choice, not where the widget puts it.

editor.stylePresetViews.partPadding.en: {padding, select, none {Flush padding} tight {Tight padding} roomy {Roomy padding} other {Normal padding}}
editor.stylePresetViews.partPadding.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: how much empty space there is between the tile’s edge and its content. Flush is none at all, tight a little, normal the usual amount, roomy a lot.

editor.stylePresetViews.partPicture.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the tile shows a picture from the web behind its content.

editor.stylePresetViews.partShadow.en: {shadow, select, soft {Soft shadow} lifted {Lifted shadow} other {Glow shadow}}
editor.stylePresetViews.partShadow.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the kind of shadow the tile has. Soft is faint and spread out, lifted is stronger so the tile looks raised, glow is a coloured glow instead of a dark shadow.

editor.stylePresetViews.partSize.context: Part of a preset’s look in a few words: the content of the tile is shown at this percentage of its normal size.

params.percent: The size as a percentage, a number such as 110.

editor.stylePresetViews.usage.en: On {tiles, plural, one {# tile} other {# tiles}} · {dashboards, plural, one {# dashboard} other {# dashboards}}
editor.stylePresetViews.usage.context: Small line under a preset’s name: how many tiles use this preset and on how many dashboards those tiles are, such as "On 3 tiles · 2 dashboards". Keep the · between the two parts.

params.dashboards: How many dashboards those tiles are on, at least 1.
params.tiles: How many tiles use the preset, at least 1.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordAccent.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the accent colour, the colour of its highlights. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordBackground.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the background of the tile. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordBorder.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the line around the tile. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordCorners.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset, such as "corners, shadow and accent": the roundness of its corners. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordGlass.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the frosted glass effect, where the background blurs what is behind it. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordGlow.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the glow around a tile whose device is on. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordPadding.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the empty space between the edge and the content. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordPicture.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the picture from the web shown behind the tile’s content. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordPlace.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the place of the content inside the tile (top left, middle…). Lowercase.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordShadow.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the shadow under the tile. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresetViews.wordSize.context: One item in a list of what a tile changed on top of its preset: the size of the content. Lowercase, a noun.

editor.stylePresets.countOfMax.context: Small counter next to the heading "Your presets": how many presets the person has out of the most they may have, such as "3 of 50".

params.count: How many presets the person has.
params.max: The most presets a person may have.

editor.stylePresets.emptyBody.en: Save a tile’s look under a name, then give other tiles the same look in one tap, on any of your dashboards.
editor.stylePresets.emptyBody.context: Explanation in the empty state of the Presets tab: what presets are for, and that they work on every dashboard.

editor.stylePresets.emptyTitle.context: Bold title of the empty state of the Presets tab, shown while the person has saved no presets.

editor.stylePresets.full.en: {max, plural, one {You have # preset, the most there can be: delete it first.} other {You have # presets, the most there can be: delete one first.}}
editor.stylePresets.full.context: Small text under the Save button when the person has reached the most presets they may have. Says the limit and that one has to go first.

params.max: The most presets a person may have.

editor.stylePresets.newTitle.context: Heading above the little form where a new preset gets its name.

editor.stylePresets.notSavable.en: The selected tiles look different: select one to save its look.
editor.stylePresets.notSavable.context: Small text under the Save button, which is greyed out: several tiles with different looks are selected, so there is no single look to save.

editor.stylePresets.saveAs.context: Button that starts saving the look of the selected tile or tiles as a preset. The … says a name is asked next.

editor.stylePresets.savePreset.context: Button that keeps the name and saves the look of the selected tile or tiles as a new preset. Primary button of the little form that asks for the name.

editor.stylePresets.saves.en: {count, plural, one {Saves this tile’s look: shape, colour and content, not its CSS.} other {Saves the look the # tiles share: shape, colour and content, not their CSS.}}
editor.stylePresets.saves.context: Small text under the Save button: what a preset keeps of the selected tile or tiles: the settings of the Shape, Colour and Content tabs, but not the CSS typed for a tile.

params.count: How many tiles are selected, at least 1.

editor.stylePresets.tapHint.en: {count, plural, one {Tap one to give it to this tile. They stay linked: change the preset and they follow.} other {Tap one to give it to the # tiles. They stay linked: change the preset and they follow.}}
editor.stylePresets.tapHint.context: Help text above the list of presets: tapping a preset gives its look to the selected tile or tiles; they stay linked to the preset, so when the preset is changed they change too. "They" are the selected tiles.

params.count: How many tiles are selected, at least 1.

editor.stylePresets.yourPresets.context: Heading above the list of the person’s saved presets.

editor.summaryTap.allOff.context: Choice in the dropdown "Switch to" for a chip that counts several devices: all of them turn off.

editor.summaryTap.allOn.context: Choice in the dropdown "Switch to" for a chip that counts several devices: all of them turn on.

editor.summaryTap.askBefore.context: Checkbox under the summary chip’s tap settings: when ticked, tapping asks "are you sure" before the devices are switched.

editor.summaryTap.off.context: Choice in the dropdown "Switch to" for a chip that shows one value (such as one lamp): it turns off.

editor.summaryTap.on.context: Choice in the dropdown "Switch to" for a chip that shows one value (such as one lamp): it turns on.

editor.summaryTap.switchTo.context: Label of a dropdown under the tap choice that switches a summary’s devices: whether they are turned on or off. Read as "Switch to [On]".

editor.tabSearch.elsewhere.context: Button under the line "Nothing in … matches", pointing at another tab that has matches for the search. It switches to that tab. For example: 3 in Other.

params.count: How many matches that tab has. A number.
params.tab: The label of the other tab, such as "Other". Already translated.

editor.tabSearch.none.context: Line in a list with tabs (such as the add-widgets window) when the person typed a search and the open tab has no match. For example: Nothing in Devices matches “clock”.

params.query: What the person typed in the search box. Not translated.
params.tab: The label of the open tab, such as "Devices" or "Flows". Already translated.

editor.tapActions.camera.context: Tap action: open a camera’s image.

editor.tapActions.dashboard.context: Tap action: go to another dashboard.

editor.tapActions.device.context: Tap action: open the device’s details.

editor.tapActions.flow.context: Tap action: start a Homey flow (an automation).

editor.tapActions.history.context: Tap action: show the history of the reading.

editor.tapActions.mood.context: Tap action: set a Homey mood (a scene).

editor.tapActions.variable.context: Tap action: set a Homey variable to a value.

editor.tapActions.widget.context: Tap action: whatever the widget itself does on a tap.

editor.tapChoices.defaultHint.context: Small grey note beside the tap choice that applies until another is picked: this is what the part does by default.

editor.tapChoices.designerOffers.context: Help line under the tap dropdown of a part that offers only some of the tap choices: it names them. For example: The widget’s designer offers show the history or open a dashboard here.

params.actions: The offered tap choices, joined by commas and "or", already lower-case: "show the history or open a dashboard". Taken from the widget’s English choice names for now.

editor.tapChoices.noCamera.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Open the camera": the device has no camera, picture or video.

editor.tapChoices.noDevice.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Open device": the part or tile has no device yet.

editor.tapChoices.noFlows.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Start a flow": the Homey has no flow that can be started by hand. A flow is a Homey automation.

editor.tapChoices.noLongerOffered.context: Small grey note beside a stored tap choice that the widget’s designer no longer offers for this part. It stays visible, greyed out, so it can be seen and changed.

editor.tapChoices.noMoods.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Set a mood": the Homey has no moods (scenes).

editor.tapChoices.noOtherDashboards.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Open a dashboard": there is no other dashboard to open.

editor.tapChoices.noReading.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Show the history": this part has no reading that has a history.

editor.tapChoices.noVariables.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Set a variable": the Homey has no Logic variables that can be changed. Logic is the Homey name for its variables.

editor.tapChoices.nothingToSwitch.context: Small grey note beside the greyed-out tap choice "Switch it on or off": this part has no device or reading that can be switched on and off.

editor.tapChoices.partDoesNothing.en: This part does nothing, or what its designer chose.
editor.tapChoices.partDoesNothing.context: Help line under the tap dropdown of a part of a widget whose designer allows no tap choices: tapping it does nothing, or the one thing the designer fixed.

editor.tapSettings.dashboard.context: Label of a dropdown under a tap choice: which dashboard to open when the part is tapped, or when a summary chip is tapped.

editor.tapSettings.device.context: Label of a dropdown under the tap choice "Open device": which device opens. It offers the tile’s own device first, then the others.

editor.tapSettings.mood.context: Label of a dropdown under the tap choice "Set a mood": which mood (a Homey scene) to switch on. "Mood" is the Homey name for it.

editor.tapSettings.openAs.context: Label of a dropdown under a tap choice: how a dashboard or device opens (as the page, a popup, a side panel or full screen). The choices read as "Open as a popup" and so on.

editor.tapSettings.over.context: Label of a dropdown under the tap choice "Show the history": the period the history covers, such as 24 hours or 7 days. Read as "Over [24 hours]".

editor.tapSettings.ownDevice.context: First choice in the dropdown "Device" of a tap that opens a device: the device the tile already shows, so no other is picked. The name follows in brackets.

params.name: The name of the tile’s device, such as "Bedroom lamp". Not translated.

editor.tapSettings.reading.context: Label of a dropdown under the tap choice "Show the history": which reading of the device the history is shown for, such as temperature or power.

editor.tapSettings.whatToSwitch.context: Label of a dropdown under the tap choice "Switch it on or off", shown when the device has more than one on/off reading: which one is switched.

editor.tapSettings.whenTapped.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what happens when a part of a tile is tapped, when the part gives no name of its own for the gesture.

editor.tileCss.atRuleNotAllowed.en: @{name} is not allowed in a tile’s CSS
editor.tileCss.atRuleNotAllowed.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it uses an at-rule (a rule that starts with @) that is not allowed, such as @namespace. The @ and the name stay as they are.

params.name: The name of the at-rule, without the @. Not translated.

editor.tileCss.badgeWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .badge reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: a small label bubble, such as a count or a status.

editor.tileCss.bigWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .big reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the large number or title a widget shows.

editor.tileCss.closeWithoutOpen.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: a closing curly bracket has no opening one before it. Keep the two brackets as they are; in the message they are written between apostrophes (quoted), keep that too.

editor.tileCss.headWhat.en: The row with the name and icon
editor.tileCss.headWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .head reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the top row of a widget with its name and icon.

editor.tileCss.hintWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .hint reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: small text in a fainter colour than the usual small text.

editor.tileCss.hostWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook :host reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the whole widget inside the tile.

editor.tileCss.iconWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .icon reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the icon of the widget.

editor.tileCss.labelWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .label reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the small text a widget shows.

editor.tileCss.nameWhat.en: What it shows, like a device’s name
editor.tileCss.nameWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .name reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the main text of the widget, for example the name of a device.

editor.tileCss.noEscapes.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it contains a backslash, which can hide forbidden words, so names must be written out in full. Keep the (\) as it is.

editor.tileCss.noFixed.en: No position: fixed: the CSS stays on its tile
editor.tileCss.noFixed.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it uses "position: fixed", which would pull content out of the tile. Keep "position: fixed" as it is.

editor.tileCss.noFontFace.en: Fonts come from the theme, not from a tile
editor.tileCss.noFontFace.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it declares a font with @font-face, but only the theme chooses fonts.

editor.tileCss.noHtml.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it contains HTML tags such as style or script; only CSS may be typed here.

editor.tileCss.noImport.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it uses @import, which loads other CSS, and that is not allowed. Keep @import as it is.

editor.tileCss.noScript.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it contains something that could run a script, which is not allowed.

editor.tileCss.noUrl.en: No url(): a tile loads nothing from elsewhere
editor.tileCss.noUrl.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it uses url(), image-set() or src(), which load a file from elsewhere, and that is not allowed. Keep url() as it is.

editor.tileCss.onlyThisTile.en: Only this tile: no :root, html, body or :host-context
editor.tileCss.onlyThisTile.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it tries to style the page outside the tile with :root, html, body or :host-context, and the CSS may only reach its own tile. Keep those four names as they are.

editor.tileCss.openNotClosed.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: an opening curly bracket is never closed. Keep the bracket as it is; in the message it is written between apostrophes (quoted), keep that too.

editor.tileCss.size.en: {lines, plural, =0 {No CSS} one {# line} other {# lines}}
editor.tileCss.size.context: Small line under a tile’s name in the list of selected tiles: how many lines of CSS the tile has, or that it has none.

params.lines: How many lines of CSS (empty lines not counted), 0 for none.

editor.tileCss.stateWhat.en: Its state, like On or Open
editor.tileCss.stateWhat.context: Short description of what the CSS hook .state reaches, shown as a tooltip on its button: the state a widget shows in words, such as On or Open.

editor.tileCss.tooLong.en: {max, plural, one {At most # character} other {At most # characters}}
editor.tileCss.tooLong.context: Problem found in the CSS typed for a tile: it is longer than the limit. The size counter below the editor shows how long it is.

params.max: The most characters a tile’s CSS may have, a number such as 4,000.

editor.tileCssEditor.checkedOnSave.en: Checked again when it is saved.
editor.tileCssEditor.checkedOnSave.context: Small help text under the code editor: the server checks the CSS once more when the dashboard is saved.

editor.tileCssEditor.clear.context: Button at the bottom of the CSS tab: remove all the CSS typed for the selected tile.

editor.tileCssEditor.editorLabel.context: Screen reader label of the code editor in which the tile’s CSS is typed.

params.label: The name of the selected tile. Not translated.

editor.tileCssEditor.hooksHint.en: Class names in every widget that stay as they are. Tap one to add a rule for it.
editor.tileCssEditor.hooksHint.context: Help text under the heading "Hooks": these CSS class names exist in every widget and will not change; tapping a chip adds an empty CSS rule for it to the editor.

editor.tileCssEditor.hooksTitle.context: Heading above the chips with CSS class names (hooks) that every widget keeps. Short.

editor.tileCssEditor.intro.en: Reaches only {label}’s widget, after the theme’s CSS. Use the theme’s variables (--hd-*) and the hooks below.
editor.tileCssEditor.intro.context: Help text under the heading "CSS for this tile": the CSS typed here only affects the widget of the selected tile, and is applied after the theme’s CSS. It points to the theme’s CSS variables and to the hooks (class names) listed further down. Keep the text inside … exactly as it is.

params.label: The name of the selected tile, such as "Living room lamp". Not translated.

editor.tileCssEditor.line.context: Button in the list of CSS problems: it jumps to the line of the CSS where the problem is. Followed by the number of the line, such as "Line 4".

editor.tileCssEditor.live.context: Status under the code editor: the CSS has no problems and is on the tile now.

editor.tileCssEditor.none.context: Status under the code editor while nothing has been typed.

editor.tileCssEditor.notLive.en: Not on the tile until it’s fixed: it keeps the last CSS without problems
editor.tileCssEditor.notLive.context: Status under the code editor while the typed CSS has problems: the tile does not use the new CSS yet and keeps the last version that was fine.

editor.tileCssEditor.title.context: Heading of the CSS tab of the style panel when one tile is selected.

editor.tileCssSelection.body.en: Each tile shows its own widget, so its CSS is written for that tile alone. Pick one to write its CSS. To give tiles the same CSS, copy that tile’s style and paste it on the others.
editor.tileCssSelection.body.context: Explanation under the heading "CSS is per tile": why the CSS is written per tile, what to do (pick one tile from the list below) and how to give several tiles the same CSS (copy the style of one tile and paste it on the others, using Copy style and the tile menu).

editor.tileCssSelection.edit.context: Button on a row of the list of selected tiles: narrow the selection to that tile and open its CSS editor.

editor.tileCssSelection.title.context: Heading of the CSS tab of the style panel when several tiles are selected: CSS cannot be written for all of them at once.

editor.tileMap.alsoOn.context: Label of the group where more places can be marked on the map besides the tile’s own device: home and other devices.

editor.tileMap.fadeHint.en: Soft shows most of the map; strong keeps it quiet behind the numbers.
editor.tileMap.fadeHint.context: Small grey text under the choice "How much shows through". Soft and strong are the names of two of its options: write them as those options, in lower case if the language allows.

editor.tileMap.fadeLabel.context: Label of the three-way choice of how strongly the map shows through behind the tile’s content: Soft, Medium or Strong. It also is the screen reader label.

editor.tileMap.fadeMedium.context: Second option of "How much shows through": a middle amount of the map shows.

editor.tileMap.fadeSoft.context: First option of "How much shows through": a gentle fade, so most of the map shows.

editor.tileMap.fadeStrong.context: Third option of "How much shows through": the map is faded strongly and stays quiet behind the numbers.

editor.tileMap.home.context: Label of the checkbox that adds the home (the Homey’s own place) as a mark on the map.

editor.tileMap.lookDark.context: Third option of "Map style": always a dark map.

editor.tileMap.lookLight.context: Second option of "Map style": always a light map.

editor.tileMap.lookStreets.context: Fourth option of "Map style": a colourful street map with many details, not tied to the theme.

editor.tileMap.lookTheme.context: First option of "Map style": the map follows the dashboard’s theme (light or dark). A theme is a set of colours.

editor.tileMap.mapBehind.context: Bold title of the on/off switch of the map behind a tile, and its screen reader label. "It" is the tile.

editor.tileMap.mapBehindHint.en: Where {deviceName} is, faded behind the tile.
editor.tileMap.mapBehindHint.context: Small grey text under the switch "A map behind it": the map shows the place of the tile’s device, faded behind the tile’s content.

params.deviceName: The name of the tile’s device, such as "Car". Not translated.

editor.tileMap.noOtherPlaces.en: No other places: devices that say where they are show up here.
editor.tileMap.noOtherPlaces.context: Small grey text in the group "Also on the map" when there is nothing to add: no other device reports its location and the Homey shares no home place.

editor.tileMap.streetNames.context: Bold title of the on/off switch that shows names on the map, and its screen reader label.

editor.tileMap.streetNamesHint.en: Names of streets and places on the map.
editor.tileMap.streetNamesHint.context: Small grey text under the switch "Street names".

editor.tileMap.styleLabel.context: Label of the four-way choice of how the map looks (Theme, Light, Dark or Streets), and its screen reader label.

editor.tileMap.zoomLabel.context: Label of the three-way choice of how far the map is zoomed out around the device: Street, Neighbourhood or Town. It also is the screen reader label.

editor.tileMap.zoomNeighbourhood.context: Second option of "How much around it": the map shows the neighbourhood around the device. In a narrow switch next to Street and Town.

editor.tileMap.zoomStreet.context: First option of "How much around it": the map is zoomed in to show the street around the device.

editor.tileMap.zoomTown.context: Third option of "How much around it": the map is zoomed out to show the whole town around the device.

editor.tileMeters.follow.context: Button in the note: makes every part of this tile follow the energy settings’ meters again.

editor.tileMeters.followsBody.en: The parts are the meters set under Settings › Energy, read as power. Change one here and it is this tile’s own.
editor.tileMeters.followsBody.context: Text of the note when every part follows the meters: the tile shows the energy settings’ meters as power, and changing a part here makes it the tile’s own.

editor.tileMeters.followsTitle.context: Bold line of the note when every part of this Energy flow tile follows the meters of the energy settings.

editor.tileMeters.meters.context: Button in the note that opens the energy settings, where the meters are set.

editor.tileMeters.ownBody.en: {count, plural, one {{parts} is this tile’s own; the rest follow your meters.} other {{parts} are this tile’s own; the rest follow your meters.}}
editor.tileMeters.ownBody.context: Text of the note naming the parts changed on this tile, such as "Solar and Battery are this tile’s own".

params.count: How many parts are the tile’s own.
params.parts: The names of the parts, already joined as a list ("Solar and Battery").

editor.tileMeters.ownTitle.context: Bold line of the note when some parts of this Energy flow tile were changed on the tile and no longer follow the energy settings’ meters.

editor.tileSettings.saveFailed.context: Message (toast, a short message that slides in at a corner and fades) in red after saving the settings of a tile failed. A reason may be given by the server instead.

editor.tileSettings.thatWidget.context: A short name for a widget, in lower case, used inside the question that asks to confirm changing tiles to another widget, such as "Change to that widget?". Used when the name of the widget is not known to the app. Not a sentence.

editor.tileSettings.widgetName.context: Title of the settings dialog of a tile whose widget has no name known to the app. A widget is the design that shows a tile. Rarely seen.

editor.tileShowing.empty.context: Reason shown on a dimmed tile in edit mode, after "Hidden now": the tile’s widget has nothing to show at the moment (for example a list with no entries), and the tile is set to hide itself then. Short.

editor.tileShowing.notWhile.context: Reason shown on a dimmed tile in edit mode, after "Hidden now": the tile is set to show only while a condition holds, and it does not hold. The condition is a short phrase that says it, such as "someone is home" or "the Kitchen light is turned on", so the whole reads "Not while someone is home".

params.condition: The condition that does not hold, as a short phrase such as "someone is home". Built by the app from the tile’s settings, and still English.

editor.tileStage.empty.context: Text on the stage of the style dialog when no tile is selected: the person should select tiles on the dashboard to change their style. A command.

editor.tileStage.livePreview.context: Small label in the corner of a stage that shows the selected tiles as they look right now, with live values and the style being edited.

editor.tilesField.arrange.context: Small button in a Tiles setting of a tile’s settings. It opens a window where the tiles inside the widget are made, placed and styled.

editor.tilesField.namesMore.context: Small line under the summary of a Tiles setting that lists the names of the first tiles it holds and says how many more there are, such as "Lamp, Thermostat, Blinds, Door and 5 more".

params.count: How many more tiles there are. A number.
params.names: The names of the first four tiles, separated by commas. Not translated.

editor.tilesField.onDashboard.en: Double-click the stack while editing the dashboard to arrange them.
editor.tilesField.onDashboard.context: Small help text in the settings of a Stack widget (a tile that shows other tiles as pages) in place of an Arrange button: the tiles of a stack are arranged on the dashboard itself. "Them" are the tiles inside the stack.

editor.tilesWouldGo.changeConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to change a tile to another widget even though the tiles inside it would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.changeTitle.en: {widgets, plural, one {Change to {name}?} other {Change # tiles to {name}?}}
editor.tilesWouldGo.changeTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person changed what a tile shows to another widget, and the tile (or several tiles at once) would lose the tiles inside it. The question ends with a question mark.

params.name: The name of the widget they would become. Not translated.
params.widgets: How many tiles are changed. A number, at least 1.

editor.tilesWouldGo.deleteConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to delete a widget even though tiles inside it would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.deleteTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person deletes one of their widgets, and tiles inside widgets on dashboards that use it would go.

params.name: The name of the widget being deleted. Not translated.

editor.tilesWouldGo.goes.en: {tiles, plural, one {{widgets, plural, one {The tile inside it goes.} other {The tile inside them goes.}}} other {{widgets, plural, one {The {tiles, number} tiles inside it go.} other {The {tiles, number} tiles inside them go.}}}}
editor.tilesWouldGo.goes.context: Last sentence of the description of a confirmation dialog: the change would make widgets that hold tiles (such as a Stack) lose the tiles inside them, and says how many. Follows a sentence that says why, when there is one. "It" is the one widget, "them" are several.

params.tiles: How many tiles would go. A number, at least 1.
params.widgets: How many widgets they are in. A number, at least 1.

editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOffConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to stop using the person’s own widget in place of the built-in one even though tiles inside would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOffReason.en: The built-in widget has no such Tiles setting.
editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOffReason.context: First sentence of the description of the confirmation dialog for no longer using one’s own widget in place of the built-in one: the built-in widget has no Tiles setting (the part of the settings that holds tiles inside the widget). The sentence about which tiles go comes after it.

editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOffTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person turns off using their own widget in place of the built-in one, and the built-in widget has no Tiles setting, so tiles inside widgets on dashboards would go.

params.name: The name of their own widget. Not translated.

editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOnConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to use the person’s own widget instead of the built-in one even though tiles inside would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOnReason.en: It has no such Tiles setting.
editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOnReason.context: First sentence of the description of the confirmation dialog for using one’s own widget instead of the built-in one: "It" is the person’s own widget, which has no Tiles setting (the part of the settings that holds tiles inside the widget). The sentence about which tiles go comes after it.

editor.tilesWouldGo.insteadOnTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person turns on using their own widget instead of the built-in one of the same name, and their widget has no Tiles setting, so tiles inside widgets on dashboards would go.

params.name: The name of their own widget. Not translated.

editor.tilesWouldGo.restoreConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to go back to an earlier save of a widget even though tiles inside it would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.restoreReason.en: That save has no such Tiles setting.
editor.tilesWouldGo.restoreReason.context: First sentence of the description of the confirmation dialog for going back to an earlier save of a widget: that save has no Tiles setting (the part of the settings that holds tiles inside the widget) like the widget has now. The sentence about which tiles go comes after it.

editor.tilesWouldGo.restoreTitle.en: Go back to this save of {name}?
editor.tilesWouldGo.restoreTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person goes back to an earlier save of one of their widgets, and that save has no Tiles setting, so tiles inside widgets on dashboards would go.

params.name: The name of the widget. Not translated.

editor.tilesWouldGo.saveConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to save a widget even though tiles inside it, on dashboards, would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.saveReason.en: This save leaves out a Tiles setting.
editor.tilesWouldGo.saveReason.context: First sentence of the description of the confirmation dialog for saving a widget: the new save has no Tiles setting (the part of the settings that holds tiles inside the widget). The sentence about which tiles go comes after it.

editor.tilesWouldGo.saveTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person saves a widget of their own in the widget editor, and the save leaves out a Tiles setting, so tiles inside widgets on dashboards would go.

params.name: The name of the widget being saved. Not translated.

editor.tilesWouldGo.uninstallConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to uninstall a community widget even though tiles inside it would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.uninstallTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person uninstalls a widget they installed from the community, and tiles inside widgets on dashboards that use it would go.

params.name: The name of the community widget. Not translated.

editor.tilesWouldGo.versionConfirm.context: Confirm button of the dialog that asks whether to move a community widget to another version even though tiles inside it would go. A command.

editor.tilesWouldGo.versionReason.en: That version leaves out a Tiles setting.
editor.tilesWouldGo.versionReason.context: First sentence of the description of the confirmation dialog for changing the version of a community widget: that version has no Tiles setting (the part of the settings that holds tiles inside the widget). The sentence about which tiles go comes after it.

editor.tilesWouldGo.versionTitle.context: Title of a confirmation dialog: the person moves a widget installed from the community to another version, and that version leaves out a Tiles setting, so tiles inside widgets on dashboards would go.

params.name: The name of the community widget. Not translated.

editor.timelineValues.failedText.en: Your Homey didn’t answer. Try again in a moment.
editor.timelineValues.failedText.context: Text under the note title when the Homey did not answer the request for its Timeline.

editor.timelineValues.failedTitle.context: Bold title of a note in the Timeline tab when the Homey did not answer.

editor.timelineValues.forbiddenText.en: Tiledash may not see your Homey’s timeline yet. Log in again and allow it (homey.notifications.readonly).
editor.timelineValues.forbiddenText.context: Text under the note title when Tiledash has no permission to read the Homey’s Timeline. Logging in again asks the Homey for it. Keep the permission name in brackets exactly as it is: homey.notifications.readonly.

editor.timelineValues.forbiddenTitle.context: Bold title of a note in the Timeline tab when Tiledash has no permission to read the Homey’s Timeline (its notifications). Use the name the Homey app gives the Timeline in your language.

editor.timelineValues.loadingTitle.context: Bold title shown in the Timeline tab while the Homey is still being asked for it.

editor.timelineValues.nothingText.en: This place takes neither text nor a number.
editor.timelineValues.nothingText.context: Text under "Nothing that fits" in the Timeline tab: the place where the value is picked takes no text and no number.

editor.timelineValues.nothingTitle.context: Bold title of a note in the Timeline tab when none of its values fit the place where a value is picked.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.addFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when adding tiles to a widget that holds tiles did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.addPage.context: Button in the notification that says there is no room on a page of a Stack: it opens the dialog to add another page. A command. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.addPageFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when adding a page to a Stack (or similar widget) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.added.en: {count, plural, one {Tile added} other {# tiles added}}
editor.useChildTilesWindow.added.context: Notification (toast) after tiles were added to a widget that holds tiles, such as a page of a Stack.

params.count: How many tiles were added. A number, at least 1.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.moveFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when moving a page of a Stack to the left or right, or dragging it to another place among the pages, did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.moved.en: {count, plural, one {Moved to {page}} other {# tiles moved to {page}}}
editor.useChildTilesWindow.moved.context: Notification (toast) after tiles were moved to another page of a Stack (or similar widget with pages).

params.count: How many tiles were moved. A number, at least 1.
params.page: The name of the page they went to. The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.noRoomLeft.context: Warning notification (toast) when tiles could not be added to a widget that holds tiles (without pages) because its grid has no free spot for them.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.noRoomOnPage.context: Warning notification (toast) when tiles could not be added or moved to a page of a Stack (or similar widget) because its grid has no free spot for them. An Add a page button may sit next to it.

params.page: The name of the page. The owner’s own name, not translated.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.noRoomToResto.en: No room to put them back
editor.useChildTilesWindow.noRoomToResto.context: Warning notification (toast) when the Undo of removing tiles from a widget could not put them back, because the page they were on has no room for them any more.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.nothingToAdd.context: Warning notification (toast) when the person closed the widget picker while adding tiles to a widget, with nothing chosen.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.removeFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when removing tiles from a widget that holds tiles did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.removePageFai.context: Red notification (toast) when removing a page of a Stack (or similar widget) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.removed.en: {count, plural, one {Tile removed} other {# tiles removed}}
editor.useChildTilesWindow.removed.context: Notification (toast) after tiles were removed from a widget that holds tiles, such as a Stack. An Undo button next to it makes them again.

params.count: How many tiles were removed. A number, at least 1.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.renameFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when changing the name or icon of a page of a Stack (or similar widget) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.restoreFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when putting tiles back into a widget (the Undo of removing them, or of taking them out) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.setupFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when opening the tiles window of a widget with pages (such as a Stack) failed while making its first page, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.takeOutFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when taking tiles out of a widget back onto the dashboard did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.takenOut.en: {count, plural, one {Tile back on the dashboard} other {# tiles back on the dashboard}}
editor.useChildTilesWindow.takenOut.context: Notification (toast) after tiles were taken out of a widget that holds tiles (such as a Stack) and put back on the dashboard itself. An Undo button next to it puts them into the widget again.

params.count: How many tiles were taken out. A number, at least 1.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.undo.context: Button in a notification (toast) after tiles were removed from a widget’s page or taken out of it, back to the dashboard. It makes the removal undone. A command.

editor.useChildTilesWindow.whenFailed.en: Couldn’t save when the page shows.
editor.useChildTilesWindow.whenFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when saving the When to show settings of a page of a Stack (the conditions that decide when the page is shown) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.usePutInto.noRoom.context: Warning notification (toast) when the selected tiles were not put into a widget that holds tiles because there is no room for all of them there. Nothing was moved.

params.where: The place they should have gone: the widget’s name, and its setting and page when it has them, joined with ›. The owner’s own names, not translated. Or the words "that widget" (translated).

editor.usePutInto.putFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when putting tiles into a widget that holds tiles did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost. The person can try again.

editor.usePutInto.putInto.en: {count, plural, one {Tile put into {where}} other {# tiles put into {where}}}
editor.usePutInto.putInto.context: Notification (toast) after the person put the selected tiles into a widget that holds tiles, such as a Stack. An Undo button next to it takes them out again.

params.count: How many tiles were put in. A number, at least 1.
params.where: The place they went: the widget’s name, and its setting and page when it has them, joined with ›, such as "Ground floor › Page 2". The owner’s own names, not translated. Or the words "that widget" (translated).

editor.usePutInto.takeOutFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when taking tiles out of a widget that holds tiles (the Undo of putting them in) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost.

editor.usePutInto.thatWidget.context: Stands where the place’s name would be in "Tile put into …" and "No room in …" when the place has no name Tiledash can show. It reads as the end of those sentences: "Tile put into that widget".

editor.usePutInto.undo.context: Button in the notification (toast) after tiles were put into a widget. It takes them out again, back on the dashboard. A command.

editor.useStackThese.added.context: Notification (toast) after the person made a new Stack from the widgets they picked in the widget picker; each pick fills a page of the stack. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.useStackThese.stacked.en: {count, plural, one {Tile stacked} other {# tiles stacked}}
editor.useStackThese.stacked.context: Notification (toast) after the person put the selected tiles into a new Stack. An Undo button next to it puts the tiles back where they were. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

params.count: How many tiles were stacked. A number, at least 1.

editor.useStackThese.undo.context: Button in the notification (toast) after tiles were stacked. It puts the tiles back on the dashboard where they were. A command.

editor.useStackThese.unstackFailed.context: Red notification (toast) when taking tiles out of a Stack again (the Undo of stacking them) did not work, for example because the connection to Tiledash was lost. A stack is a tile that holds several tiles as pages.

editor.valueField.clear.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button next to a value field that removes the picked value and leaves the field empty. Used for optional values.

params.label: What the field is for, such as "Value". Comes from the screen, already translated where possible.

editor.valueField.labelEmpty.context: Screen reader label of a value field that has nothing picked yet, not visible as text. It says what the field is for, then the invitation to pick a value, such as "Show when: Pick a value".

params.label: What the field is for, such as "Value". Comes from the screen, already translated where possible.
params.placeholder: The invitation shown in the empty field, such as "Pick a value". Already translated.

editor.valueField.labelPicked.context: Screen reader label of a value field that has a value picked, not visible as text. It says what the field is for, then the name of the picked value and where it comes from, such as "Show when: Temperature, Bedroom · Bedroom climate".

params.from: Where the value comes from, such as "Bedroom · Bedroom climate" or "Variable · Number". Already translated.
params.label: What the field is for, such as "Value". Comes from the screen, already translated where possible.
params.title: The name of the picked value, such as "Temperature". Not translated.

editor.valueField.pick.context: Text in an empty value field, on the line where a picked value is shown, inviting the person to open the picker and choose a value for this place on a tile (a reading of a device, a variable or an energy value).

editor.valuePicker.chooseMeters.context: Small button under the "No energy meters yet" text in the value picker. It opens the place where the energy meters are chosen.

editor.valuePicker.groupNumbers.context: Heading over the Logic variables in the value picker that hold a number. Plural: a group of variables.

editor.valuePicker.groupText.context: Heading over the Logic variables in the value picker that hold a piece of text.

editor.valuePicker.groupYesNo.context: Heading over the Logic variables in the value picker that hold a yes or no (on or off) value.

editor.valuePicker.inTextDevices.context: The Devices tab of the value picker named inside the sentence "Search devices and variables", in lower case. Used only to build the placeholder of the search box.

editor.valuePicker.inTextEnergy.context: The Energy tab of the value picker named inside the sentence "Search devices and energy", in lower case. Used only to build the placeholder of the search box.

editor.valuePicker.inTextPeople.context: The People tab of the value picker named inside a sentence such as "Search devices and people", in lower case. Used only to build the placeholder of the search box.

editor.valuePicker.inTextPrices.context: The Prices tab of the value picker named inside the sentence "Search energy and prices", in lower case. Used only to build the placeholder of the search box.

editor.valuePicker.inTextTimeline.context: The Timeline tab of the value picker named inside a sentence such as "Search devices and timeline", in lower case. Used only to build the placeholder of the search box.

editor.valuePicker.inTextVariables.context: The Variables tab of the value picker named inside the sentence "Search devices and variables", in lower case. Used only to build the placeholder of the search box.

editor.valuePicker.noMetersText.en: Pick which devices measure your electricity, solar, gas and water.
editor.valuePicker.noMetersText.context: Help text under the heading "No energy meters yet" in the value picker. Meters are devices that measure how much electricity, solar power, gas and water is used.
