editor.valuePicker.noMetersTitle.context: Bold heading in the Energy tab of the value picker when no energy meters are chosen yet. A help text and a button follow below it.

editor.valuePicker.noPricesText.en: Choose where your prices come from: Homey’s own, the day-ahead market or a fixed tariff.
editor.valuePicker.noPricesText.context: Help text under the heading "No prices yet" in the value picker. It lists the ways to get energy prices: the Homey’s own prices, the day-ahead market (the next day’s wholesale prices) or a fixed tariff.

editor.valuePicker.noPricesTitle.context: Bold heading in the Prices tab of the value picker when no price source is set up yet. A help text and a button follow below it.

editor.valuePicker.noRoom.context: Heading over the devices of the value picker that are not in any room (zone) of the Homey. Other headings are the names of rooms.

editor.valuePicker.readingsCount.context: Small grey text on a folded device in the value picker when it does not show live values: how many readings the device has. A reading is a value of a device, such as its temperature or whether it is on.

params.count: How many readings the device has. A number.

editor.valuePicker.searchDevices.context: Placeholder text in the search box at the top of the value picker when it only offers the readings of devices. A reading is a value of a device, such as its temperature.

editor.valuePicker.searchEverything.context: Placeholder text in the search box at the top of the value picker when it has three or more tabs. The search covers every tab.

editor.valuePicker.searchTabs.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs (Devices, Variables, Energy, Prices, People) at the top of the value picker. Not visible as text.

editor.valuePicker.searchTwo.context: Placeholder text in the search box at the top of the value picker when it has two tabs, such as "Search devices and variables". The search covers both.

params.first: The name of the first tab in lower case, such as "devices". Already translated.
params.second: The name of the second tab in lower case, such as "variables". Already translated.

editor.valuePicker.searchVariables.context: Placeholder text in the search box at the top of the value picker when it only offers the Homey’s Logic variables.

editor.valuePicker.setupPrices.context: Small button under the "No prices yet" text in the value picker. It opens the place where the price source is chosen.

editor.valuePicker.tabDevices.context: Name of a tab of the value picker that lists the readings of the Homey’s devices, such as the temperature of a thermostat.

editor.valuePicker.tabEnergy.context: Name of a tab of the value picker that lists the Homey’s energy values, such as the electricity used now or today.

editor.valuePicker.tabPeople.context: Name of a tab of the value picker that lists values about the people of the home, such as who is home.

editor.valuePicker.tabPrices.context: Name of a tab of the value picker that lists energy price values, such as the current electricity price.

editor.valuePicker.tabTimeline.context: Name of a tab of the value picker that lists values from the Homey’s Timeline (its notifications), such as the latest entry. Use the name the Homey app gives the Timeline in your language.

editor.valuePicker.tabVariables.context: Name of a tab of the value picker that lists the Homey’s Logic variables: values that Flows (the Homey’s automations) keep, such as a mode or a count.

editor.valueSource.device.context: Small line under the name of a picked reading that is gone: it says the value was a reading of a device.

editor.valueSource.energy.context: Small line under the name of a picked energy value, such as the electricity you use. It says what group the value is in. Also used before a dot, in "Energy · Electricity".

editor.valueSource.fromHost.context: Small line under the name of a picked energy or price value that says where it comes from: the kind (Energy or Prices) and the group it is in, such as "Energy · Electricity". The dot with spaces around it stays.

params.group: The group of the value, such as Electricity. Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.valueSource.fromVariable.context: Small line under the name of a picked Logic variable that says where the value comes from: a variable, and what kind it is. The dot with spaces around it separates the two parts and stays.

params.type: The kind of the variable: Yes/no, Number or Text. Already translated.

editor.valueSource.hostGone.context: Name shown in a value field in place of an energy or price value that was picked once but is no longer available. It is marked as a problem. Under it the word "Energy" is shown.

editor.valueSource.prices.context: Small line under the name of a picked price value, such as the current electricity price. It says what group the value is in. Used before a dot, in "Prices · Electricity".

editor.valueSource.readingGone.context: Name shown in a value field in place of a reading of a device (such as its temperature) that was picked once but no longer exists on the Homey, because the device or the reading is gone. It is marked as a problem. Under it the word "Device" is shown.

editor.valueSource.typeNumber.context: The kind of a Logic variable that holds a number. Shown after "Variable · " under a picked value.

editor.valueSource.typeText.context: The kind of a Logic variable that holds a piece of text. Shown after "Variable · " under a picked value.

editor.valueSource.typeYesNo.context: The kind of a Logic variable that holds a yes or no (on or off) value. Shown after "Variable · " under a picked value, and as a heading that groups such variables in the value picker.

editor.valueSource.variable.context: Small line under the name of a picked Logic variable that is gone or not known yet: it says the value is a variable (a value that Flows keep on the Homey).

editor.valueSource.variableGone.context: Name shown in a value field in place of a Logic variable that was picked once but no longer exists on the Homey. It is marked as a problem. Under it the word "Variable" is shown.

editor.valueSource.variableKnown.context: Name shown in a value field for a picked Logic variable while the list of variables is not known yet (still loading, or could not be read). Under it the word "Variable" is shown.

editor.valuesEditor.addReading.context: Small button under the readings of a value. It opens the value picker to add another reading, which is then added to the others.

editor.valuesEditor.addValue.context: Button under the list of values of a tile. It opens the value picker to add a new value to the tile.

editor.valuesEditor.changeIcon.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the round button on the Look tab that shows the icon of a value and opens a list to choose another.

editor.valuesEditor.colour.context: Screen reader label of the row of colour swatches on the Look tab that sets the colour of a value. Not visible as text.

editor.valuesEditor.decimals.context: Label over the choice of how many decimals a number value shows on the Reading tab. Also its screen reader label.

editor.valuesEditor.empty.context: Small grey line under the name of a value in the folded list when the value has no reading in it yet, so there is nothing it shows.

editor.valuesEditor.extraChart.context: Part of the small grey line under the name of a value in the folded list, lower case: the value is also drawn in the tile’s chart. The parts are separated by dots, such as "Bedroom · Bedroom climate · in the chart · a ring".

editor.valuesEditor.extraRing.context: Part of the small grey line under the name of a value in the folded list, lower case: the value is shown as a ring. The parts are separated by dots, such as "Energy · Gas · a ring".

editor.valuesEditor.extraTap.context: Part of the small grey line under the name of a value in the folded list, lower case: the value has its own tap action. The parts are separated by dots, such as "Energy · Gas · a tap".

editor.valuesEditor.fullRing.context: Label of a number box on the Look tab of a value that is shown as a ring: the number at which the ring is full, such as 100. It reads as the start of a sentence that the number completes.

editor.valuesEditor.hintSum.en: More readings add up; tap + to subtract one. One reading with − reads the other way round, for a battery that reports charging as negative.
editor.valuesEditor.hintSum.context: Small help text under the readings of a value. More readings are added up; the + button in front of a reading turns it into a subtraction. A single reading with a minus sign reads the opposite way, which is useful for a battery that reports charging as a negative number.

editor.valuesEditor.hintText.en: A text reading shows as it reads, so it can’t be added up, charted or shown as a ring.
editor.valuesEditor.hintText.context: Small help text under the readings of a value whose reading is a piece of text. A text cannot be added to other readings, drawn in a chart or shown as a ring.

editor.valuesEditor.icon.context: Screen reader label of the icon picker in the popover that opens from the icon button of a value. Not visible as text.

editor.valuesEditor.inChart.context: Label of a switch on the Look tab that draws the value in the tile’s history chart. Also the screen reader label of that switch. A line may follow below it saying why it cannot be in the chart.

editor.valuesEditor.label.context: Label of the text box on the Reading tab where the person types a name for the value. When it is empty the name of the reading is used.

editor.valuesEditor.labelTotal.context: Grey example text in the empty Label box of a value that adds up more than one reading: the name such a value gets when it has no label.

editor.valuesEditor.looks.context: Label over the icon and colour choices of a value on the Look tab. Plural: the ways the value looks.

editor.valuesEditor.moveDown.context: Small button on an open value that moves the value one place down in the list of values of the tile.

editor.valuesEditor.moveUp.context: Small button on an open value that moves the value one place up in the list of values of the tile.

editor.valuesEditor.none.en: No values yet. Add a reading of any device; add more to it to calculate.
editor.valuesEditor.none.context: Text shown in place of the list of values of a tile when it has none. A reading is a value of a device, such as its temperature. More readings in one value are added up (calculated).

editor.valuesEditor.pointsAt.context: Label over a dropdown that chooses which place of a picture the value points at, such as "Heat pump", "Upstairs" or "Garden" on a picture of a house. Also its screen reader label.

editor.valuesEditor.position.context: Label over the picker on the Look tab that chooses in which of nine spots of the tile (top left, top right, bottom left…) the value shows. Also its screen reader label.

editor.valuesEditor.quickBig.context: Button in the "Quick layout" row that places every value of a tile at once: the first value big, the others beside it, all at the bottom left.

editor.valuesEditor.quickEven.context: Button in the "Quick layout" row that places every value of a tile at once: all the same size, at the bottom left. "Even" means equal.

editor.valuesEditor.quickLayout.context: Small label in front of a row of buttons ("One big", "Ring in the corner", "All even") that place every value of a tile in one click. Shown when there is more than one value.

editor.valuesEditor.quickRing.context: Button in the "Quick layout" row that places every value of a tile at once: like "One big", with the first percentage value as a ring in the top right corner.

editor.valuesEditor.readings.context: Label over the list of readings of a value on the Reading tab. A reading is a value of a device, such as its temperature. More than one reading are added up.

editor.valuesEditor.removeNamed.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button on a value in the folded list. It removes that value from the tile.

params.name: The label of the value, such as "Temperature". Not translated.

editor.valuesEditor.removeReading.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button after a reading of a value. It removes that reading from the value.

editor.valuesEditor.removeThis.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of a small X button on a value in the folded list that has no label. It removes that value from the tile.

editor.valuesEditor.showAs.context: Label over a two-option switch on the Look tab that chooses whether the value is shown as a number or as a ring. Also its screen reader label.

editor.valuesEditor.showFigure.context: First option of a two-option switch (segmented control) "Show as": the value is shown as a number. The other option is "Ring".

editor.valuesEditor.showRing.context: Second option of a two-option switch (segmented control) "Show as": the value is shown as a round progress ring. The other option is "Number".

editor.valuesEditor.signAdded.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the + button in front of a reading in a calculated value. The reading is added now; the button makes it subtracted.

editor.valuesEditor.signSubtracted.context: Screen reader label (tooltip) of the − button in front of a reading in a calculated value. The reading is subtracted now; the button makes it added.

editor.valuesEditor.size.context: Label over a three-option switch (Small, Normal, Big) on the Look tab that chooses the size of the value on the tile. Also its screen reader label.

editor.valuesEditor.sizeBig.context: Last of three options (segmented control) for the size of a value on a tile. The others are "Small" and "Normal".

editor.valuesEditor.sizeNormal.context: Middle of three options (segmented control) for the size of a value on a tile. The others are "Small" and "Big".

editor.valuesEditor.sizeSmall.context: First of three options (segmented control) for the size of a value on a tile. The others are "Normal" and "Big".

editor.valuesEditor.tabLook.context: Second of three tabs (segmented control) of an open value: how the value looks, such as its icon, colour, position and size.

editor.valuesEditor.tabReading.context: First of three tabs (segmented control) of an open value: what the value reads, such as which device reading, with its label and decimals. A reading is a value of a device, such as its temperature.

editor.valuesEditor.tabTap.context: Third of three tabs (segmented control) of an open value: what happens when the person taps the value. Short for the action of tapping, not a water tap.

editor.valuesEditor.tabsLabel.context: Screen reader label of the three tabs (Reading, Look, Tap) of an open value. Not visible as text.

editor.valuesEditor.tapHint.en: Without one, a tap on this value does what tapping the tile does.
editor.valuesEditor.tapHint.context: Small help text on the Tap tab of a value. "One" is a tap action of its own: without it, tapping the value does what tapping the whole tile does.

editor.valuesEditor.thisValue.context: A short name for the value, in lower case, handed to the tap settings of a value, which put it into their own labels, such as "Tap: this value". Not a sentence.

editor.valuesEditor.unit.context: Label of the text box on the Look tab where the person types the unit of a value (such as W or °C). Only asked for a number variable, which has no unit of its own.

editor.valuesEditor.unitExample.context: Grey example text in the empty Unit box: a few units of measure as examples, separated by commas.

editor.valuesEditor.unitHint.en: A variable has no unit of its own: say which it is.
editor.valuesEditor.unitHint.context: Small help text under the Unit box. A variable (a value that Flows keep on the Homey) does not say what unit it is in, so the person says it.

editor.valuesEditor.useDefaultIcon.context: Small button in the icon popover of a value that removes the chosen icon, so the one that belongs to the reading is used again.

editor.valuesEditor.valueName.context: Name shown for a value in the folded list when it has no label and nothing is known about it yet.

editor.variableTap.add.context: Choice in the dropdown "What it does" for a number variable: a tap adds the amount typed in the field beside it ("By") to the variable.

editor.variableTap.by.context: Label of the field where the amount is typed that "Add" or "Subtract" changes the variable by. Read as "Add [by] 5".

editor.variableTap.chooseVariable.context: Placeholder of the dropdown that picks a Logic variable, shown while none is picked.

editor.variableTap.confirm.context: Checkbox under the variable fields: when ticked, tapping asks "are you sure" before the variable is changed.

editor.variableTap.flip.context: Choice in the dropdown "What it does" for a yes/no variable: a tap changes it to the opposite of what it is now.

editor.variableTap.no.context: The current value of a yes/no Logic variable that is off (false), shown in bold after "Now:".

editor.variableTap.noPermission.en: Tiledash may not read your Logic variables yet. Log in again and allow it.
editor.variableTap.noPermission.context: Note with a lock icon in the tap settings, shown instead of the variable fields when Tiledash has no permission to read the Homey’s Logic variables. Logging in again asks the Homey for that permission.

editor.variableTap.now.context: Small note under the variable fields: what the variable is now. The value is shown in bold (the tag). For example: Now: Yes.

params.value: The variable’s current value: a number, a text, or Yes, No or a dash when it has none.

editor.variableTap.setNo.context: Choice in the dropdown "What it does" for a yes/no variable: a tap always makes it no.

editor.variableTap.setTo.context: Choice in the dropdown "What it does" for a number or text variable: a tap sets it to a value typed in the field beside it.

editor.variableTap.setYes.context: Choice in the dropdown "What it does" for a yes/no variable: a tap always makes it yes.

editor.variableTap.subtract.context: Choice in the dropdown "What it does" for a number variable: a tap subtracts the amount typed in the field beside it ("By") from the variable.

editor.variableTap.typeNumber.context: Small grey note beside a Logic variable in the dropdown: its type is a number.

editor.variableTap.typeText.context: Small grey note beside a Logic variable in the dropdown: its type is text.

editor.variableTap.typeYesNo.context: Small grey note beside a Logic variable in the dropdown: its type is yes or no (true or false).

editor.variableTap.value.context: Label of the field where the value is typed that "Set to" gives the variable. A number or a text.

editor.variableTap.variable.context: Label of the dropdown that picks which Logic variable a tap changes.

editor.variableTap.whatItDoes.context: Label of the dropdown that chooses what a tap does to the picked variable: flip it, set it, add to it or subtract from it.

editor.variableTap.yes.context: The current value of a yes/no Logic variable that is on (true), shown in bold after "Now:".

editor.variablesNotice.failedText.en: Your Homey didn’t answer just now. Try again in a moment.
editor.variablesNotice.failedText.context: Help text under the heading "Variables couldn’t be read" in the value picker. The Homey (the smart-home hub) did not answer.

editor.variablesNotice.failedTitle.context: Bold heading in the Variables tab of the value picker when asking the Homey for its Logic variables failed. A short text follows below it.

editor.variablesNotice.forbiddenText.en: Check the app’s permissions: it needs to read variables (homey.logic.readonly), and you may need to log in again after changing them.
editor.variablesNotice.forbiddenText.context: Help text under the heading "Variables aren’t available" in the value picker. It says to check the permissions of the Tiledash app on the Homey. "homey.logic.readonly" is the technical name of the permission and stays as it is.

editor.variablesNotice.forbiddenTitle.context: Bold heading in the Variables tab of the value picker when the Homey refused to share its Logic variables with Tiledash. A text with what to check follows below it.

editor.variablesNotice.loading.context: Bold heading in the Variables tab of the value picker while the Homey’s Logic variables are still being loaded.

editor.variablesNotice.needLocation.context: Part of the list in "This needs …" in the value picker: one kind of value a variable can hold, a location written as a text of two coordinates (latitude and longitude, with a comma between them). The coordinates are an example and stay as they are. Lower case, as it sits inside a sentence.

editor.variablesNotice.needNumber.context: Part of the list in "This needs …" in the value picker: one kind of value a variable can hold, a number. Lower case, as it sits inside a sentence.

editor.variablesNotice.needText.context: Part of the list in "This needs …" in the value picker: one kind of value a variable can hold, a piece of text. Lower case, as it sits inside a sentence.

editor.variablesNotice.needYesNo.context: Part of the list in "This needs …" in the value picker: one kind of value a variable can hold, a yes or no value (on or off). Lower case, as it sits inside a sentence.

editor.variablesNotice.noFitText.en: This needs {needs}. Your variables hold something else.
editor.variablesNotice.noFitText.context: Help text under the heading "None of your variables fits" in the value picker. It says what kind of value the place needs, such as "This needs a number or text. Your variables hold something else."

params.needs: What the place needs, as a list in the language’s style, such as "a number or yes or no". Made from the four messages that start with "need". Already translated.

editor.variablesNotice.noFitTitle.context: Bold heading in the Variables tab of the value picker when the Homey has variables, but none holds the kind of value this place on the tile needs. A text with what is needed follows below it.

editor.variablesNotice.noneText.en: Make one in the Homey app, under Flows › Variables. Flows can keep anything in it: a mode, a count, a position.
editor.variablesNotice.noneText.context: Help text under the heading "No variables yet" in the value picker. It points to the place in the Homey app (the Homey’s own app, not Tiledash) where variables are made: the Flows section, then Variables. Use the words the Homey app uses in your language if you know them.

editor.variablesNotice.noneTitle.context: Bold heading in the Variables tab of the value picker when the Homey has no Logic variables at all. A text on how to make one follows below it.

editor.wallPanel.aboveTilesHeading.context: Small heading in the Screen section of the wall panel dialog, above the switches for showing the dashboard’s name and summaries, and the time, over the tiles.

editor.wallPanel.afterMinutes.context: Choice in a dropdown that sets a time: the panel falls asleep after this many minutes without a touch, such as "After 5 minutes".

params.minutes: The number of minutes, 1 or more.

editor.wallPanel.afterSeconds.context: Choice in the dropdown for closing popups: a popup closes after this many seconds without a touch, such as "After 30 seconds".

params.seconds: The number of seconds, 1 or more.

editor.wallPanel.alertsHeading.context: Small heading in the Sleep & alerts section of the wall panel dialog, above the Wake for alerts switch. A noun.

editor.wallPanel.behaviourHeading.context: Small heading in the Screen section of the wall panel dialog, above the settings for full screen, keeping the screen on and closing popups. A noun.

editor.wallPanel.closePopups.en: Close popups when nobody touches them
editor.wallPanel.closePopups.context: Label of the dropdown that sets how long a popup (a dashboard shown on top of the panel) may stay open untouched before it closes. Choices such as "After 30 seconds" or "Never".

editor.wallPanel.closePopupsName.context: Name of the dropdown that sets when popups close on their own, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wallPanel.copied.context: Replaces the Copy button’s text for two seconds after the link was copied to the clipboard.

editor.wallPanel.copy.context: Small button beside the panel’s link. It copies the link to the clipboard. A command.

editor.wallPanel.dashboard.context: Name of the dropdown that picks the main dashboard of the wall panel, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wallPanel.dashboardsLead.en: The dashboards a swipe moves between, in this order. It always starts on its main dashboard.
editor.wallPanel.dashboardsLead.context: Short line at the top of the Dashboards section of the wall panel dialog. The panel swipes between the listed dashboards in the order shown; its main dashboard always comes first.

editor.wallPanel.defaultName.context: The name suggested for a new wall panel, filled into the name field for the person to type over, built from the name of its dashboard, such as "Home panel".

params.name: The name of the dashboard the panel starts on. Not translated.

editor.wallPanel.description.en: A screen that shows your dashboards and nothing else, and stays on. Saved on your account: a tablet only needs the link. Hold the top-left corner (or press Esc) to get back.
editor.wallPanel.description.context: Text under the title of the wall panel dialog. It says what a wall panel is, that it is saved on the account so a tablet only needs its link, and how to leave a running panel: hold the top-left corner of the screen or press the Esc key.

editor.wallPanel.dim.context: Label of a switch in the sleep section, also its name for screen readers. When on, the screen is darkened while the panel sleeps.

editor.wallPanel.dimHint.en: Darker still, for a bedroom or a hallway at night.
editor.wallPanel.dimHint.context: Help text under the Dim while asleep switch: the screen gets even darker while asleep.

editor.wallPanel.einkClear.context: Label of the dropdown (and its name for screen readers) that sets how often an e-ink panel flashes black and white once to clear the faint traces of earlier images (ghosting). Choices such as "Every hour". Shown only with the E-ink switch on.

editor.wallPanel.einkClearHint.en: Clearing flashes the screen black and white once, to wipe away the faint traces e-ink leaves behind.
editor.wallPanel.einkClearHint.context: Help text under the e-ink settings. It explains what clearing does: the screen flashes black and white once to wipe away ghosting.

editor.wallPanel.einkHint.en: Black on white without motion; values change in steps, alarms and locks right away.
editor.wallPanel.einkHint.context: Help text under the E-ink screen switch. The panel shows black on white, nothing moves, new values show in steps, and alarms and door locks show right away.

editor.wallPanel.einkRefresh.context: Label of the dropdown (and its name for screen readers) that sets how often an e-ink panel takes in new values, with choices such as "Every minute". Shown only with the E-ink switch on.

editor.wallPanel.einkTitle.context: Label of a switch in the wall panel dialog, also its name for screen readers. Turns on the mode for e-ink screens (like an e-reader).

editor.wallPanel.everyHour.context: Choice in the dropdown for how often an e-ink screen clears ghosting: once an hour.

editor.wallPanel.everyMinutes.context: Choice in the dropdowns for how often an e-ink screen shows new values or clears ghosting: "Every minute" for one minute, else such as "Every 5 minutes".

params.minutes: The number of minutes, 1 or more.

editor.wallPanel.everySeconds.context: Choice in the dropdown for how often an e-ink screen shows new values, such as "Every 30 seconds".

params.seconds: The number of seconds, 1 or more.

editor.wallPanel.fullScreen.context: Label of a switch in the wall panel dialog, also its name for screen readers. The panel opens in full screen, without the browser around it.

editor.wallPanel.fullScreenUnsupported.en: This browser can’t go full screen by itself.
editor.wallPanel.fullScreenUnsupported.context: Note under the Full screen switch when the browser cannot be put into full screen by a web page. The switch is off and disabled.

editor.wallPanel.generalLead.en: What it’s called, where it starts, and the link a tablet opens.
editor.wallPanel.generalLead.context: Short line at the top of the General section of the wall panel dialog, saying what is in it: the panel’s name, the dashboard it starts on and the link to open on a tablet.

editor.wallPanel.keepOn.context: Label of a switch in the wall panel dialog, also its name for screen readers. While the panel shows, the screen does not dim or lock.

editor.wallPanel.keepOnHint.en: While the panel shows, the screen won’t dim or lock.
editor.wallPanel.keepOnHint.context: Help text under the Keep the screen on switch.

editor.wallPanel.keepOnUnsupported.en: This browser can’t keep the screen on; use the tablet’s own setting.
editor.wallPanel.keepOnUnsupported.context: Note under the Keep the screen on switch when the browser cannot stop the screen from dimming. The person should use the device’s own screen-timeout setting instead. The switch is disabled.

editor.wallPanel.languageLead.en: Words and formats on this panel. It follows your account unless you pick others.
editor.wallPanel.languageLead.context: Short line at the top of the Language & region section of the wall panel dialog. The panel uses the account’s language and formats unless others are picked here.

editor.wallPanel.linkHint.en: Opening this link starts the panel straight away, so a tablet that opens it on start runs the panel on its own.
editor.wallPanel.linkHint.context: Help text under the panel’s link. Opening the link runs the panel at once, so a tablet set to open it at start-up becomes a wall panel by itself.

editor.wallPanel.linkLabel.context: Label above the link of the saved wall panel. A kiosk browser is a browser set up to open one web page in full screen on a wall-mounted tablet.

editor.wallPanel.linkNone.en: The link appears once the panel is saved.
editor.wallPanel.linkNone.context: Shown in place of the panel’s link while the panel is new and not saved yet.

editor.wallPanel.mainFixedHint.en: Always first. Pick another under General.
editor.wallPanel.mainFixedHint.context: Small text on the first, fixed row of the panel’s dashboard list (its main dashboard), which can’t be moved or removed. Another main dashboard is picked in the General section, under Starts on.

editor.wallPanel.nameLabel.context: Label of the text field for the name of the wall panel, which is also how it is called in the sidebar.

editor.wallPanel.namePlaceholder.context: Grey example text in the empty name field of a wall panel: three example places, separated by commas.

editor.wallPanel.never.context: Choice in a dropdown that sets a time (when the panel falls asleep, how often an e-ink screen clears itself, when popups close): it never happens.

editor.wallPanel.saveAndStart.context: Blue button in the footer of the wall panel dialog. It saves the panel and runs it on this screen straight away. A command.

editor.wallPanel.saveFailed.context: Red message (toast) when saving a wall panel failed.

editor.wallPanel.saved.context: Green message (toast) after a wall panel was saved without starting it. The quotes are around the name of the panel.

params.name: The name of the wall panel. Not translated.

editor.wallPanel.screenLead.en: How it fills the screen, and what shows on it.
editor.wallPanel.screenLead.context: Short line at the top of the Screen section of the wall panel dialog.

editor.wallPanel.sectionDashboards.context: Tab of the wall panel dialog, in the row above its settings (some may sit under More when the row is full): the dashboards the panel swipes between, in their order.

editor.wallPanel.sectionGeneral.context: Tab of the wall panel dialog, in the row above its settings (some may sit under More when the row is full): the panel’s name, the dashboard it starts on and its link.

editor.wallPanel.sectionLanguage.context: Tab of the wall panel dialog, in the row above its settings (some may sit under More when the row is full): the panel’s own language and its way of writing dates, times and numbers.

editor.wallPanel.sectionScreen.context: Tab of the wall panel dialog, in the row above its settings (some may sit under More when the row is full): the layout, what shows above the tiles, full screen, keeping the screen on, popups and the e-ink mode. A noun.

editor.wallPanel.sectionSleep.context: Tab of the wall panel dialog, in the row above its settings (some may sit under More when the row is full): what the panel does when nobody touches it (falls asleep to another dashboard) and whether alerts wake it. Nouns.

editor.wallPanel.sections.context: Name of the row of tabs of the wall panel dialog (General, Dashboards, Screen…), read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wallPanel.shift.context: Label of a switch in the sleep section, also its name for screen readers. While asleep everything on screen drifts by about a pixel a minute, so no image stays in one place.

editor.wallPanel.shiftHint.en: For OLED screens: everything moves a pixel a minute, so nothing burns in. Too slow to notice.
editor.wallPanel.shiftHint.context: Help text under the Shift the screen slowly switch. It protects OLED screens from burn-in (a faint permanent image) by moving everything a pixel a minute, too slowly to notice.

editor.wallPanel.showName.context: Label of a switch in the wall panel dialog, also its name for screen readers. The dashboard’s name and its summaries (small live figures such as "3 lights on") show above the tiles.

editor.wallPanel.showTime.context: Label of a switch in the wall panel dialog, also its name for screen readers. The time shows above the dashboard.

editor.wallPanel.sleepAfter.en: Fall asleep when nobody touches it
editor.wallPanel.sleepAfter.context: Label of the dropdown that sets how long the panel may stay untouched before it falls asleep (shows its sleep dashboard). Choices such as "After 5 minutes" or "Never".

editor.wallPanel.sleepAfterName.context: Name of the dropdown that sets when the panel falls asleep, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wallPanel.sleepDashboard.context: Label of the dropdown that picks the dashboard the panel shows while it sleeps, such as a big clock.

editor.wallPanel.sleepDashboardName.context: Name of the dropdown that picks the dashboard shown while the panel sleeps, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wallPanel.sleepHeading.context: Heading of the section about sleeping in the wall panel dialog. A noun: what the panel does when nobody touches it.

editor.wallPanel.sleepLead.en: What it does when nobody touches it, and when something needs your attention.
editor.wallPanel.sleepLead.context: Short line at the top of the Sleep & alerts section of the wall panel dialog: falling asleep when untouched, and waking for alerts (smoke, a leak, the doorbell…).

editor.wallPanel.sleepScreenTag.context: Small text beside a dashboard in the list of dashboards to add to the panel: the panel shows this one while it sleeps, such as a big clock.

editor.wallPanel.sleepShowName.en: Show the name and summaries while asleep
editor.wallPanel.sleepShowName.context: Label of a switch in the sleep section, also its name for screen readers. The sleep dashboard’s name and summaries (small live figures) show above it while the panel sleeps.

editor.wallPanel.sleepShowTime.context: Label of a switch in the sleep section, also its name for screen readers. The time shows above the sleep dashboard while the panel sleeps.

editor.wallPanel.startsHere.context: Small tag on the first row of the panel’s dashboard list: the dashboard the panel starts on (its main dashboard, always first on the panel).

editor.wallPanel.startsOn.context: Label of the dropdown that picks the main dashboard of the wall panel: the one it starts on and wakes up to.

editor.wallPanel.startsOnHint.en: Where it starts, and where it goes back to when it wakes up.
editor.wallPanel.startsOnHint.context: Help text under the Starts on dropdown of the wall panel dialog: the panel starts on this dashboard and returns to it when it wakes from sleep.

editor.wallPanel.swipeHint.en: Swipe between these {count} in this order; dots at the bottom show where you are.
editor.wallPanel.swipeHint.context: Help text under the list of dashboards on the panel when there are two or more. The panel swipes between them in the order of the list, and a row of dots at the bottom shows which one is on screen.

params.count: How many dashboards are on the panel, at least 2.

editor.wallPanel.swipeOnlyHint.en: Only {name}: add more to swipe between them.
editor.wallPanel.swipeOnlyHint.context: Help text under the list of dashboards on the panel when only its main dashboard is on it. Adding more dashboards to the list lets the panel swipe between them.

params.name: The name of the panel’s main dashboard. Not translated.

editor.wallPanel.theDashboard.context: Stand-in used inside a sentence of the Layout setting, in place of the name of the panel’s main dashboard, when that name is not known yet. Reads as "…on the dashboard". Lower case, no capital.

editor.wallPanel.thenSwipesTo.context: Label above the list of the other dashboards on a wall panel, in the order a swipe reaches them after the main dashboard. Rows can be moved up and down, removed and added.

editor.wallPanel.titleEdit.context: Title of the dialog that changes the settings of an existing wall panel (a screen that shows dashboards and nothing else, and stays on).

editor.wallPanel.titleNew.context: Title of the dialog that makes a new wall panel (a screen that shows dashboards and nothing else, and stays on).

editor.wallPanel.wakeForAlerts.context: Label of a switch in the wall panel dialog, also its name for screen readers. When on, an alert wakes the panel from its sleep.

editor.wallPanel.wakeForAlertsHint.en: Smoke, a leak, the alarm, motion or the doorbell wake it from sleep and show full screen, and keep it on while they last. Which devices alert is set in your account.
editor.wallPanel.wakeForAlertsHint.context: Help text under the Wake for alerts switch. Alerts (smoke, a water leak, the alarm, motion, the doorbell) wake a sleeping panel, show full screen and keep the screen on while they last. Which devices count as alerts is set on the account page.

editor.wallPanel.wakeTouchHint.en: A touch wakes it up again, back to {name}; that first touch doesn’t press anything.
editor.wallPanel.wakeTouchHint.context: Help text at the end of the sleep section. Touching the sleeping panel wakes it and brings back its main dashboard; that first touch does not press a tile.

params.name: The name of the panel’s main dashboard. Not translated.

editor.weatherPlace.credit.context: Small credit line under the search: the search is done by that service. Keep the service name OpenStreetMap Nominatim exactly.

editor.weatherPlace.homeyUnknown.en: This Homey’s location isn’t known (it isn’t set, or Tiledash may not read it). Search for the place instead.
editor.weatherPlace.homeyUnknown.context: Orange text under the choice when This Homey is chosen but its location can not be read: it is not set, or Tiledash has no permission. It points to the Search option.

editor.weatherPlace.nameHint.context: Small grey text under the name field of the pinned place: the name is shown on the weather tile.

editor.weatherPlace.nameLabel.context: Label of the field where the person can change the name of the pinned place. "Its" is the pinned place.

editor.weatherPlace.nearHomey.context: Line under the choice when This Homey is chosen: the weather is for the place near the Homey, which is named. It starts with a map pin icon.

params.name: The name of the place near the Homey, such as "Utrecht". Not translated.

editor.weatherPlace.nothingFound.en: Nothing found; try another spelling, or pin it on the map.
editor.weatherPlace.nothingFound.context: Grey text when a search finds no place. It suggests another spelling, or the third option "Pin on a map" to choose the place on a map.

editor.weatherPlace.pinnedPlace.context: The name a place gets when the person drops a pin on the map, before they type a name. It is saved as the place’s name and shown on the weather tile.

editor.weatherPlace.searchButton.context: Button next to the search field: it runs the search for the typed place name.

editor.weatherPlace.searchPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the search field where a place is typed by name: a town or an address.

editor.weatherPlace.searching.context: Text of the search button while the search is running. It is disabled meanwhile.

editor.weatherPlace.wayHomey.context: First option of "Weather for": the place where the Homey is (its own location setting). A Homey is the smart-home hub.

editor.weatherPlace.wayMap.context: Third option of "Weather for": drop a pin on a map to choose the place.

editor.weatherPlace.waySearch.context: Second option of "Weather for": find the place by typing its name. A verb or a noun, as a short option.

editor.weatherPlace.weatherFor.context: Label of the three-way choice of which place the weather is for (This Homey, Search, Pin on a map), and its screen reader label.

editor.widgetPicker.browseAll.context: Button at the end of the Community tab of the add-widgets window, after the question "Not what you’re after?". It goes to the community page. A command.

editor.widgetPicker.browseCommunity.context: Button under the empty Community tab of the add-widgets window. It goes to the community page, where widgets, themes and partials made by people can be browsed. A command.

editor.widgetPicker.community.context: Small badge on a widget that comes from the community (made by another person), in the looks of the add-widgets window.

editor.widgetPicker.communityLoading.context: Screen reader text while the Community tab of the add-widgets window loads the community’s widgets. Grey placeholder rows show meanwhile. Not visible as text.

editor.widgetPicker.communityLooks.context: Screen reader label of the group of cards of community looks (not installed yet) in the add-widgets window. Not visible as text.

editor.widgetPicker.communityNone.en: Nothing in the community fits your Homey yet. Widgets people share show up here.
editor.widgetPicker.communityNone.context: Text shown on the Community tab of the add-widgets window when the community has no widget for anything on the person’s Homey, and none that stands alone. A button "Browse the community" is under it.

editor.widgetPicker.communityOffline.en: Couldn’t reach the community. Widgets you installed are still here.
editor.widgetPicker.communityOffline.context: Text on the Community tab of the add-widgets window when the community could not be loaded (no connection, or the server had a problem). A button "Try again" follows it.

editor.widgetPicker.everyLevel.context: A row on the Other tab of the add-widgets window: adds a Stack (a tile that holds several tiles on pages you swipe between) with a Floor plan for each level of the person’s floor plan (a drawing of their house).

params.plan: The name of the floor plan, such as "Our house".

editor.widgetPicker.everyLevelDetail.en: A Stack with a Floor plan for each of its {count} levels
editor.widgetPicker.everyLevelDetail.context: Line under the row "Every level of …" in the add-widgets window. A level is a floor of the house; a Stack holds tiles on pages you swipe between.

params.count: How many levels the plan has, 2 or more.

editor.widgetPicker.exampleDashboard.context: Example name of a dashboard, shown on the preview of the Dashboard button widget in the add-widgets window (the button that opens another dashboard). It is demo content: use a common name of a room or dashboard in the language.

editor.widgetPicker.fits.en: {kind, select, device {{count, plural, one {# device} other {# devices}}} flow {{count, plural, one {# flow} other {# flows}}} mood {{count, plural, one {# mood} other {# moods}}} other {{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}}}
editor.widgetPicker.fits.context: Small text next to the title of an installed or own widget in the add-widgets window: what it can be added for, and how many of those the person’s Homey has, such as "3 devices" or "1 flow". Flows are automations of the Homey; moods are scenes.

params.count: How many of those the Homey has. A number.
params.kind: What the widget fits: device, flow or mood. A code, not translated; the message has a branch for each.

editor.widgetPicker.fitsNone.en: Nothing on your Homey fits it.
editor.widgetPicker.fitsNone.context: Line under the title of an installed or own widget in the add-widgets window when the person’s Homey has no device, Flow or mood this widget can be used for.

editor.widgetPicker.flowDisabled.context: Small text next to the name of a Flow (an automation of the Homey) in the add-widgets window: the Flow is switched off.

editor.widgetPicker.forYourHomey.context: Title of the first group on the Community tab of the add-widgets window: community widgets that fit a device, Flow or mood of the person’s Homey, each with the things it fits under it.

editor.widgetPicker.inCommunityNote.en: Not installed yet: adding one installs it for you.
editor.widgetPicker.inCommunityNote.context: Small text under the heading "In the community": these widgets are not installed yet, and adding one to the dashboard installs it automatically.

editor.widgetPicker.inCommunityTitle.context: Small heading in the right half of the add-widgets window, above the community’s looks (not installed yet) for the ticked thing.

editor.widgetPicker.installed.context: Small badge with a check mark on a community widget in the add-widgets window that the person has installed already.

editor.widgetPicker.installsWhenAdded.context: Small text on the card of a suggested community widget that is not installed yet: who made it and how many use it, then a note that adding it to the dashboard installs it.

params.by: Who made it and how many use it, such as "@tiledash · 214 use it". Already translated.

editor.widgetPicker.looks.context: Screen reader label of the group of cards in the right half of the add-widgets window, where one look (one widget) is picked for the ticked thing. Not visible as text.

editor.widgetPicker.makeWidget.context: Button that opens the widget editor to make a new widget of the person’s own. Shown under the empty My own tab and in the footer of the add-widgets window; in the footer a small "Pro" badge can follow it. A command.

editor.widgetPicker.moreInCommunity.en: {count, plural, one {# more in the community} other {# more in the community}}
editor.widgetPicker.moreInCommunity.context: Small button with a community icon at the end of a device’s row in the add-widgets window: the community has more widgets (looks) for this device. Clicking it shows them. For example "3 more in the community".

params.count: How many more looks the community has. A number.

editor.widgetPicker.noRoom.context: Title of the group of devices that are in no room of the home, in the list of devices of the add-widgets window (devices are grouped by room). Also shown next to a device’s name when it is found by a search.

editor.widgetPicker.notWhatYouWant.context: Question at the end of the Community tab of the add-widgets window. A button "Browse the whole community" follows it.

editor.widgetPicker.official.context: Small badge on a community widget that is made by Tiledash itself (not by another person).

editor.widgetPicker.ownNone.en: Widgets you make show up here: start from any widget to change how it looks, or from nothing.
editor.widgetPicker.ownNone.context: Text shown on the My own tab of the add-widgets window while the person made no widgets yet. A button "Make a widget…" is under it. Making a widget starts from an existing widget (to change how it looks) or from an empty one.

editor.widgetPicker.pickLeft.en: Pick something on the left to see how it can look.
editor.widgetPicker.pickLeft.context: Text in the right half of the add-widgets window while nothing is selected: it asks to choose a device, Flow, mood or widget in the list on the left.

editor.widgetPicker.popular.context: Title of the group, on the Community tab of the add-widgets window, of the community widgets that stand alone (not tied to a device), the most used first.

editor.widgetPicker.publishedNew.context: Small text under a suggested community widget that nobody uses yet: who made it, and that it is new, such as "@tiledash · new".

params.publisher: The publisher’s handle, such as "@tiledash". Not translated.

editor.widgetPicker.recommended.context: Small badge on the first look of a ticked thing in the add-widgets window: the widget that fits it best.

editor.widgetPicker.retry.context: Button after the text "Couldn’t reach the community" on the Community tab of the add-widgets window: loads it again. A command.

editor.widgetPicker.searchPlaceholder.en: Search devices, flows, moods and widgets
editor.widgetPicker.searchPlaceholder.context: Placeholder of the search box at the top of the add-widgets window. It searches every tab at once.

editor.widgetPicker.selected.context: Small count in the footer of the add-widgets window: how many things are ticked, such as "3 selected". Only shown when at least one is ticked.

params.count: How many things are ticked. A number.

editor.widgetPicker.showMore.context: Button at the end of the Community tab of the add-widgets window: loads more widgets from the community. A command.

editor.widgetPicker.tabCommunity.context: Tab of the add-widgets window: every widget from the community (where people share widgets), installed or not, those that fit the person’s Homey first. Adding one that is not installed installs it.

editor.widgetPicker.tabDevices.context: Tab of the add-widgets window: the devices of the Homey (lights, sensors, thermostats) to put on the dashboard.

editor.widgetPicker.tabFlows.context: Tab of the add-widgets window: the Flows of the Homey (its automations) that can be started with a button.

editor.widgetPicker.tabMoods.context: Tab of the add-widgets window: the moods of the Homey (scenes that set several devices at once).

editor.widgetPicker.tabOther.context: Tab of the add-widgets window: widgets that are not about one device, Flow or mood, such as a clock, a weather forecast or an energy overview.

editor.widgetPicker.tabOwn.context: Tab of the add-widgets window: the widgets the person made themselves.

editor.widgetPicker.tabsLabel.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs (Devices, Flows, Moods…) of the add-widgets window. Not visible as text.

editor.widgetPicker.usedBy.en: {publisher} · {count, plural, one {# uses it} other {# use it}}
editor.widgetPicker.usedBy.context: Small text under a suggested community widget: who made it and how many people use it, such as "@tiledash · 214 use it". The part before the dot is the publisher’s handle.

params.count: How many people have it installed. A number.
params.publisher: The publisher’s handle, such as "@tiledash". Not translated.

editor.widgetPicker.yours.context: Small badge on a widget that the person made themselves, in the looks of the add-widgets window.

editor.widgetSettings.blocking.en: To save, choose {kind, select, one {a {noun}} many {{noun}} other {at least {min, number} {noun}}}{more, plural, =0 {} other { and # more}}.
editor.widgetSettings.blocking.context: Small line under the settings of a tile that says what keeps Save from working: a required setting is not chosen yet, such as "To save, choose a charger" or "To save, choose at least 3 smoke detectors and 1 more." The line ends with a full stop.

params.kind: How the setting counts: "one" (a single thing, "a charger"), "many" (several, no article, "readings") or "least" (a minimum, "at least 3 smoke detectors").
params.min: The smallest number the setting takes. A number.
params.more: How many more settings are waiting to be chosen. A number, zero for none.
params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.

editor.widgetSettings.blockingOnTab.en: To save, choose {kind, select, one {a {noun}} many {{noun}} other {at least {min, number} {noun}}}{more, plural, =0 {} other { and # more}} on <tab>{tabName}</tab>.
editor.widgetSettings.blockingOnTab.context: Small line under the settings of a tile that says what keeps Save from working when the setting that is missing is on another tab than the open one, such as "To save, choose a charger on Tap." The name of the tab is a button that goes there. The line ends with a full stop.

params.kind: How the setting counts: "one" (a single thing, "a charger"), "many" (several, no article, "readings") or "least" (a minimum, "at least 3 smoke detectors").
params.min: The smallest number the setting takes. A number.
params.more: How many more settings are waiting to be chosen. A number, zero for none.
params.noun: The name of the setting in lower case, such as "charger". Comes from the widget, not translated by this message.
params.tabName: The name of the tab, such as "Look" or "Tap". Already translated.

editor.widgetSettings.decimalsFor.context: Screen reader label of the choice of how many decimals a number on the tile shows. Not visible as text.

params.reading: The name of the reading, such as "Temperature". Comes from the device, not translated.

editor.widgetSettings.description.en: What this tile shows and how it behaves.
editor.widgetSettings.description.context: Small description under the title (the name of the tile) of the settings dialog of a tile. It is read out to screen readers more than it is looked at.

editor.widgetSettings.headingSettings.context: Small heading over the settings of a built-in widget when the dialog has no tabs. The settings are the choices that belong to the widget, such as which device it shows.

editor.widgetSettings.headingWhatItShows.context: Small heading over the settings of a widget of the person’s own (made in the widget code editor), on the Content tab: the choices that decide what the tile shows.

editor.widgetSettings.leadChart.en: The small history chart on the tile.
editor.widgetSettings.leadChart.context: Short line at the top of the Chart tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings): a small chart of recent values drawn on the tile.

editor.widgetSettings.leadContent.en: What the tile shows: its devices, values or text.
editor.widgetSettings.leadContent.context: Short line at the top of the Content tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings), saying what is in it.

editor.widgetSettings.leadLayout.en: How the parts of the tile are arranged.
editor.widgetSettings.leadLayout.context: Short line at the top of the Layout tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings), saying what is in it.

editor.widgetSettings.leadLive.en: What the live plan shows, following your devices.
editor.widgetSettings.leadLive.context: Short line at the top of the Live plan tab of a Floor plan tile’s settings (tabs above the settings): the plan drawn live, its furniture, readings and lights.

editor.widgetSettings.leadLook.en: How the tile looks: the widget that shows it, its colours and decimals.
editor.widgetSettings.leadLook.context: Short line at the top of the Look tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings). The widget is one of the looks offered for the tile, such as a dial or a bar; the same word as the list of looks there.

editor.widgetSettings.leadMap.en: A map behind the tile, around where the device is.
editor.widgetSettings.leadMap.context: Short line at the top of the Map tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings): a map drawn behind the tile, around the device’s location.

editor.widgetSettings.leadPicture.en: How the picture of this level shows, made in the floor planner.
editor.widgetSettings.leadPicture.context: Short line at the top of the Picture tab of a Floor plan tile’s settings (tabs above the settings): a picture of the level, made in the floor planner, shown instead of the live plan.

editor.widgetSettings.leadShow.en: Whether the tile is always on the dashboard, or only when something applies.
editor.widgetSettings.leadShow.context: Short line at the top of the When to show tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings): the tile can always show, or only under conditions.

editor.widgetSettings.leadTap.en: What happens when you tap the tile.
editor.widgetSettings.leadTap.context: Short line at the top of the Tap tab of a tile’s settings (tabs above the settings). Tap as in touching or clicking the tile.

editor.widgetSettings.looksLabel.context: Screen reader label of the list of looks (other widgets that can show the same device) in the settings of a tile. Not visible as text. A widget is a tile design.

editor.widgetSettings.noSettings.en: This widget has no settings. Its look is set with Style.
editor.widgetSettings.noSettings.context: Grey text under the heading "Settings" in the settings of a tile when its widget has nothing to set. "Style" is the name of the button "Style…" in the footer of the dialog, where colours and fonts are set.

editor.widgetSettings.numbers.context: Small heading over the decimals choices, one per number the tile shows, on the Look tab of the settings of a tile. Plural: the numbers on the tile.

editor.widgetSettings.recommended.context: Small badge on the first look (the best-fitting widget) in the list of looks in the settings of a tile.

editor.widgetSettings.style.context: Button in the footer of the settings dialog of a tile. It opens the style panel where colours, fonts and the look of the tile are set. The dots mean it opens something else.

editor.widgetSettings.tabsLabel.context: Screen reader label of the row of tabs of a tile’s settings (Content, Look, Tap…). Not visible as text.

editor.widgetSettings.whenToShow.context: Name of the last tab of the settings of a tile, where the person sets when the tile is visible on the dashboard (always, or only under conditions). Also the heading of that part when there are no tabs.

editor.wizard.allLeftOut.en: You left everything out. Tick something on the right, or start empty.
editor.wizard.allLeftOut.context: Shown in the preview of the new-dashboard dialog when every item of the suggestion was unticked. The list with ticks is at the right of the preview.

editor.wizard.create.context: Blue button in the footer of the new-dashboard dialog, second step. It makes the dashboard with the chosen name and tiles. A command.

editor.wizard.createFailed.context: Title of the red box above the buttons of the new-dashboard dialog when creating the dashboard failed. The reason follows below it.

editor.wizard.descriptionFirst.en: We looked at your rooms, devices and favourites. Pick a start; you can change everything later.
editor.wizard.descriptionFirst.context: Text under the title of the new-dashboard dialog, first step, for a person who has no dashboard yet. Tiledash looked at their Homey and offers starting points.

editor.wizard.descriptionStart.en: Start from a suggestion built from your Homey, or from an empty wall.
editor.wizard.descriptionStart.context: Text under the title of the new-dashboard dialog, first step. The person picks a suggestion made from their Homey, or an empty dashboard (the "wall").

editor.wizard.descriptionTune.en: Name it and leave out what you don’t need. The preview shows your real devices.
editor.wizard.descriptionTune.context: Text under the title of the new-dashboard dialog, second step. The person names the dashboard and unticks what they do not want; the preview shows their own devices.

editor.wizard.emptyWallPreview.en: An empty wall. Add widgets and headings once it’s made.
editor.wizard.emptyWallPreview.context: Shown in the preview of the new-dashboard dialog when the "An empty wall" start is chosen. Widgets (types of tiles) and headings can be added after the dashboard is created.

editor.wizard.metaCounts.en: {sections, plural, one {# section} other {# sections}} · {tiles, plural, one {# tile} other {# tiles}}
editor.wizard.metaCounts.context: Small grey line at the bottom of a start card. It says how many sections (groups of tiles under a heading) and tiles the suggestion has, such as "3 sections · 12 tiles".

params.sections: How many sections the suggestion has, at least 1.
params.tiles: How many tiles the suggestion has, at least 0.

editor.wizard.metaEmpty.context: Small grey line at the bottom of the card "An empty wall": the dashboard starts with no tiles.

editor.wizard.metaNoRooms.context: Small grey line at the bottom of the card "One room" when the person’s Homey has no room with devices yet, so this start cannot be chosen.

editor.wizard.moreInRoom.en: {count} more in this room; its own dashboard has everything.
editor.wizard.moreInRoom.context: Small grey note under a section of the list when the suggestion leaves some devices of the room out to keep the dashboard tidy. It says how many, and that a dashboard made for just that room has them all.

params.count: How many devices were left out, at least 1.

editor.wizard.nameLabel.context: Label of the text field for the name of the new dashboard.

editor.wizard.namePlaceholder.context: Grey example text in the empty name field of the new dashboard, giving two example names separated by a comma. A wall panel is a screen that shows dashboards.

editor.wizard.onIt.context: Small heading above the list of everything the new dashboard will have (sections and devices with ticks). Unticking an item leaves it out. A short phrase.

editor.wizard.recommended.context: Small badge on the start card of the overview ("Home"), marking it as the best choice for most people.

editor.wizard.roomLabel.context: Name of the dropdown on the card "One room" that picks the room, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wizard.startEmptyDescription.context: Description on the card "An empty wall" in the new-dashboard dialog. The person adds every tile (a box that shows a device, flow or value) themselves.

editor.wizard.startEmptyName.context: Name of a start choice (a card) in the new-dashboard dialog: a dashboard with nothing on it. The "wall" is the empty dashboard the person fills.

editor.wizard.startFrom.context: Name of the group of start choices on the first step of the new-dashboard dialog, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

editor.wizard.startRoomDescription.en: Everything in a room you pick, grouped by what it does.
editor.wizard.startRoomDescription.context: Description on the card "One room" in the new-dashboard dialog. The person picks a room on the card; its devices are grouped by kind (lights, climate…).

editor.wizard.startRoomName.context: Name of a start choice (a card) in the new-dashboard dialog: a dashboard with everything in one room that the person picks on the card, grouped by what it does.

editor.wizard.stepPick.context: Name of the first of the two steps shown as a numbered row at the top of the new-dashboard dialog: choose where the dashboard starts from.

editor.wizard.stepTune.context: Name of the second of the two steps shown as a numbered row at the top of the new-dashboard dialog: name the dashboard and choose what stays on it.

editor.wizard.summaries.context: Name of a section that has no heading text of its own, in the preview and in the list of what is on the new dashboard. It is a heading with a row of summaries (small live figures such as "3 lights on").

editor.wizard.tileCount.context: Small count in the footer of the new-dashboard dialog, second step: how many tiles (boxes that show a device, flow or value) the new dashboard will have.

params.count: How many tiles the new dashboard will have, at least 0.

editor.wizard.titleFirst.context: Title of the new-dashboard dialog for a person who has no dashboard yet. Friendlier than the usual title. Also the title shown while the dialog loads.

editor.wizard.titleNew.context: Title of the dialog that makes a new dashboard, opened from the sidebar or the switcher. Also the title shown while the dialog loads.

editor.wizardHost.createFailed.context: Red text in the new-dashboard dialog, above its buttons, when making the dashboard failed.

editor.wizardHost.homeyFailed.context: Red message (toast) when the rooms and devices of the person’s Homey could not be read for the new-dashboard dialog. The dialog closes.

editor.wizardHost.loading.en: Looking at your rooms and devices…
editor.wizardHost.loading.context: Text under the title of the new-dashboard dialog while it is still loading: Tiledash reads the rooms and devices of the person’s Homey to build suggestions. A short wait.

editor.zonePicker.nested.context: Label of a switch under the chosen zone, shown when the zone has rooms inside it (a floor has rooms). On: the tile counts the devices of those rooms too. Under it, a line lists the rooms.

editor.zonePicker.none.context: First choice in the dropdown that picks a zone (a floor or a room of the home) in a tile’s settings: no zone is chosen. Only offered when the setting is optional.

editor.zonePicker.placeholder.context: Placeholder of the dropdown that picks a zone (a floor or a room of the home) in a tile’s settings, while nothing is chosen.
